questions.answer_summary: Expected: firm fundus at umbilicus, moderate lochia rubra, afterpains with breastfeeding. Report: pad saturated in 1 hour, unilateral calf symptoms, T 101.2°F.

rows.text: Pain, warmth, and swelling in one calf

questions.stem: A 2-hour-old newborn of a mother with gestational diabetes is jittery, has a weak suck, and has an axillary temperature of 97.2°F (36.2°C). Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the newborn is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Infants of diabetic mothers are at high risk for hypoglycemia, which can cause jitteriness, poor feeding, and hypothermia. Early feeding (breast milk or formula) and glucose rechecks are standard, and skin-to-skin contact helps maintain temperature. Water provides no glucose, and bathing worsens heat loss.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: hypoglycemia. Actions: obtain a heel-stick glucose; initiate feeding per protocol and notify the RN. Monitor: blood glucose; temperature.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Obtain a heel-stick blood glucose per protocol
Initiate feeding per protocol and notify the RN
Move the newborn to an open crib away from the mother

questions.stem: Which task can the LPN/VN delegate to an assistive personnel (AP) on a pediatric unit?
questions.rationale: Measuring vital signs on a stable child is within AP scope. Teaching, data collection, and dose calculation require licensed nursing knowledge.

options.text: Measuring vital signs on a stable 7-year-old
Reinforcing asthma inhaler teaching with a parent
Collecting data on an infant's respiratory status
Calculating a medication dose

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN count the respiratory rate of a sleeping 3-month-old?
questions.rationale: Infants breathe mainly with the diaphragm, and their breathing pattern is irregular. Counting abdominal movements for a full minute while the infant is quiet gives an accurate rate.

options.text: Count chest movements for 15 seconds and multiply by 4
Observe abdominal movements for a full 60 seconds
Count respirations only while the infant is crying
Place a hand firmly on the chest and count for 30 seconds

questions.stem: Which method should the LPN/VN use to obtain an accurate heart rate in an infant?
questions.rationale: The apical pulse, counted for a full minute, is the most accurate method in infants and young children because peripheral pulses are harder to feel and rhythms may be irregular.

options.text: Radial pulse for 15 seconds
Apical pulse for 1 full minute
Carotid pulse for 30 seconds
Pedal pulse for 1 minute

questions.stem: A parent calls about a 6-week-old with a rectal temperature of 100.6°F (38.1°C). What should the LPN/VN advise?
questions.rationale: A temperature of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher in an infant under 3 months requires prompt medical evaluation because of the risk of serious bacterial infection. Medication should not be given before evaluation unless directed.

options.text: "Give acetaminophen and check again tomorrow."
"The baby needs to be evaluated by a provider right away."
"Give a lukewarm bath and continue to monitor."
"This is normal after feeding."

questions.stem: Which actions should the LPN/VN include for a child after a tonsillectomy? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Frequent swallowing can indicate bleeding. Cool liquids soothe the throat, and avoiding red fluids prevents confusion with blood. Straws, coughing, and nose blowing can dislodge clots. Citrus irritates the throat.

options.text: Watch for frequent swallowing
Offer cool, clear liquids such as ice pops
Avoid red- or brown-colored fluids
Discourage the use of straws
Encourage vigorous coughing and nose blowing
Offer citrus juice

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce with parents to help prevent ear infections in their infant?
questions.rationale: Feeding while lying flat and secondhand smoke increase the risk of otitis media. Breastfeeding and up-to-date vaccines are also protective.

options.text: "Prop the bottle so the baby can feed independently."
"Hold the baby upright during feedings and avoid exposure to cigarette smoke."
"Give the bottle at bedtime while the baby is lying down."
"Clean the ear canals with cotton swabs daily."

questions.stem: The parent of a toddler with mild croup asks when to seek emergency care. Which response by the LPN/VN is correct?
questions.rationale: Stridor at rest, drooling, retractions, or cyanosis indicate significant airway obstruction. A barking cough that is worse at night is typical of mild croup.

options.text: "Only if the cough lasts more than a week."
"If your child has noisy, high-pitched breathing at rest, drools, or has trouble breathing."
"If your child has a runny nose."
"If your child coughs at night."

questions.stem: A 10-year-old with asthma has a peak flow reading of 65% of personal best. How should the LPN/VN interpret this?
questions.rationale: Green is 80–100% of personal best, yellow is 50–79% (caution), and red is below 50% (medical alert).

options.text: Green zone: continue usual care
Yellow zone: use the rescue inhaler and follow the asthma action plan
Red zone: seek emergency care immediately
The meter is broken

questions.stem: A child is suspected of having pinworms. When should the parent perform the tape test?
questions.rationale: Female worms lay eggs around the anus at night. Collecting the sample in the morning before hygiene gives the best result. Family members are often treated, and handwashing is emphasized.

options.text: After lunch
First thing in the morning before bathing or toileting
Right after a bath
At bedtime after brushing teeth

questions.stem: A parent calls because a toddler just swallowed an unknown amount of a household cleaner. The child is alert and breathing normally. What should the LPN/VN advise first?
questions.rationale: Poison Control provides immediate, substance-specific guidance. Inducing vomiting is not recommended because caustic substances can cause further injury. The parent calls 911 if the child has trouble breathing, has a seizure, or becomes unresponsive.

options.text: "Make your child vomit."
"Call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 right away and follow their instructions."
"Give your child a large glass of milk and wait."
"Wait to see if symptoms develop."

questions.stem: The parent of an 18-month-old asks when to turn the car seat forward-facing. What is the best response by the LPN/VN?
questions.rationale: The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends rear-facing seats for as long as possible, up to the seat's limits, because this position best protects the head, neck, and spine.

options.text: "At 12 months."
"Keep your child rear-facing as long as possible, until reaching the seat's maximum height or weight limit."
"As soon as your child can sit without help."
"When your child can walk."

questions.stem: Which foods should the LPN/VN advise parents to avoid giving or cut up for a 2-year-old because of choking risk? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Round, firm, or small hard foods can block a young child's airway. Grapes and hot dogs should be cut lengthwise into small pieces. Soft foods like mashed banana are safe.

options.text: Whole grapes
Hot dogs cut into rounds
Whole nuts
Popcorn
Hard candy
Mashed banana

questions.stem: Which sign indicates that a toddler may be ready to begin toilet training?
questions.rationale: Physical readiness (bladder control for about 2 hours) and the ability to communicate are key signs. Readiness typically appears between 18 and 36 months, not at a specific age.

options.text: Age of 12 months
Stays dry for about 2 hours and can communicate the need to go
Can count to 10
Sleeps through the night

questions.stem: A parent asks how to handle a toddler's temper tantrums. Which response by the LPN/VN is best?
questions.rationale: Tantrums are normal as toddlers seek independence. Ensuring safety and not reinforcing the behavior with attention or rewards reduces tantrums. Consistent routines also help.

options.text: "Give the child what they want so the tantrum stops."
"Make sure your child is safe, stay calm, and ignore the tantrum behavior."
"Spank the child to stop the tantrum."
"Lock the child in a room until they calm down."

questions.stem: Which intervention best meets the developmental needs of a hospitalized 15-year-old?
questions.rationale: Adolescents focus on identity, independence, and peer relationships. Privacy, involvement in decisions, and peer contact support coping.

options.text: Assigning a room with a toddler
Providing privacy and allowing contact with friends when appropriate
Having parents make all decisions without the teen's input
Limiting phone use completely

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN prepare a 4-year-old for a blood draw?
questions.rationale: Preschoolers think concretely and have a limited sense of time. Brief, simple explanations close to the procedure, with play demonstrations, reduce fear. Honesty about discomfort builds trust.

options.text: Explain the procedure a week in advance in detail
Use simple words, show the steps on a doll, and explain shortly before the procedure
Tell the child it won't hurt at all
Say nothing to avoid upsetting the child

questions.stem: Which pain scale is most appropriate for a 5-year-old who can communicate?
questions.rationale: The FACES scale works well for children about 3 years and older. The numeric scale is better for older children who understand numbers. FLACC is for infants and nonverbal children.

options.text: 0–10 numeric scale
Wong-Baker FACES scale
FLACC scale
Glasgow Coma Scale

questions.stem: Which site should the LPN/VN use for an intramuscular vaccine in a 4-month-old?
questions.rationale: The vastus lateralis (anterolateral thigh) is the preferred IM site for infants because it is well developed and away from major nerves and vessels.

options.text: Deltoid
Vastus lateralis
Dorsogluteal
Ventrogluteal in all cases

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN give an oral liquid medication to an infant?
questions.rationale: Giving small amounts into the cheek with the infant semi-upright reduces choking and spitting. If mixed into a full bottle, the infant may not receive the whole dose.

options.text: Mix it into a full bottle of formula
Use an oral syringe and give small amounts slowly into the side of the cheek
Pour it quickly into the back of the throat
Give it while the infant is lying flat

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce for a parent of an infant with diaper dermatitis?
questions.rationale: Reducing moisture and irritation and using a barrier promote healing. Fragrances irritate skin. A red rash with satellite lesions may indicate candida and should be reported.

options.text: "Use scented baby wipes to keep the area clean."
"Change diapers frequently, allow air exposure, and apply a zinc oxide barrier cream."
"Change the diaper only when it's heavily soiled."
"Apply cornstarch powder heavily at every change."

questions.stem: A parent of a child with sickle cell disease calls to report a temperature of 101.8°F (38.8°C). What should the LPN/VN advise?
questions.rationale: Children with sickle cell disease have functional asplenia and are at high risk for overwhelming bacterial sepsis. Fever of about 101°F (38.3°C) or higher requires urgent evaluation and antibiotics.

options.text: "Give acetaminophen and watch for 2 days."
"Bring your child to be evaluated right away."
"Give a cool bath and recheck in the morning."
"Fever is common in sickle cell disease and isn't concerning."

questions.stem: A child is prescribed methylphenidate for ADHD. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Morning dosing reduces insomnia. Stimulants can decrease appetite and affect growth, so height, weight, sleep, and BP are monitored. Extended-release forms are not crushed.

options.text: "Give the dose at bedtime."
"Give it in the morning, and we'll monitor growth, appetite, and sleep."
"Stop the medication on school days."
"Crush extended-release tablets into food."

questions.stem: The mother of a child just diagnosed with leukemia is crying in the hallway. What is the best response by the LPN/VN?
questions.rationale: Offering presence and acknowledging the parent's feelings is therapeutic. The other responses dismiss emotions, give false reassurance, or deflect.

options.text: "Please try to stay strong for your child."
"This is a lot to take in. I can stay with you for a few minutes if you'd like."
"Leukemia is very treatable now, so don't worry."
"You should ask the doctor about your concerns."

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is collecting data on a 2-year-old at a well-child visit. For each finding, indicate whether it is expected or should be reported to the RN.
questions.rationale: Toddler heart rates of about 90–150/min, tantrums, and shin bruises from active play are normal. Bruising in protected areas at different healing stages suggests possible abuse. Not walking by 18 months is a developmental delay, and tachypnea with retractions indicates respiratory distress.
questions.answer_summary: Expected: HR 110, tantrums, shin bruises. Report: patterned bruising in various stages, not walking at 2 years, RR 50 with retractions.

rows.text: Bruises on the back and upper arms in different stages of healing

questions.stem: An 18-month-old with an ear infection and a temperature of 103.1°F (39.5°C) suddenly has generalized jerking of the arms and legs while sitting on the parent's lap. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the child is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Febrile seizures are common between 6 months and 5 years during a rapid rise in temperature. Care focuses on safety, airway, and timing. A seizure lasting 5 minutes or more requires emergency treatment. Nothing is placed in the mouth, and cold baths and restraint are unsafe.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: simple febrile seizure. Actions: side-lying on a safe surface and protect from injury; time the seizure and call the RN. Monitor: airway and breathing; seizure duration and LOC afterward.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Place the child on their side on a safe surface and protect from injury
Time the seizure and call for the RN
Place a finger or object in the child's mouth
Put the child in a cold bath
Hold the child's arms and legs still

bowtie_groups.label: Parameters to monitor (choose 2)
options: Seizure duration and level of consciousness afterward

questions.stem: Which task can the LPN/VN delegate to a trained assistive personnel (AP) on a psychiatric unit?
questions.rationale: Trained APs may provide continuous observation. Assessing risk, teaching, and deciding on precaution levels require licensed nursing and provider judgment.

options.text: Maintaining one-to-one observation of a client on suicide precautions
Determining a client's level of suicide risk
Reinforcing medication teaching
Deciding when a client can come off precautions

questions.stem: A client says, "I'm worthless. I can't do anything right." Which response by the LPN/VN is most therapeutic?
questions.rationale: Reflecting the client's statement encourages further expression. Disagreeing, generalizing, and scolding shut down communication.

options.text: "That's not true. You're a great person."
"You're feeling that you can't do anything right?"
"Everybody feels that way sometimes."
"You shouldn't say things like that."

questions.stem: A client with paranoid delusions refuses meals, saying the food is poisoned. Which action by the LPN/VN is best?
questions.rationale: Sealed packages address the client's fear without reinforcing or arguing with the delusion. Hiding medication violates trust and the client's rights.

options.text: Tell the client the food is safe and insist they eat
Offer foods in sealed, unopened packages
Hide medication in the food
Argue with the client about the delusion

questions.stem: A client is having a panic attack, breathing rapidly and saying, "I think I'm dying." What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: During panic, the client's ability to process information is severely limited. A calm presence and simple directions help. Exploring causes can wait until anxiety decreases.

options.text: Leave the client alone to calm down
Stay with the client, speak calmly, and give simple, brief directions
Ask the client to explain what triggered the attack
Encourage the client to join a group activity

questions.stem: A client with a pattern of heavy daily drinking and two DUIs says, "I only drink socially. I don't have a problem." Which defense mechanism is the client using?
questions.rationale: Denial is refusing to acknowledge a painful reality. Projection attributes one's own feelings to others, sublimation channels impulses into acceptable activities, and displacement redirects feelings to a safer target.

options.text: Projection
Denial
Sublimation
Displacement

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is reinforcing teaching for a client starting fluoxetine. Which client statement indicates a need for further teaching?
questions.rationale: SSRIs usually take 2–6 weeks for full effect and should not be stopped abruptly. Suicidal thoughts can increase early in treatment, especially in young people, and must be reported.

options.text: "It may take several weeks before I feel better."
"I'll stop taking it if I don't feel better in a week."
"I'll tell my provider if I have thoughts of hurting myself."
"I won't take St. John's wort with this."

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce for a client taking lorazepam for anxiety?
questions.rationale: Benzodiazepines combined with alcohol or opioids can cause fatal respiratory depression. They cause sedation, and abrupt discontinuation can cause withdrawal and seizures.

options.text: "Drinking a little alcohol with it is fine."
"Avoid alcohol and driving until you know how it affects you, and don't stop it suddenly."
"Double the dose if you feel anxious."
"It is safe to take with opioid pain medicine."

questions.stem: A client taking an antipsychotic reports a dry mouth. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Anticholinergic dry mouth is relieved by sugarless products and frequent sips of water. Sugary drinks increase dental caries, and alcohol mouthwash dries the mouth further.

options.text: "Stop taking the medication."
"Try sugarless gum or hard candy and sip water frequently."
"Drink sugary soda."
"Use alcohol-based mouthwash."

questions.stem: A client is taking olanzapine long term. Which data should the LPN/VN expect to be monitored regularly?
questions.rationale: Second-generation antipsychotics can cause weight gain, diabetes, and dyslipidemia (metabolic syndrome). Regular monitoring and lifestyle support are recommended.

options.text: Weight, blood glucose, and lipids
Hearing and vision only
Serum lithium levels
Pupil size

questions.stem: Which finding helps the LPN/VN distinguish delirium from dementia?
questions.rationale: Delirium has an acute onset, fluctuates, affects attention and consciousness, and is often reversible when the cause (infection, medications, dehydration) is treated. Dementia is gradual and progressive.

options.text: Gradual memory loss over several years
Sudden onset of confusion over hours to days with fluctuating attention
Stable level of consciousness
Irreversible decline

questions.stem: Which finding in an older adult may indicate depression and should be reported?
questions.rationale: Anhedonia, appetite changes, and sleep disturbance lasting 2 weeks or more suggest depression, which is often underrecognized in older adults and may be mistaken for dementia.

options.text: Enjoying weekly visits with family
Loss of interest in usual activities, poor appetite, and sleep changes over several weeks
Mild forgetfulness about names
Waking once at night to void

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is reinforcing teaching for a client taking disulfiram. Which statement indicates understanding?
questions.rationale: Disulfiram causes a severe reaction (flushing, vomiting, tachycardia, hypotension) with any alcohol, including hidden sources. It deters drinking rather than reducing cravings.

options.text: "I can use mouthwash that contains alcohol."
"I'll check labels and avoid alcohol in cough syrups, mouthwash, and some sauces."
"I can drink one beer a day."
"The medication will reduce my cravings."

questions.stem: Which intervention should the LPN/VN include when caring for a client with anorexia nervosa?
questions.rationale: Supervision prevents hiding food, excessive exercise, and purging. Weights are taken consistently (same time, same clothing, often back to the scale). Discussions focus on feelings rather than food.

options.text: Allow the client to eat alone in their room
Observe the client during meals and for a period after meals as prescribed
Weigh the client in street clothes at varying times
Discuss food and calories at length

questions.stem: Which approach is most helpful when caring for a hospitalized child with autism spectrum disorder?
questions.rationale: Children with ASD often rely on routine and may be sensitive to noise, light, and touch. Consistency and preparation reduce distress.

options.text: Assign different staff each shift for variety
Keep a consistent routine, limit sensory stimulation, and prepare the child for changes
Place the child in a busy playroom
Frequently rearrange the child's room

questions.stem: A client with terminal cancer says, "If I can just live until my daughter's wedding, I'll be ready." Which stage of grief does this statement reflect?
questions.rationale: Bargaining involves trying to postpone loss in exchange for something. Stages of grief are not always linear.

options.text: Denial
Anger
Bargaining
Acceptance

questions.stem: A client arrives at a clinic distraught after a house fire destroyed their home. What is the LPN/VN's priority?
questions.rationale: Crisis intervention addresses immediate safety and needs, mobilizes support and resources, and restores functioning. Long-term exploration is not the focus.

options.text: Explore childhood experiences
Focus on the immediate problem, safety, and resources such as shelter
Schedule long-term therapy
Discuss insurance paperwork in detail

questions.stem: The LPN/VN notices bruises on a client's upper arms. The client's partner stays in the room and answers all questions. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Screening for intimate partner violence must be done privately to protect the client. Controlling behavior by a partner is a warning sign. The nurse provides safety resources and reports to the RN.

options.text: Ask the client about abuse in front of the partner
Find a way to speak with the client privately to screen for safety
Ignore the bruises
Confront the partner

questions.stem: Which action is correct when the LPN/VN is caring for a client in wrist restraints?
questions.rationale: Frequent checks and regular release prevent injury. Restraints are tied to the bed frame with quick-release knots.

options.text: Check circulation and skin at the prescribed intervals, and release each restraint at least every 2 hours for range of motion and toileting
Check the client once per shift
Secure the restraints to the side rails
Use a tight knot that cannot be released quickly

questions.stem: A client is pacing, clenching fists, and raising their voice at staff. What should the LPN/VN do first?
questions.rationale: Verbal de-escalation is the first intervention for escalating agitation. The nurse stays calm, keeps personal space, stands near an exit, and offers choices. Restraint is a last resort.

options.text: Call security to restrain the client
Use a calm voice, maintain a safe distance, and offer choices to reduce tension
Turn your back to show you are not a threat
Argue with the client about their behavior

questions.stem: A client reports trouble falling asleep. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Consistent sleep times, limiting caffeine and screen light, and a relaxing bedtime routine improve sleep.

options.text: "Drink coffee after dinner to relax."
"Keep a regular sleep schedule and avoid screens and caffeine before bed."
"Take long naps during the day."
"Exercise vigorously right before bed."

questions.stem: A newly admitted client with OCD washes their hands repeatedly and is late for breakfast. What is the best initial approach by the LPN/VN?
questions.rationale: Abruptly stopping rituals increases anxiety. Initially, time is allowed for rituals, and limits are introduced gradually alongside therapy such as exposure and response prevention.

options.text: Prevent the client from washing hands
Allow time for the ritual while gradually setting limits as treatment progresses
Punish the client for being late
Ridicule the behavior to show it is unnecessary

questions.stem: Which findings are negative symptoms of schizophrenia? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Negative symptoms reflect a loss of normal functions. Hallucinations and delusions are positive symptoms, which add abnormal experiences.

options.text: Flat affect
Poverty of speech (alogia)
Lack of motivation (avolition)
Inability to experience pleasure (anhedonia)
Auditory hallucinations
Delusions of persecution

questions.stem: Which findings suggest opioid withdrawal?
questions.rationale: Opioid withdrawal causes flu-like symptoms and autonomic hyperactivity. It is very uncomfortable but rarely life-threatening in healthy adults. Pinpoint pupils and slow breathing indicate opioid intoxication.

options.text: Pinpoint pupils and slow respirations
Yawning, runny nose, dilated pupils, gooseflesh, and diarrhea
Hypothermia and bradycardia
Sedation and constipation

questions.stem: A client takes lithium. For each finding, indicate whether it is an expected side effect or a possible sign of toxicity that should be reported.
questions.rationale: Fine tremor, polyuria, and transient GI upset are common. Coarse tremor, neurological changes, and persistent GI symptoms suggest toxicity. Vomiting and diarrhea can also raise levels through dehydration.
questions.answer_summary: Expected: fine tremor, thirst/polyuria, mild initial nausea. Report: coarse tremor, confusion/slurred speech, persistent vomiting and diarrhea.

questions.stem: A resident being treated for depression has seemed unusually calm today, gave away a favorite photograph, and told the LPN/VN, "Thank you for everything. I won't be needing help anymore." Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the resident is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Sudden calm, giving away possessions, and farewell statements are warning signs of suicide. The resident must not be left alone, and the RN must be notified at once for a full risk assessment. Nurses never promise secrecy about safety concerns.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: high risk for suicide. Actions: stay with the resident under constant observation; report to the RN immediately. Monitor: behaviors and statements; environment for hazards.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Stay with the resident and keep them under constant observation
Report the findings to the RN immediately
Leave the resident alone to rest
Promise to keep the conversation secret
Tell the resident to cheer up

bowtie_groups.label: Parameters to monitor (choose 2)
options: Behaviors and statements about death or suicide
The environment for items that could be used for self-harm

questions.stem: Which action by the LPN/VN correctly verifies the right client before giving medications?
questions.rationale: Two identifiers, stated by the client when possible and matched to the ID band and MAR, prevent wrong-client errors.

options.text: Checking the name on the door
Asking the client to state their full name and date of birth and comparing with the ID band and MAR
Asking "Are you Mrs. Smith?"
Relying on recognizing the client from yesterday

questions.stem: Carvedilol 12.5 mg PO is prescribed. The available tablets are 25 mg and scored. How many tablets should the LPN/VN give?
questions.rationale: 12.5 mg ÷ 25 mg = 0.5 tablet. Only scored tablets are split.

options.text: 0.25 tablet
0.5 tablet
1 tablet
2 tablets

questions.stem: Furosemide 20 mg is prescribed. The oral solution is labeled 40 mg/4 mL. How many milliliters should the LPN/VN give?
questions.rationale: Concentration is 10 mg/mL. 20 mg ÷ 10 mg/mL = 2 mL.

options.text: 1 mL
2 mL
4 mL
8 mL

questions.stem: A client weighs 154 lb. A medication is prescribed at 2 mg/kg. What dose should the LPN/VN prepare?

options.text: 70 mg
140 mg
154 mg
308 mg

questions.stem: A client is prescribed 10 mL of cough syrup. The client asks how much this is using a household measure. Which response by the LPN/VN is correct?
questions.rationale: 5 mL equals about 1 teaspoon, so 10 mL is about 2 teaspoons. Kitchen spoons vary in size, so a calibrated device is recommended.

options.text: "About 1 teaspoon."
"About 2 teaspoons, but please use the marked dosing cup or oral syringe."
"About 1 tablespoon."
"About 1 ounce."

questions.stem: A client's pre-lunch glucose is 245 mg/dL. The sliding scale for insulin lispro is: 150–200 mg/dL = 2 units; 201–250 mg/dL = 4 units; 251–300 mg/dL = 6 units; above 300 mg/dL = call the provider. How much insulin should the LPN/VN give?
questions.rationale: 245 mg/dL falls within the 201–250 range, which calls for 4 units. The meal tray should be available because lispro acts quickly.

options.text: 2 units
4 units
6 units
Call the provider

questions.stem: An antibiotic of 1 g in 100 mL is prescribed to infuse over 30 minutes by pump. At what rate should the pump be set?

options.text: 50 mL/hr
100 mL/hr
200 mL/hr
300 mL/hr

questions.stem: At what angle should the LPN/VN give a subcutaneous injection to a client with average body tissue?
questions.rationale: Subcutaneous injections are given at 45–90 degrees depending on the amount of subcutaneous tissue and needle length. Intradermal is 10–15 degrees, and IM is 90 degrees.

options.text: 10–15 degrees
45–90 degrees, depending on tissue and needle length
Always 15 degrees
180 degrees

questions.stem: Why does the LPN/VN use the Z-track method for certain IM injections?
questions.rationale: Displacing the skin before injection and releasing it afterward seals the medication in the muscle. The method is often used for irritating drugs such as iron dextran.

options.text: To speed absorption
To prevent medication from leaking into subcutaneous tissue and staining or irritating the skin
To reduce the amount of medication needed
To allow a larger volume in the deltoid

questions.stem: How does the LPN/VN locate the ventrogluteal injection site?
questions.rationale: The ventrogluteal site is the preferred IM site for adults because it is away from major nerves and vessels. The dorsogluteal site risks sciatic nerve injury.

options.text: Place the palm on the greater trochanter, the index finger on the anterior superior iliac spine, and spread the middle finger toward the iliac crest; inject in the center of the V
Divide the buttock into quadrants and inject in the lower inner quadrant
Measure 3 fingerbreadths below the acromion
Inject in the middle third of the outer thigh

questions.stem: Which technique is correct when the LPN/VN instills eye drops?
questions.rationale: The conjunctival sac holds the medication. Pressure on the inner canthus limits systemic absorption. The dropper tip should not touch the eye, and the nurse waits about 5 minutes between different drops.

options.text: Place the drop directly on the cornea
Place the drop into the lower conjunctival sac, then apply gentle pressure to the inner corner of the eye
Touch the dropper tip to the eyelid to steady it
Have the client squeeze the eye shut tightly afterward

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN position the ear to give ear drops to an adult?
questions.rationale: In adults, pulling up and back straightens the ear canal. In children younger than about 3, the pinna is pulled down and back.

options.text: Pull the pinna down and back
Pull the pinna up and back
Push the tragus inward
Do not move the ear

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is reinforcing teaching for a client using a fentanyl transdermal patch. Which client statement indicates a need for further teaching?
questions.rationale: Heat increases absorption from fentanyl patches and can cause overdose and respiratory depression. Used patches still contain drug and must be disposed of safely, away from children and pets.

options.text: "I'll remove the old patch before applying a new one."
"I'll put a heating pad over the patch when my back hurts."
"I'll rotate application sites."
"I'll fold the used patch sticky sides together and dispose of it as instructed."

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN instruct a client to take a sublingual tablet?
questions.rationale: Sublingual medications are absorbed directly into the bloodstream through the mucosa under the tongue. Swallowing reduces effectiveness.

options.text: "Swallow it with water."
"Place it under your tongue and let it dissolve completely without chewing or swallowing it."
"Chew it thoroughly."
"Place it between your cheek and gum and swallow after 1 minute."

questions.stem: Which technique is correct when the LPN/VN inserts a rectal suppository in an adult?
questions.rationale: Left Sims' position follows colon anatomy. The suppository must pass the internal sphincter and be placed against the rectal wall, not into stool, to be absorbed.

options.text: Position the client in the right lateral position and insert 1 inch
Position the client in left Sims' position and insert the lubricated suppository beyond the internal anal sphincter, about 3–4 inches
Insert the suppository into a mass of stool
Have the client stand while inserting

questions.stem: A client refuses a scheduled blood pressure medication. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Clients have the right to refuse medication. Understanding the reason, such as side effects, may allow the problem to be solved. Hiding medication is unethical and illegal.

options.text: Hide the medication in food
Explore the reason for refusal, provide information, respect the decision, document, and notify the RN or provider
Tell the client they must take it
Document that the medication was given

questions.stem: The LPN/VN realizes a client received a double dose of a scheduled oral medication. What should the nurse do first?
questions.rationale: The client's safety is the first priority. The nurse then notifies the RN and provider, follows orders, and completes the facility's error report.

options.text: Complete an incident report
Check the client's condition and vital signs
Wait to see if the client develops symptoms
Tell the client not to worry

questions.stem: The LPN/VN gives oral oxycodone for pain rated 7/10. When should the nurse reassess the client's pain?
questions.rationale: Oral opioids generally reach peak effect in 30–60 minutes. Reassessment evaluates effectiveness and sedation. IV medications are reassessed sooner, in about 15–30 minutes.

options.text: At the next shift
About 30–60 minutes after administration
Only if the client calls
After 4 hours

questions.stem: During the shift-change narcotic count, the LPN/VN and the oncoming nurse find that one oxycodone tablet is missing. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Any controlled substance discrepancy must be reported and resolved according to policy before the count is signed.

options.text: Sign the count and look for it later
Report the discrepancy to the charge nurse or supervisor immediately and follow facility policy before signing
Replace the tablet from another client's supply
Ignore it, since one tablet is not significant

questions.stem: An older adult takes nine medications from three different providers. Which action by the LPN/VN best promotes safe medication use?
questions.rationale: A "brown bag" review supports medication reconciliation and helps identify duplications, interactions, and unnecessary medications.

options.text: Tell the client to stop the least important medications
Encourage the client to bring all medications, including over-the-counter and herbal products, to each visit for review
Suggest using several pharmacies
Advise taking all medications at the same time

questions.stem: A client with dysphagia has several oral medications due. Which medication should the LPN/VN not crush?
questions.rationale: Extended-release tablets release drug over time. Crushing can release the entire dose at once. The nurse contacts the pharmacy or provider for an alternative.

options.text: Acetaminophen 325 mg tablet
Metoprolol succinate 50 mg extended-release (XL) tablet
Furosemide 20 mg tablet
Lisinopril 10 mg tablet

questions.stem: A client taking simvastatin asks whether they can drink grapefruit juice every morning. What should the LPN/VN advise?
questions.rationale: Grapefruit inhibits the CYP3A4 enzyme, increasing levels of simvastatin and some other drugs, which raises the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.

options.text: "Yes, it improves the medicine's effect safely."
"Avoid grapefruit juice, because it can raise the medication level and increase the risk of muscle damage."
"Only drink it at night."
"It doesn't matter."

questions.stem: A client taking oral contraceptives is prescribed rifampin. Which information should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Rifampin induces liver enzymes that increase metabolism of hormonal contraceptives, reducing their effectiveness.

options.text: "No changes are needed."
"Use a backup form of birth control, because rifampin can make oral contraceptives less effective."
"Stop the birth control pills."
"Take the pills twice a day."

questions.stem: For each action, indicate whether it is correct or incorrect medication administration technique.
questions.rationale: Rubbing enoxaparin sites increases bruising, reusing patch sites irritates the skin, and crushing enteric-coated tablets destroys the protective coating.
questions.answer_summary: Correct: pinna up and back (adult), 5 minutes between eye drops, sublingual under the tongue. Incorrect: rubbing an enoxaparin site, reusing the same patch site, crushing enteric-coated tablets.

rows.text: Pulling an adult's pinna up and back for ear drops
Rubbing the site after an enoxaparin injection
Applying a new nitroglycerin patch to the same site every day
Waiting about 5 minutes between two different eye drops
Placing a sublingual tablet under the tongue to dissolve

questions.stem: An older adult received oxycodone 10 mg 1 hour ago after surgery. The LPN/VN finds the client difficult to arouse, with RR 8/min, pinpoint pupils, and SpO2 86% on room air. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the client is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Deep sedation, slow respirations, pinpoint pupils, and hypoxemia after an opioid indicate opioid toxicity. Naloxone is given per protocol or prescription, and opioids are held. Sedation usually precedes respiratory depression, so sedation scales help detect risk early.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: opioid-induced respiratory depression. Actions: stimulate the client and call for the RN/rapid response; raise the head of the bed and apply oxygen. Monitor: RR and SpO2; sedation level.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Stimulate the client and call for the RN/rapid response immediately
Raise the head of the bed and apply oxygen per protocol
Give the next scheduled opioid dose

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: Which task is outside the LPN/VN's scope of practice in most states?
questions.rationale: Initial assessment and developing the plan of care are RN responsibilities. LPNs/VNs contribute data and implement the plan. Scope varies by state.

options.text: Administering oral medications to a stable client
Reinforcing discharge teaching
Performing the initial admission assessment and developing the nursing care plan
Collecting data on a client's wound

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: Which task can the LPN/VN appropriately delegate to an assistive personnel (AP)?
questions.rationale: Routine tasks for stable clients can be delegated. Decisions about medications, teaching, and evaluation require licensed nursing judgment.

options.text: Ambulating a stable client who has walked independently before
Checking a client's blood pressure before giving a cardiac medication and deciding whether to give it
Reinforcing teaching about a new medication
Evaluating a client's response to pain medication

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: An AP reports that a resident's BP is 82/48 mm Hg. What should the LPN/VN do first?
questions.rationale: The nurse verifies abnormal findings, collects additional data (symptoms, orthostatic changes), and reports promptly. An antihypertensive would worsen hypotension.

options.text: Document the value
Recheck the BP and collect additional data, then report to the RN
Tell the AP to check it again in 4 hours
Give the resident's scheduled antihypertensive

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: The LPN/VN in a long-term care facility has four residents to see. Which resident should the nurse see first?
questions.rationale: A fall with hip pain and inability to bear weight suggests a fracture, which is an acute physical problem needing prompt data collection and reporting.

options.text: A resident who fell and reports new hip pain and cannot bear weight
A resident requesting help with a phone call
A resident due for a scheduled daily vitamin
A resident who wants a snack

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: Which strategy helps the LPN/VN manage time effectively during a busy shift?
questions.rationale: Clustering care reduces interruptions for clients and saves time. Documentation is done in real time or as close as possible for accuracy.

options.text: Completing tasks in the order clients call
Clustering care, such as giving medications while collecting data and assisting with repositioning
Saving all documentation until the end of the shift
Skipping breaks

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: The LPN/VN receives a prescription that seems unsafe for the client's condition. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Nurses are accountable for their actions and must question orders that seem unsafe. They do not change orders independently.

options.text: Give the medication because the provider ordered it
Hold the medication and clarify the order with the RN or provider, using the chain of command if needed
Change the dose to a safer amount
Ask the client whether they want it

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: A caller says they are a resident's nephew and asks about the resident's condition. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: HIPAA requires that information be shared only with authorized individuals. Facilities use verification methods such as privacy codes.

options.text: Share the information since the caller is family
Verify that the caller is authorized, such as with a privacy code or the resident's consent, before sharing information
Give only the diagnosis
Hang up without explanation

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: Which social media post by a nurse is a privacy violation?
questions.rationale: Posting any image or details of a client's condition without consent is a violation, even without a name or face, because the client may still be identifiable.

options.text: "Proud to be a nurse!" with no client information
A photo of a client's unusual wound, with the face cropped out, captioned "Crazy case today"
A post sharing a public health article
A post about a nursing conference

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: Which documentation entry by the LPN/VN is best?
questions.rationale: Documentation should be objective, specific, and factual, including direct quotes. Opinions and labels are avoided.

options.text: "Client seems depressed."
"Client ate 25% of lunch. States, 'I'm not hungry.' Lying in bed with the curtains closed."
"Client had a bad day."
"Client is being difficult."

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: The LPN/VN forgot to document a dressing change done 3 hours ago. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Late entries are clearly labeled to preserve the accuracy of the record. Backdating entries is falsification.

options.text: Document it with the original time as if it were on time
Add a late entry labeled as such, with the current date and time, and reference when the care was given
Skip documenting it
Ask a coworker to document it

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: A resident with advanced dementia can no longer make decisions and has a durable power of attorney for health care. Who makes health care decisions for the resident?
questions.rationale: A durable power of attorney for health care names an agent to make decisions when the person cannot. The agent is guided by the resident's known wishes.

options.text: The nursing staff
The person named as health care agent
Any family member who visits
The facility administrator

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: The LPN/VN is asked to witness a consent signature. The client received IV morphine 15 minutes ago and is drowsy. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Valid consent requires a client who is competent and not impaired by sedating medications. Consent is postponed unless it is an emergency.

options.text: Witness the signature since the client can hold a pen
Notify the RN or provider that the client may not be able to give informed consent right now
Have the client's spouse sign
Sign for the client

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: A competent resident refuses a morning bath. What is the LPN/VN's best response?
questions.rationale: Residents have the right to refuse care. Offering choices respects autonomy while meeting hygiene needs. The refusal is documented.

options.text: "You must take a bath now."
"That's okay. Would you prefer a bath later, or a different kind of hygiene care?"
Give the bath anyway
Report the resident for being uncooperative

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: The LPN/VN notices bruises on the wrists of a resident whose adult son recently became the caregiver. The resident seems fearful when he visits. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Nurses are mandated reporters of suspected elder abuse. Findings are documented objectively and reported per policy and state law.

options.text: Confront the son
Report the findings to the RN and follow the facility's mandatory reporting process
Wait to see if more bruises appear
Ask the resident to keep a diary

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: The charge nurse asks the LPN/VN to perform a procedure the nurse has never been trained to do. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Nurses must practice within their competence and scope. Requesting training or supervision protects clients.

options.text: Attempt the procedure using an online video
Explain that they have not been trained and ask for help or supervision
Refuse and leave the unit
Ask the AP to do it

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: Which information is most important for the LPN/VN to include in shift report about a resident?
questions.rationale: Effective handoff, often using SBAR, focuses on current status, changes, pending care, and risks to ensure continuity and safety.

options.text: The resident's favorite TV show
Changes in condition, pending tasks, and safety concerns such as fall risk
The nurse's personal opinion of the family
Every routine task completed

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: A confused resident keeps trying to get out of bed. What should the LPN/VN try first?
questions.rationale: Least-restrictive alternatives are tried first. Restraints and four raised side rails can increase injury and are considered restraints requiring a provider order.

options.text: Apply a vest restraint
Use alternatives such as scheduled toileting, a low bed, a bed alarm, and frequent checks
Raise all four side rails
Give a sedative without an order

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: The LPN/VN finds a resident on the floor. What should the nurse do first?
questions.rationale: Checking for injuries such as head trauma or fractures before moving prevents further harm. The nurse then gets help, notifies the RN, documents, and completes the report.

options.text: Help the resident back into bed right away
Check the resident for injury before moving them
Complete an incident report
Call the family

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: A Muslim client asks whether the meals contain pork. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Respecting religious and cultural dietary practices is part of client-centered care. Dietary services can provide appropriate meals, such as halal options.

options.text: Tell the client to eat what is served
Verify the meal contents with dietary services and arrange meals that meet the client's religious dietary needs
Tell the client to have family bring all meals
Remove the meat without asking

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: A client who speaks limited English needs medication teaching. Which approach by the LPN/VN is best?
questions.rationale: Qualified medical interpreters ensure accurate communication and confidentiality. Family members, especially children, should not interpret medical information.

options.text: Have the client's 12-year-old child interpret
Use a qualified medical interpreter, in person or by phone or video
Speak more loudly and slowly in English
Give the client written instructions in English

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: A resident is admitted to a long-term care facility from the hospital. Which action helps prevent medication errors?
questions.rationale: Medication reconciliation at care transitions identifies omissions, duplications, and discrepancies. The nurse reports discrepancies for provider clarification.

options.text: Continue the resident's home medication list without review
Participate in medication reconciliation by comparing the hospital discharge list with prior home medications and reporting differences
Start only new medications
Ask the resident which medications to continue

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: The LPN/VN sees a coworker leave a room on contact precautions without performing hand hygiene. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Peer accountability supports a culture of safety. Hand hygiene is the most important measure to prevent healthcare-associated infections.

options.text: Say nothing to avoid conflict
Remind the coworker in a respectful way and follow facility policy for reporting if the behavior continues
Post about it anonymously online
Tell the client

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: A 6-year-old in the clinic has burns in a stocking pattern on both feet, and the parent says the child "stepped in hot bathwater." What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Symmetric immersion (stocking or glove) burns suggest intentional injury. Nurses are mandated reporters and must report reasonable suspicion of abuse. Proof is not required.

options.text: Accept the explanation
Report the findings to the RN or provider and follow child abuse reporting laws
Ask the parent to explain it again
Wait until the next visit

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: For each task, indicate whether the LPN/VN can appropriately delegate it to an AP.
questions.rationale: APs perform routine personal care and standardized tasks for stable clients. Teaching, data collection, and medication administration require licensed nursing knowledge (except for certified medication aides where permitted).
questions.answer_summary: Can delegate: vital signs, bathing, feeding (stable residents). Cannot: teaching, wound data collection, medication administration.

rows.text: Taking vital signs on a stable resident
Feeding a resident without swallowing difficulties
Reinforcing teaching about a new inhaler
Collecting data on a new pressure injury

questions.set_title: Set 16: Management of Care, Delegation, Legal and Ethical Issues
questions.stem: A resident who takes warfarin is found on the floor next to the bed. The resident is alert, has a small cut on the forehead, and says, "I hit my head." Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the resident is at greatest risk for, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Anticoagulated clients who hit their head are at high risk for intracranial hemorrhage, even if they seem well at first. Prompt evaluation (often CT imaging) and frequent neuro checks are needed. Aspirin increases bleeding risk.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: intracranial bleeding. Actions: check for injury and keep still; notify the RN and provider immediately. Monitor: neurological status; vital signs.

bowtie_groups.label: Condition (choose 1)
options: Intracranial bleeding after a head injury

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Check for injury and keep the resident still until evaluated
Notify the RN and provider immediately
Quickly lift the resident back into bed without checking

bowtie_groups.label: Parameters to monitor (choose 2)
options: Neurological status (level of consciousness and pupils)

questions.stem: Which actions should the LPN/VN take to reduce fall risk for a hospitalized older adult? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: A low, locked bed, items within reach, nonskid footwear, and scheduled toileting reduce falls. Night-lights improve visibility, and high shelves encourage unsafe reaching.

options.text: Keep the bed in the lowest position with the wheels locked
Keep the call light and personal items within reach
Provide nonskid footwear
Offer scheduled toileting
Keep the room dark at night
Place frequently used items on a high shelf

questions.stem: Why should the LPN/VN avoid raising all four side rails for a confused resident who tries to get out of bed?
questions.rationale: Full side rails restrict movement and legally function as a restraint requiring an order. Residents who climb over them fall from a greater height.

options.text: It is always required by policy
Four raised rails are considered a restraint and can increase injury if the resident climbs over them
It makes the bed harder to clean
It prevents staff from reaching the resident

questions.stem: During a fire, the charge nurse directs evacuation of residents from the affected wing. In what order should residents generally be moved?
questions.rationale: Moving ambulatory residents first (who can often be guided out quickly) allows the most people to reach safety in the least time. Residents in immediate danger are rescued first. Horizontal evacuation to another smoke compartment is used before vertical evacuation.

options.text: Bedridden residents first, then wheelchair users, then ambulatory residents
Ambulatory residents first, then those in wheelchairs, then bedridden residents
Residents farthest from the fire first
Alphabetical order

questions.stem: The LPN/VN finds a resident receiving an electrical shock from a faulty lamp. What should the nurse do first?
questions.rationale: Touching a person still in contact with an electrical source can shock the rescuer. The power source is removed first, then the nurse assesses the resident and begins CPR if needed.

options.text: Pull the resident away with bare hands
Turn off the power or unplug the device before touching the resident
Pour water on the lamp
Start CPR while the resident is still in contact with the lamp

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce to prevent accidental poisoning in an older adult's home?
questions.rationale: Original labeled containers prevent mix-ups. Good lighting, pill organizers, and never sharing medications reduce errors.

options.text: "Store your medications in unlabeled containers to save space."
"Keep medications in their original labeled containers and use a pill organizer if helpful."
"Take medications in the dark so you don't wake your spouse."
"Share medications with your spouse if you run out."

questions.stem: Which action is correct when the LPN/VN uses a gait belt to ambulate a client?
questions.rationale: A snug waist belt allows the nurse to steady the client and guide a controlled descent if they start to fall. Gait belts are not for lifting dependent clients.

options.text: Place the belt loosely around the chest
Secure the belt snugly around the waist over clothing and walk slightly behind the client on the weaker side
Hold the client by the arm instead
Use the belt to lift a client who cannot bear weight

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is transferring a client with left-sided weakness from the bed to a wheelchair. Which action is correct?
questions.rationale: Positioning the chair on the strong side lets the client pivot using stronger muscles. Locked brakes and raised footrests prevent the chair from moving and the client from tripping.

options.text: Place the wheelchair on the client's left side with the brakes unlocked
Place the wheelchair on the client's right (strong) side, lock the brakes, and raise the footrests
Have the client pull on the wheelchair to stand
Place the wheelchair facing away from the bed

questions.stem: Which action is correct when using a full-body mechanical lift?
questions.rationale: Mechanical lifts require at least two trained staff, correct sling size, equipment checks, and adherence to weight limits for safety.

options.text: Operate the lift alone to save time
Use at least two staff, check the sling for damage, and confirm the lift's weight limit
Lift the client high above the bed
Leave the client suspended while getting supplies

questions.stem: While putting on sterile gloves, the LPN/VN does which of the following that breaks sterile technique?
questions.rationale: The bare hand may touch only the inside of the cuff. Touching the outer surface contaminates the glove. Gloved hands touch only sterile surfaces.

options.text: Picks up the first glove by its folded inside cuff with the bare hand
Slides the gloved fingers under the cuff of the second glove
Touches the outside of the second glove with the bare hand
Keeps gloved hands above waist level

questions.stem: Which procedure requires surgical (sterile) asepsis?
questions.rationale: Entering a sterile body cavity such as the bladder requires sterile technique. The other procedures use medical (clean) asepsis.

options.text: Administering oral medications
Inserting an indwelling urinary catheter
Giving a cleansing enema
Feeding a client

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN handle soiled linens?
questions.rationale: Shaking linens disperses microorganisms, and contact with the uniform spreads contamination. Linens are rolled and bagged at the bedside.

options.text: Shake them to remove debris
Hold them away from the uniform and place them directly in the linen bag without shaking
Place them on the floor until finished
Carry them against the body to the hamper

questions.stem: Where should the LPN/VN dispose of a dressing heavily saturated with blood?
questions.rationale: Items saturated with blood or other potentially infectious materials are regulated medical waste and go in labeled biohazard containers.

options.text: Regular trash
A red biohazard bag or container per facility policy
A sharps container
The recycling bin

questions.stem: A small amount of blood spills on the floor. Which action by the LPN/VN is correct?
questions.rationale: Blood spills are handled with PPE and disinfected with an appropriate agent to eliminate bloodborne pathogens.

options.text: Wipe it with a dry paper towel and leave
Wear gloves, absorb the spill, and clean the area with an EPA-registered disinfectant or bleach solution per policy
Cover it with a towel and wait for housekeeping without warning others
Mop it with water only

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is irrigating a large wound. Which PPE is needed in addition to gloves?
questions.rationale: Standard precautions require PPE based on the anticipated exposure. Irrigation can splash fluid onto the clothing, eyes, and mouth.

options.text: No additional PPE
A gown and eye protection or a face shield
Sterile booties
An N95 respirator only

questions.stem: A client on droplet precautions must be transported to radiology. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Masking the client contains respiratory droplets. Notifying the receiving department allows them to prepare appropriate precautions.

options.text: Have the client wear a surgical mask during transport and notify the receiving department
Cancel the test
Have transport staff wear N95 respirators and leave the client unmasked
No precautions are needed outside the room

questions.stem: Which food choice should the LPN/VN advise a client receiving chemotherapy to avoid?
questions.rationale: Unpasteurized products can carry organisms such as Listeria that cause severe infection in immunocompromised people. Raw eggs and undercooked meats are also avoided.

options.text: Well-cooked chicken
Unpasteurized milk and soft cheeses made from it
Pasteurized yogurt
Washed fresh fruit

questions.stem: Parents mention they keep a handgun at home. Which safety instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Safe storage (unloaded, locked, with ammunition stored separately) reduces unintentional injuries and suicides among children and teens.

options.text: "Keep it loaded in a nightstand for quick access."
"Store it unloaded and locked, with ammunition locked separately."
"Hide it under the mattress."
"Teach young children to use it safely."

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce with parents of a 2-year-old?
questions.rationale: Young children can drown quickly and silently in just a few inches of water. Constant adult supervision is essential. Bath seats are not safety devices.

options.text: "You can leave your child in the bath for a minute to answer the phone."
"Never leave your child alone in or near water, even for a moment."
"Bath seats make it safe to step away."
"An older sibling can supervise bathing."

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is about to give medications and notices the client is not wearing an identification band. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Proper identification is essential before any medication or procedure. The band is replaced per policy before proceeding.

options.text: Give the medications since the nurse knows the client
Hold the medications, have a correct ID band applied per policy, and then verify identity with two identifiers
Ask the roommate to confirm the client's name
Use the room number to identify the client

questions.stem: A client reports a penicillin allergy, but no allergy band is on the wrist and none is documented in the chart. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Documenting allergies and applying alert bands prevents exposure to known allergens.

options.text: Ignore it since it isn't documented
Report it to the RN, document the allergy and reaction, and ensure an allergy band is applied per policy
Give penicillin if prescribed
Tell the client to remind every nurse

questions.stem: A client is going for an MRI. Which action should the LPN/VN take?
questions.rationale: Metal objects can become projectiles, and some implants and medication patches with metallic backing can cause burns or malfunction in the MRI's magnetic field.

options.text: Leave the client's metal hair clips in place
Remove jewelry, hairpins, and other metal objects, and report any implants such as pacemakers or metal fragments
Give the client a metal oxygen tank for the trip
Apply a nicotine patch with a foil backing

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is caring for a client with a sealed radioactive implant. Which principle reduces the nurse's exposure?
questions.rationale: Time, distance, and shielding are the core principles of radiation safety. Pregnant staff should not be assigned to these clients.

options.text: Spending as much time as possible in the room
Limiting time, maximizing distance, and using shielding
Standing close to the implant site
Assigning the same pregnant nurse every day

questions.stem: A client asks how much water to store for a home emergency kit. Which recommendation by the LPN/VN is correct?
questions.rationale: Emergency preparedness guidance recommends about 1 gallon of water per person per day for at least 3 days, plus supplies such as food, medications, and a flashlight.

options.text: "About 1 cup per person per day."
"About 1 gallon per person per day, for at least 3 days."
"Only bottled soda is needed."
"Water isn't needed if you have food."

questions.stem: For each procedure, indicate whether it requires medical asepsis (clean technique) or surgical asepsis (sterile technique).
questions.rationale: The GI tract is not sterile, so NG tubes and enemas use clean technique. Procedures entering sterile areas or the bloodstream, such as the bladder, central lines, and the lower airway in hospitalized clients, require sterile technique.
questions.answer_summary: Medical asepsis: oral meds, NG tube, enema. Surgical asepsis: urinary catheter, central line dressing, hospital tracheal suctioning.

questions.stem: The LPN/VN smells smoke and finds a wastebasket on fire in a resident's room. The resident is in bed next to it. Complete the diagram by choosing the situation, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take first, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: RACE: Rescue, Alarm, Contain (close doors), Extinguish if small. Opening windows feeds the fire with oxygen, elevators are not used during fires, and doors are closed to contain smoke. Residents are checked for smoke inhalation, and all residents are accounted for.
questions.answer_summary: Situation: fire in a resident's room. Actions: rescue the resident; activate the alarm. Monitor: respiratory status of exposed residents; accountability for all residents.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take first (choose 2)
options: Remove the resident from the room (Rescue)
Open the windows to let out smoke
Use the elevator to evacuate residents
Leave the room door open when exiting

bowtie_groups.label: Parameters to monitor (choose 2)
options: Respiratory status of residents exposed to smoke
Accountability for all residents in the area

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is testing a client's distance vision with a Snellen chart. Which technique is correct?
questions.rationale: The standard Snellen test is performed at 20 feet, one eye at a time. A result of 20/40 means the client sees at 20 feet what a person with normal vision sees at 40 feet.

options.text: Have the client stand 5 feet from the chart
Have the client stand 20 feet from the chart and test each eye separately, with glasses if worn for distance
Test both eyes together only
Have the client read the chart from a handheld card

questions.stem: A worker splashes a cleaning chemical into one eye. What should the LPN/VN do first?
questions.rationale: Immediate, prolonged irrigation limits chemical damage to the eye. Flushing from the inner to outer canthus keeps the chemical away from the other eye. Emergency evaluation follows.

options.text: Cover the eye with a patch and transport to the hospital
Immediately flush the eye with large amounts of water or saline for at least 15 minutes, from the inner to the outer corner
Rub the eye to remove the chemical
Apply antibiotic ointment

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce about hearing aid care?
questions.rationale: Removing the battery or opening the battery door extends battery life. Moisture and heat damage hearing aids. The device is cleaned with a dry cloth or brush.

options.text: "Wear it in the shower."
"Open the battery door or remove the battery at night, and keep the device dry and clean."
"Clean it with alcohol daily."
"Store it in the bathroom."

questions.stem: Which approach should the LPN/VN use when communicating with a client who has hearing loss?
questions.rationale: Facing the client allows lipreading and seeing facial expressions. High-pitched sounds are often lost first in age-related hearing loss, and shouting distorts speech.

options.text: Shout directly into the client's ear
Face the client in a well-lit area, speak clearly in a normal to slightly lower pitch, and reduce background noise
Speak while walking away
Exaggerate lip movements dramatically

questions.stem: A client with age-related macular degeneration has lost central vision. Which intervention should the LPN/VN include?
questions.rationale: Macular degeneration affects central vision while peripheral vision is often retained. Bright, even lighting, magnification, and a consistent environment support safety and independence.

options.text: Keep the room dim
Provide good lighting, magnifiers, and large-print materials, and approach from the side where the client sees best
Rearrange the furniture often
Encourage the client to drive at night

questions.stem: A client with open-angle glaucoma uses timolol eye drops. Which finding should the LPN/VN report?
questions.rationale: Timolol is a beta blocker that can be absorbed systemically, causing bradycardia, hypotension, and bronchospasm. Pressing the inner canthus after instillation reduces absorption.

options.text: Improved comfort
Heart rate of 48/min and dizziness
Slight stinging when the drops are instilled
Clear vision

questions.stem: Before irrigating a client's ear to remove cerumen, which information is most important for the LPN/VN to obtain?
questions.rationale: Ear irrigation is contraindicated with a perforated tympanic membrane or tubes because fluid can enter the middle ear. Irrigation uses body-temperature water to prevent vertigo.

options.text: The client's favorite music
A history of a perforated eardrum or ear tubes
Whether the client wears glasses
The client's blood type

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce for a client with varicose veins?
questions.rationale: Elevation, movement, and compression promote venous return. Prolonged standing, crossing the legs, and constrictive bands worsen pooling.

options.text: "Stand for long periods to strengthen your legs."
"Elevate your legs when sitting, avoid prolonged standing, and wear compression stockings as prescribed."
"Cross your legs when sitting."
"Wear tight knee-high socks."

questions.stem: A client reports painful hemorrhoids. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Soft stools reduce straining, and sitz baths soothe tissue. Prolonged sitting and straining increase venous pressure in the rectum.

options.text: "Strain during bowel movements to empty completely."
"Increase fiber and fluids and use warm sitz baths for comfort."
"Sit on the toilet for long periods."
"Avoid all fluids."

questions.stem: A client with a known inguinal hernia reports severe groin pain, nausea, and vomiting. The bulge is tender and cannot be pushed back in. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: A painful, irreducible hernia with nausea and vomiting suggests incarceration or strangulation, which can cut off blood supply to the bowel and requires emergency surgery.

options.text: Encourage the client to push the hernia back in
Report the findings to the RN or provider immediately
Apply a heating pad and reassess in 4 hours
Give a laxative

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce for a client with carpal tunnel syndrome?
questions.rationale: Neutral wrist positioning reduces pressure on the median nerve. Repetitive flexion and sleeping with the wrists bent worsen symptoms.

options.text: "Keep your wrist flexed while typing."
"Wear a wrist splint in a neutral position, especially at night, and take breaks from repetitive motions."
"Sleep with your wrists bent under your pillow."
"Squeeze a stress ball for hours daily."

questions.stem: Which strategy should the LPN/VN reinforce for a client with fibromyalgia?
questions.rationale: Gradual low-impact exercise, sleep hygiene, stress management, and prescribed medications are the mainstays of fibromyalgia management.

options.text: Complete bed rest
Regular low-impact exercise such as walking or water aerobics, and good sleep habits
High-impact exercise daily
Avoiding all activity during flares permanently

questions.stem: A perimenopausal client reports hot flashes. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Layered clothing, a cool environment, and avoiding triggers help. Clients should discuss the risks and benefits of hormone therapy with their provider.

options.text: "Drink hot coffee when a hot flash starts."
"Dress in layers, keep the room cool, and limit caffeine, alcohol, and spicy foods."
"Take extra blankets to bed."
"Avoid all exercise."

questions.stem: A parent asks when the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine is recommended. Which response by the LPN/VN is accurate?
questions.rationale: The vaccine is recommended for all preteens, regardless of sex, before exposure. It is most effective when given early. Catch-up vaccination is recommended through age 26.

options.text: "Only after a child becomes sexually active."
"It is routinely recommended at age 11 to 12 and can be started as early as age 9."
"Only for girls."
"At age 30."

questions.stem: A client with genital herpes asks about managing the infection. Which statement by the client indicates understanding?
questions.rationale: Herpes is lifelong. Antivirals reduce outbreak frequency and transmission but do not cure it. The virus can shed and spread without visible lesions.

options.text: "The antiviral medication will cure the virus."
"I'll avoid sexual contact during outbreaks, use condoms, and take antivirals as prescribed to reduce outbreaks and transmission."
"I can't spread herpes if I don't have sores."
"I only need treatment once."

questions.stem: A 58-year-old client asks whether he should have a PSA test. Which response by the LPN/VN reflects current guidance?
questions.rationale: The USPSTF recommends shared decision-making about PSA screening for men aged 55–69 because of the risks of false positives, overdiagnosis, and overtreatment.

options.text: "Everyone must have one every month."
"For men aged 55 to 69, PSA screening is an individual decision to make with your provider after discussing benefits and risks."
"PSA tests are never recommended."
"Only men over 80 need it."

questions.stem: An infant is recovering from cleft lip repair. Which action should the LPN/VN take to protect the suture line?
questions.rationale: Elbow immobilizers prevent the infant from touching the incision, and back or side positioning keeps the face off the mattress. Sucking and rubbing strain the repair. Restraints are released regularly for skin checks and range of motion.

options.text: Place the infant prone to sleep
Use elbow restraints (arm immobilizers) as prescribed and position the infant on the back or side
Allow the infant to suck on a pacifier
Clean the suture line with a dry cotton ball roughly

questions.stem: An infant is placed in a Pavlik harness for developmental dysplasia of the hip. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: The harness keeps the hips flexed and abducted for joint development. Only the provider adjusts the straps. Lotions and powders can irritate the skin.

options.text: "Remove the harness at night."
"Keep the harness on as prescribed, check the skin under the straps daily, and do not adjust the straps yourself."
"Apply lotion and powder under the straps."
"Tighten the straps if the baby kicks."

questions.stem: A newborn has an unrepaired myelomeningocele. Which action should the LPN/VN take?
questions.rationale: Prone positioning and a moist sterile dressing protect the sac from injury, drying, and infection. Children with spina bifida are at high risk for latex allergy, so latex precautions start at birth.

options.text: Place the newborn supine
Position the newborn prone, cover the sac with a sterile, moist, nonadherent dressing, and use latex-free equipment
Leave the sac open to air
Use latex gloves for care

questions.stem: A 3-year-old with a ventriculoperitoneal shunt has vomiting, irritability, headache, and sleepiness. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: These are signs of increased intracranial pressure from shunt malfunction or infection, which requires urgent evaluation.

options.text: Give an antiemetic and let the child sleep
Report the findings to the RN or provider immediately
Encourage the child to drink more fluids
Document the findings for the next visit

questions.stem: A child has chickenpox. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce with the parent?
questions.rationale: Varicella is contagious until all lesions crust. Aspirin is avoided because of the risk of Reye's syndrome. Short nails reduce scratching and secondary infection.

options.text: "Give aspirin for fever."
"Keep your child home until all lesions have crusted, trim fingernails, and use acetaminophen for fever."
"Your child can return to school tomorrow."
"Scratching helps the lesions heal."

questions.stem: A child is diagnosed with strep throat. Which instruction best prevents rheumatic fever?
questions.rationale: Completing antibiotic therapy for group A strep infection prevents rheumatic fever, which can cause permanent heart valve damage.

options.text: "Stop the antibiotic when the sore throat improves."
"Give the full course of antibiotics exactly as prescribed."
"Use throat lozenges instead of antibiotics."
"Save leftover antibiotics for the next infection."
