questions.stem: A pregnant client had a nonstress test. The report says it was "reactive." What does this mean?
questions.rationale: A reactive nonstress test (in a pregnancy of 32 weeks or more, accelerations of at least 15 beats/min lasting 15 seconds, twice in 20 minutes) indicates adequate fetal oxygenation. A nonreactive result requires further testing.

options.text: The fetus is in distress
The fetal heart rate showed at least two accelerations within 20 minutes, which is reassuring
The test must be repeated immediately
The client is in labor

questions.stem: For each finding reported by a client at 28 weeks' gestation, indicate whether it is an expected pregnancy change or should be reported to the RN.
questions.rationale: Braxton Hicks contractions, pigmentation changes, and heartburn are normal. Infection can trigger preterm labor, leaking fluid may indicate ruptured membranes, and persistent vomiting with weight loss suggests hyperemesis gravidarum.
questions.answer_summary: Expected: Braxton Hicks contractions, linea nigra, heartburn. Report: UTI symptoms with fever, leaking fluid, persistent vomiting with weight loss.

rows.text: Irregular, painless tightening that eases with rest
Dark line down the middle of the abdomen
Continuous leaking of clear fluid from the vagina
Vomiting several times daily with weight loss

questions.stem: During a heat wave, an 85-year-old resident in a room without air conditioning is found confused, with hot, flushed, dry skin and a temperature of 105°F (40.6°C). HR is 124/min. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the resident is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Heat stroke (temperature above about 104°F with CNS dysfunction) is life-threatening. Rapid cooling and emergency care are essential. Antipyretics are ineffective because this is not a fever, and oral fluids are unsafe with altered consciousness.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: heat stroke. Actions: activate emergency response and notify the RN; begin active cooling. Monitor: core temperature; level of consciousness.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Activate emergency response and notify the RN immediately
Begin cooling: move the resident to a cool area, remove excess clothing, and apply cool compresses to the neck, axillae, and groin
Give large amounts of oral fluid to the confused resident
Give acetaminophen to lower the temperature
Cover the resident with a warm blanket

questions.stem: A 14-year-old at a school clinic reports sudden, severe pain in one testicle with nausea and vomiting. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Testicular torsion is a surgical emergency. The testicle may be lost if blood flow is not restored within about 6 hours.

options.text: Apply ice and have him rest for a few hours
Arrange immediate emergency evaluation, since this may be testicular torsion
Give ibuprofen and send him back to class
Tell him it's probably a pulled muscle

questions.stem: The LPN/VN has been meeting with a client for several weeks, and discharge is approaching. Which action is appropriate for the termination phase?
questions.rationale: Termination involves summarizing goals achieved, discussing feelings about separation, and planning for the future. Nurses maintain professional boundaries and do not continue personal contact.

options.text: Give the client a personal phone number to stay in touch
Review the client's progress and discuss feelings about ending the relationship
Start exploring new problems in depth
End the relationship without warning

questions.stem: A client prescribed buspirone for generalized anxiety asks how it works. Which statement by the LPN/VN is accurate?
questions.rationale: Buspirone is not a PRN drug. It takes about 2–4 weeks to be fully effective and has low potential for dependence.

options.text: "Take it only when you feel a panic attack starting."
"It takes a few weeks to reach full effect, so take it every day as prescribed."
"It works within minutes, like lorazepam."
"It is highly addictive."

questions.stem: A client with somatic symptom disorder frequently reports new physical symptoms, and medical workups have been negative. Which approach should the LPN/VN use?
questions.rationale: The client's distress is real. New symptoms still need evaluation, but the nurse limits attention to symptoms and encourages expression of feelings and healthy coping.

options.text: Tell the client the symptoms are imaginary
Acknowledge the client's distress, report new symptoms for evaluation, and focus conversations on feelings and coping
Ignore all new complaints
Encourage more diagnostic tests

questions.stem: The parent of a 6-year-old with Down syndrome wants to enroll the child in gymnastics. Which information should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Atlantoaxial instability can lead to spinal cord injury with neck flexion. Evaluation and guidance help determine safe activities. Children with Down syndrome also have higher rates of heart defects and hypotonia.

options.text: "Children with Down syndrome can't participate in sports."
"Talk with the child's provider first, because some children have neck instability (atlantoaxial instability)."
"There are no special considerations."
"Only swimming is allowed."

questions.stem: Which feeding technique should the LPN/VN use for a child with spastic cerebral palsy?
questions.rationale: Upright positioning with a slight chin tuck reduces aspiration risk. Children with CP often have oral-motor difficulties and need more time, small bites, and high-calorie foods.

options.text: Feed the child lying flat
Position the child upright with the head slightly flexed, and allow extra time to eat
Feed quickly to prevent fatigue
Use large bites to reduce feeding time

questions.stem: An infant has serial casts for clubfoot. Which finding should the LPN/VN report?
questions.rationale: Cool, pale, or swollen toes suggest impaired circulation from a tight cast. Casts are changed frequently as the infant grows.

options.text: Pink toes with brisk capillary refill
Toes that are cool, pale, and swollen
The infant is feeding well
The cast is dry and intact

questions.stem: A 5-year-old boy uses his hands to "walk up" his legs to stand from the floor. How should the LPN/VN document this finding?
questions.rationale: Gowers sign indicates proximal muscle weakness and is characteristic of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, an X-linked disorder seen mainly in boys.

options.text: Normal development
Gowers sign, which should be reported
Babinski sign
Moro reflex

questions.stem: A 7-month-old is choking on a piece of food, cannot cry or cough, but is still responsive. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Abdominal thrusts are not used in infants because of the risk of liver injury. Back blows and chest thrusts are the correct technique. If the infant becomes unresponsive, the nurse begins CPR.

options.text: Perform abdominal thrusts
Give up to 5 back blows followed by up to 5 chest thrusts, repeating until the object comes out or the infant becomes unresponsive
Perform a blind finger sweep
Hold the infant upside down by the feet

questions.stem: A parent asks whether it is safe to keep children's chewable vitamins with iron on the kitchen counter. Which response by the LPN/VN is best?
questions.rationale: Children may think chewable vitamins are candy. Iron overdose can cause severe GI bleeding, shock, and liver failure.

options.text: "Yes, vitamins are harmless."
"Keep them locked up and out of reach. Iron overdose is a leading cause of poisoning deaths in young children."
"Only adult vitamins are dangerous."
"Keep them in the refrigerator door."

questions.stem: A parent is worried about small red blotches with pale yellow centers on a 2-day-old newborn's chest and back. What should the LPN/VN tell the parent?
questions.rationale: Erythema toxicum is a benign newborn rash that appears in the first few days and resolves without treatment.

options.text: "This is erythema toxicum, a common harmless rash that goes away on its own."
"This is a serious infection."
"This is an allergic reaction to formula."
"This means the baby is too hot."

questions.stem: A parent asks why the newborn needs a hearing test before discharge. Which response by the LPN/VN is best?
questions.rationale: Universal newborn hearing screening identifies hearing loss early. Intervention by about 6 months improves speech and language outcomes.

options.text: "It's only done if there's a family history."
"Early detection of hearing loss allows early treatment, which supports language development."
"It tests for ear infections."
"It isn't necessary until the child starts school."

questions.stem: A newborn is diagnosed with phenylketonuria (PKU). Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce with the parents?
questions.rationale: PKU prevents normal breakdown of phenylalanine, which can cause intellectual disability. Dietary restriction, including avoiding the sweetener aspartame, prevents damage.

options.text: "Feed a regular diet as the child grows."
"Your child will need a special formula and a lifelong low-phenylalanine diet, and should avoid aspartame."
"PKU goes away by age 2."
"Give extra protein."

questions.stem: A newborn boy has hypospadias. The parents ask about circumcision. What should the LPN/VN explain?
questions.rationale: In hypospadias, the urethral opening is on the underside of the penis. Surgical repair, usually in infancy, may use foreskin tissue.

options.text: "Circumcision should be done before discharge."
"Circumcision is usually delayed because the foreskin may be needed for surgical repair."
"Hypospadias requires no treatment."
"Circumcision will fix the condition."

questions.stem: Shortly after a laboring client receives an epidural, which finding should the LPN/VN report to the RN immediately?
questions.rationale: Epidural anesthesia causes vasodilation, which can lead to hypotension and reduced placental blood flow. Treatment includes lateral positioning, IV fluids, and vasopressors as prescribed.

options.text: Decreased sensation in the legs
BP 84/50 mm Hg with dizziness
Pain relief
Mild itching

questions.stem: A breastfeeding client asks how to store pumped breast milk. Which instruction is correct?
questions.rationale: CDC guidance supports these time limits. Microwaving creates hot spots that can burn the infant and damages milk components. Thawed milk should not be refrozen.

options.text: "Warm frozen milk in the microwave."
"Fresh milk can stay at room temperature up to about 4 hours and in the refrigerator up to about 4 days. Thaw it in the refrigerator or warm water, not the microwave."
"Refreeze milk after it's thawed."
"Leave milk out overnight."

questions.stem: A client with hereditary hemochromatosis asks about diet. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Hemochromatosis causes iron overload. Vitamin C increases iron absorption, and alcohol worsens liver damage. Clients with iron overload are vulnerable to Vibrio infection from raw shellfish. Treatment is regular phlebotomy.

options.text: "Take iron supplements daily."
"Avoid iron and vitamin C supplements, limit alcohol, and avoid raw shellfish."
"Eat raw oysters for extra zinc."
"Cook in cast-iron pans as often as possible."

questions.stem: Which action by the LPN/VN is correct when caring for a client with a nephrostomy tube?
questions.rationale: Gravity drainage prevents backflow into the kidney. Nephrostomy tubes are not clamped or irrigated without a specific prescription. Decreased output may indicate obstruction or dislodgement.

options.text: Clamp the tube when the client walks
Keep the drainage bag below the level of the kidney and report decreased drainage or new flank pain
Irrigate the tube routinely with large volumes
Place the drainage bag on the client's abdomen

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce after shock wave lithotripsy for a kidney stone?
questions.rationale: Fluids help flush stone fragments, and straining collects them for analysis. Mild hematuria and flank bruising are expected. Fever, severe pain, or inability to urinate should be reported.

options.text: "Limit fluids to reduce urine output."
"Drink plenty of fluids, strain your urine, and expect light pink urine and some bruising on your back."
"Report pink urine immediately."
"Stop straining urine after the first day."

questions.stem: A client receiving radiation to the head and neck has severe dry mouth. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Radiation can damage salivary glands, causing xerostomia and dental decay. Moisture, saliva substitutes, fluoride, and regular dental care help. Alcohol and sugar worsen dryness and decay.

options.text: "Use alcohol-based mouthwash."
"Sip water frequently, use saliva substitutes or sugar-free gum, and keep up with dental care."
"Eat dry, crunchy foods."
"Drink sugary sodas."

questions.stem: A client with Sjögren's syndrome reports dry, gritty eyes. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Sjögren's is an autoimmune disorder that damages tear and salivary glands. Artificial tears and humidified air relieve dryness and protect the cornea.

options.text: "Use a fan blowing on your face."
"Use preservative-free artificial tears and a humidifier."
"Rub your eyes to stimulate tears."
"Wear contact lenses all day."

questions.stem: An off-duty LPN/VN stops to help at the scene of a car crash. Which action is protected under most Good Samaritan laws?
questions.rationale: Good Samaritan laws protect rescuers who act in good faith within their training and without compensation. Once care begins, the rescuer stays until care is transferred to someone with equal or greater training.

options.text: Performing procedures outside nursing training
Providing emergency care within the nurse's training, in good faith, without expecting payment
Charging the victim for care
Leaving the victim once care has started without handing off to another rescuer

questions.stem: Under the Patient Self-Determination Act, what must a facility do when a client is admitted?
questions.rationale: The act requires facilities receiving Medicare or Medicaid funds to inform clients of their rights to accept or refuse treatment and to create advance directives. Clients are not required to have one.

options.text: Require every client to sign a DNR order
Ask whether the client has an advance directive and provide information about the right to make one
Choose a health care proxy for the client
Keep advance directives out of the medical record

questions.stem: For each newborn finding, indicate whether it is expected or should be reported to the RN.
questions.rationale: Acrocyanosis, molding, and pseudomenstruation (from maternal hormones) are normal. Central cyanosis suggests cardiac or respiratory disease, absent femoral pulses suggest coarctation of the aorta, and no urine by 24 hours may indicate a renal or urinary tract problem.
questions.answer_summary: Expected: acrocyanosis, molding, pseudomenstruation. Report: central cyanosis, absent femoral pulses, no voiding by 24 hours.

rows.text: Bluish hands and feet in the first 24 hours
Molding of the head after vaginal birth
Small amount of blood-tinged vaginal discharge in a female newborn
Bluish color of the lips and tongue
No urine output by 24 hours of age

questions.stem: An 8-year-old with asthma comes to the school health office after recess. The child is wheezing, has intercostal retractions, and can speak only a few words at a time. The child's asthma action plan and albuterol inhaler with spacer are on file. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the child is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Wheezing, retractions, and speaking in short phrases indicate a moderate to severe exacerbation. A short-acting bronchodilator is the rescue medication. Inhaled corticosteroids are controller medications, not rescue drugs. Parents are notified, and emergency help is called if the child does not respond quickly.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: acute asthma exacerbation. Actions: give albuterol with spacer per plan; keep upright and call 911 if not improving. Monitor: RR and work of breathing; ability to speak and SpO2.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Give albuterol with the spacer per the asthma action plan
Keep the child sitting upright and call 911 if there is no rapid improvement or symptoms worsen
Have the child lie flat to rest
Give the inhaled corticosteroid as the rescue medication
Send the child back to class to see if it passes

bowtie_groups.label: Parameters to monitor (choose 2)
options: Respiratory rate and work of breathing
Ability to speak in full sentences and SpO2 if available

questions.stem: Which oxygen delivery device provides the most precise oxygen concentration?
questions.rationale: Venturi masks use color-coded adapters to deliver a set FiO2. This is useful for clients such as those with COPD who need controlled oxygen.

options.text: Nasal cannula
Venturi mask
Simple face mask
Face tent

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is checking a client's nonrebreather mask. Which observation indicates correct use?
questions.rationale: A nonrebreather needs a high flow rate (usually 10–15 L/min) to keep the reservoir bag inflated and deliver high oxygen concentrations. A collapsing bag means the flow is too low.

options.text: The reservoir bag collapses completely with each breath
The reservoir bag stays at least partially inflated during inspiration
The flow rate is set at 2 L/min
The mask is loosely fitted

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN check orthostatic vital signs?
questions.rationale: A drop in systolic BP of 20 mm Hg or more (or diastolic of 10 or more), or a significant pulse rise, indicates orthostatic hypotension. The nurse stays close to prevent falls.

options.text: Measure BP only while standing
Measure BP and pulse after the client lies down for several minutes, then again 1–3 minutes after sitting or standing
Measure BP in both arms at the same time
Measure pulse only

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is measuring an apical-radial pulse on a client with atrial fibrillation. Which technique is correct?
questions.rationale: Simultaneous counting shows the pulse deficit, which is the difference between apical and radial rates. A deficit means some beats are not perfusing the periphery.

options.text: Count the apical pulse, then count the radial pulse 5 minutes later
Have two nurses count the apical and radial pulses at the same time for 1 full minute
Count the radial pulse for 15 seconds and multiply by 4
Count only the radial pulse

questions.stem: Which nonpharmacological pain management strategy should the LPN/VN offer a client with chronic back pain?
questions.rationale: Relaxation techniques, distraction, heat or cold, and gentle activity complement medications and can reduce pain perception.

options.text: Complete bed rest for weeks
Guided imagery, relaxation breathing, and heat or cold as appropriate
Avoiding all movement
Taking extra doses of opioids

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is performing passive range-of-motion exercises for an unconscious client. Which action is correct?
questions.rationale: Gentle, supported movement to the point of resistance maintains joint mobility without causing injury. ROM is usually done at least twice daily.

options.text: Force each joint past the point of resistance
Move each joint smoothly to the point of resistance, supporting the limb above and below the joint
Perform exercises only once a week
Move joints rapidly

questions.stem: Which action by the LPN/VN is correct when caring for a client with sequential compression devices?
questions.rationale: Sequential compression devices promote venous return to prevent DVT. They are generally contraindicated on a leg with an existing DVT because they could dislodge the clot.

options.text: Apply the sleeves to a leg with a known new DVT
Check the fit, keep the device on as prescribed, and briefly remove it to inspect the skin each shift
Keep the sleeves off while the client is in bed
Apply them over thick padding

questions.stem: A client's feeding pump alarms for an occluded tube. What should the LPN/VN try first?
questions.rationale: Kinks are ruled out first. Gentle warm water flushes clear most clogs. Acidic juices can curdle formula and worsen occlusion, and forceful flushing can rupture the tube.

options.text: Flush with cranberry juice
Check for kinks, then gently flush with warm water using a large syringe per policy
Replace the tube immediately
Increase the pump rate

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN position an unconscious client for oral care?
questions.rationale: Side-lying lets fluid drain from the mouth and reduces aspiration risk. Suction removes secretions. The nurse uses a soft toothbrush or swabs and does not place fingers in the client's mouth.

options.text: Supine with the head flat
On the side with the head turned, with suction available
Sitting upright with the head tilted back
Prone

questions.stem: Which action by the LPN/VN is correct when cleaning a client's dentures?
questions.rationale: Padding the sink prevents breakage if the dentures are dropped. Hot water can warp them. Dentures wrapped in napkins are often thrown away by mistake.

options.text: Clean them over a hard, empty sink
Clean them over a sink lined with a towel or partly filled with water, then store them in a labeled cup with water
Soak them in hot water
Wrap them in a paper towel on the meal tray

questions.stem: An unconscious client does not blink and the eyes remain partly open. Which intervention should the LPN/VN include?
questions.rationale: Without blinking, the cornea dries and can ulcerate. Lubrication and protecting the eyes prevent corneal damage.

options.text: Leave the eyes open to air
Apply prescribed lubricating drops or ointment and keep the lids gently closed per protocol
Rub the eyes with a dry cloth
Tape the eyes open

questions.stem: Which intervention best promotes sleep for a hospitalized older adult?
questions.rationale: Minimizing interruptions, dimming lights, reducing noise, and avoiding caffeine support sleep and may help prevent delirium.

options.text: Waking the client every hour for vital signs when not required
Clustering nighttime care to allow longer periods of uninterrupted sleep
Keeping the room brightly lit all night
Offering coffee at bedtime

questions.stem: An 88-year-old resident's room heater failed overnight. The resident is confused and slow to respond, with a temperature of 94.6°F (34.8°C). Which statement about this finding is accurate?
questions.rationale: Older adults have reduced thermoregulation and may not shiver. Gradual rewarming with blankets and warm fluids (if alert) is used, and the RN is notified.

options.text: "Shivering will always be present."
"Older adults may not shiver, and confusion may be an early sign of hypothermia."
"This temperature is normal for older adults."
"Rapid rewarming in a hot bath is best."

questions.stem: A client has died, and no autopsy or medical examiner review is required. Which action by the LPN/VN is appropriate?
questions.rationale: Postmortem care maintains dignity and appearance. When an autopsy or medical examiner case is involved, tubes and lines are left in place. Belongings are returned to the family.

options.text: Leave all tubes in place
Remove tubes per policy, clean the body, place a pillow under the head, and allow the family private time
Place the body prone
Discard the client's belongings

questions.stem: A client with a serious illness asks to see a spiritual leader from their faith community. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Spiritual needs are part of holistic care, especially during serious illness. Supporting rituals and visits promotes comfort and coping.

options.text: Tell the client that spiritual visits are not allowed
Help arrange the visit, involving the chaplain or contacting the client's faith leader
Suggest a different religion
Ignore the request

questions.stem: A client avoids eye contact during conversation. How should the LPN/VN interpret this?
questions.rationale: Norms for eye contact vary widely across cultures. Some view direct eye contact as disrespectful. Nurses avoid assumptions and practice culturally responsive communication.

options.text: As a sign of dishonesty
As behavior that may reflect cultural norms. The nurse observes and asks about preferences rather than assuming meaning.
As a sign of depression in every case
As rudeness

questions.stem: After explaining how to use a new inhaler, which action by the LPN/VN best confirms the client's understanding?
questions.rationale: Teach-back and return demonstration verify understanding and identify misunderstandings. A "yes" to "Do you understand?" is unreliable.

options.text: Asking "Do you understand?"
Asking the client to explain the steps in their own words and demonstrate using the inhaler
Giving the client a pamphlet
Having the family confirm understanding

questions.stem: The LPN/VN plans to reinforce discharge teaching, but the client is grimacing and rating pain 8/10. What should the nurse do first?
questions.rationale: Pain, anxiety, and fatigue interfere with learning. Meeting physical needs first improves readiness to learn.

options.text: Proceed with teaching to stay on schedule
Address the client's pain, then begin teaching when the client is more comfortable
Give the teaching materials to the family only
Skip the teaching

questions.stem: A parent asks how to give liquid acetaminophen to a toddler. Which instruction is most important for the LPN/VN to reinforce?
questions.rationale: Dosing errors are common with pediatric liquids. Using the correct concentration, weight-based dosing, and the provided measuring device prevents overdose. Kitchen spoons are inaccurate.

options.text: "Use any kitchen spoon to measure it."
"Check the concentration on the label, dose by your child's weight, and use the syringe or cup that comes with the product."
"Give adult tablets cut in half."
"Give it every 2 hours for fever."

questions.stem: A child has a sandpaper-like rash, a red "strawberry" tongue, and a sore throat. What should the LPN/VN reinforce with the parent?
questions.rationale: Scarlet fever is caused by group A strep. Completing antibiotics prevents complications such as rheumatic fever. Aspirin is avoided in children.

options.text: "This rash is caused by an allergy and needs no treatment."
"This is likely scarlet fever. Give the full course of antibiotics, and your child can usually return to school after 12–24 hours of treatment and no fever."
"Your child must stay home for 2 weeks."
"Give aspirin for the fever."

questions.stem: A child has bright red cheeks ("slapped cheek" rash) followed by a lacy rash on the arms. The parent's sister is pregnant and visited last week. What should the LPN/VN advise?
questions.rationale: Fifth disease (parvovirus B19) is contagious before the rash appears. Infection in pregnancy can cause fetal anemia and hydrops, so exposed pregnant people should be evaluated.

options.text: "There is no risk to anyone."
"Your sister should contact her prenatal provider, because parvovirus B19 can affect a developing baby."
"Keep your child home until the rash is gone for a month."
"Your child needs antibiotics."

questions.stem: The LPN/VN finds a skin tear with an intact flap on an older adult's forearm. Which action is correct?
questions.rationale: Preserving and approximating the flap promotes healing. Nonadherent dressings and avoiding tape protect fragile skin. The nurse may draw an arrow on the dressing to show the direction of removal.

options.text: Remove the skin flap
Gently clean the tear, reposition the flap over the wound, and apply a nonadherent dressing
Apply adhesive tape directly over the flap
Leave the wound open to air

questions.stem: A pregnant client asks which fish are safe to eat. Which response by the LPN/VN is correct?
questions.rationale: Low-mercury fish provide important omega-3 fatty acids. High-mercury fish can harm fetal brain development. Raw fish and unheated deli meats carry infection risks such as Listeria.

options.text: "Eat as much swordfish and king mackerel as you like."
"Choose low-mercury fish like salmon or shrimp, and avoid high-mercury fish such as shark, swordfish, and king mackerel."
"Avoid all fish during pregnancy."
"Raw sushi is the safest choice."

questions.stem: For each finding in a 78-year-old resident, indicate whether it is an expected age-related change or should be reported to the RN.
questions.rationale: Loss of elasticity, presbyopia, and mild nocturia are normal aging changes. Acute confusion suggests delirium, new incontinence may indicate infection or another illness, and rapid unintentional weight loss may signal malignancy, depression, or malnutrition.
questions.answer_summary: Expected: decreased elasticity, presbyopia, nocturia once. Report: acute confusion, new incontinence, rapid weight loss.

rows.text: Difficulty reading small print up close
Waking once at night to urinate
Sudden confusion that began this morning
Unintentional weight loss of 10 lb in 1 month

questions.stem: An 80-year-old resident who takes warfarin has a nosebleed that started 5 minutes ago. The resident is alert and anxious. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the resident is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Leaning forward prevents swallowing blood and aspiration, and direct pressure controls most anterior bleeds. Anticoagulant use increases bleeding risk, and an INR may be needed. Tilting the head back and blowing the nose worsen bleeding, and aspirin impairs clotting.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: anterior epistaxis with increased bleeding risk. Actions: sit up, lean forward, and pinch the soft part of the nose; notify the RN. Monitor: bleeding amount and duration; vital signs.

bowtie_groups.label: Condition (choose 1)
options: Anterior epistaxis with increased bleeding risk

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Have the resident sit up and lean forward while firmly pinching the soft part of the nose for 10–15 minutes
Notify the RN of the nosebleed and the resident's anticoagulant use
Have the resident lie flat with the head tilted back
Pack the nose with tissue and have the resident blow the nose

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is reinforcing teaching about colostomy irrigation. Which instruction is correct?
questions.rationale: Lukewarm water and a moderate height prevent cramping, and the cone tip reduces the risk of perforation. If cramping occurs, the flow is paused. Ileostomies are not irrigated because output is liquid.

options.text: "Use cold water and hang the bag high above your head."
"Use lukewarm water, insert the cone tip gently into the stoma, and hang the bag at about shoulder height."
"Force the water in quickly."
"Irrigate an ileostomy the same way."

questions.stem: A client is prescribed oxygen at 8 L/min by nasal cannula. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Flow above about 6 L/min by standard nasal cannula dries the mucosa without much increase in FiO2. A different device may be needed, and the nurse clarifies before changing therapy. High-flow nasal cannula is a separate device.

options.text: Set the flow at 8 L/min
Clarify the prescription, because nasal cannula flow is generally limited to about 6 L/min
Use a Venturi mask instead without asking
Set the flow at 2 L/min

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN help position a client for a thoracentesis?
questions.rationale: Leaning forward spreads the intercostal spaces and allows fluid to collect at the lung bases for easier removal.

options.text: Supine with the head flat
Sitting on the edge of the bed, leaning forward over a padded over-bed table
Prone
Trendelenburg

questions.stem: The LPN/VN measures the abdominal girth of a client with ascites daily. Which technique ensures accuracy?
questions.rationale: Consistent position, location, and timing allow valid comparisons. Marking the skin helps maintain the same measurement site.

options.text: Measure at a different spot each day
Measure with the client supine at the same marked location, at the same time each day
Measure over clothing
Measure only when the client is standing

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is reinforcing teaching with the family of a client who has type 1 diabetes about using a glucagon kit. Which instruction is correct?
questions.rationale: Glucagon is for severe hypoglycemia when the person cannot safely eat or drink. Vomiting is common, so side-lying prevents aspiration. Carbohydrates are given once the person is alert.

options.text: "Give it only if your family member is awake and can swallow."
"After giving glucagon, turn your family member onto their side, because vomiting may occur, and call for emergency help."
"Give it with a glass of juice."
"Give it for high blood sugar."

questions.stem: Which action by the client indicates correct use of an insulin pen?
questions.rationale: Priming removes air and confirms flow. Holding the needle in place ensures the full dose is delivered. Pen needles are single-use, and pens are never shared, even with a new needle, because of infection risk.

options.text: Skipping the priming step
Priming with 2 units, dialing the dose, injecting, and holding the needle in place for about 10 seconds
Reusing the same needle for a week
Sharing the pen with a family member who also has diabetes

questions.stem: A client starting metformin reports nausea and loose stools. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: GI upset is common and lessens when metformin is taken with food. Muscle pain, fatigue, and breathing difficulty may signal lactic acidosis, a rare but serious adverse effect.

options.text: "Stop taking it."
"Take it with meals. These side effects often improve over time. Report muscle pain, unusual tiredness, or trouble breathing right away."
"Take it on an empty stomach."
"Double the dose to get used to it faster."

questions.stem: A client with Graves' disease has bulging eyes and cannot fully close the eyelids. Which intervention should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Protecting the cornea from drying and irritation prevents ulceration. Head elevation reduces periorbital swelling.

options.text: "Keep your head flat when sleeping."
"Wear sunglasses outdoors, use lubricating eye drops, and elevate the head of the bed at night."
"Avoid blinking."
"Rub your eyes when they feel dry."

questions.stem: A client had a barium enema this morning. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Barium can harden and cause constipation or impaction. Fluids and laxatives help clear it. Light-colored stools are expected. No bowel movement in 2 days should be reported.

options.text: "Limit your fluids today."
"Drink extra fluids and take the prescribed laxative. Your stools may be white or light-colored for a day or two."
"Report white stools immediately."
"Stay NPO for 24 hours."

questions.stem: Which intervention should the LPN/VN include in a bowel training program for a resident with fecal incontinence?
questions.rationale: The gastrocolic reflex after meals stimulates peristalsis. Consistent timing, adequate fiber and fluids, and privacy help establish regularity.

options.text: Offer toileting at random times
Offer toileting at the same time each day, often 30 minutes after a meal
Restrict fluids and fiber
Use briefs only

questions.stem: Which action is correct when the LPN/VN applies an external condom catheter?
questions.rationale: Leaving space at the tip prevents irritation, and avoiding tight application prevents circulation problems. Circumferential tape can act as a tourniquet. Daily changes allow skin inspection.

options.text: Apply it tightly at the base to prevent leaks
Leave a small space between the tip of the penis and the end of the catheter, and change it daily with skin care
Use adhesive tape wrapped completely around the penis
Leave it on for a week

questions.stem: A client's arm cast was just removed. The skin is dry and flaky. What should the LPN/VN recommend?
questions.rationale: Skin under a cast is fragile. Gentle cleansing and moisturizing allow dead skin to shed naturally without breakdown.

options.text: "Scrub the skin vigorously to remove the flakes."
"Wash gently with mild soap and water, pat dry, and apply lotion."
"Apply alcohol to the skin."
"Keep the arm wrapped in plastic."

questions.stem: Which strategy should the LPN/VN reinforce to help a client prevent migraines?
questions.rationale: Identifying triggers such as certain foods, sleep changes, and stress helps prevention. Overusing pain relievers can cause medication-overuse (rebound) headaches.

options.text: "Skip meals to reduce triggers."
"Keep a headache diary to identify triggers, and maintain regular sleep and meal schedules."
"Drink more alcohol to relax."
"Take pain relievers every day, even without a headache."

questions.topic: Guiding a client with visual impairment
questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN guide a client who is blind while walking?
questions.rationale: The sighted guide technique lets the client feel changes in direction and pace. Verbal cues about steps, doors, and obstacles support safety.

options.text: Push the client from behind
Offer an elbow for the client to hold and walk about a half step ahead, describing obstacles
Pull the client by the hand
Walk beside the client without speaking

questions.stem: A client with burns had a split-thickness skin graft to the leg. Which action by the LPN/VN protects the graft?
questions.rationale: Movement and shearing can dislodge a new graft before it attaches. Immobilization and elevation promote adherence. Dressing changes follow the surgeon's orders.

options.text: Encourage walking on the grafted leg on the first day
Immobilize and elevate the grafted area as prescribed and avoid pressure on the graft
Remove the dressing to check the graft every hour
Apply heat to promote circulation

questions.stem: A client with folate deficiency anemia asks which foods to eat. Which foods should the LPN/VN suggest?
questions.rationale: These foods are rich in folate. Alcohol use can impair folate absorption and should be limited.

options.text: White rice and potatoes
Dark leafy greens, legumes, citrus fruits, and fortified grains
Butter and cream
Candy and soda

questions.stem: A client is scheduled for allergy skin testing next week. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Antihistamines suppress skin reactions and can cause false-negative results. Lotions can interfere with test placement and reading.

options.text: "Take an antihistamine the morning of the test."
"Stop antihistamines for the period your provider specifies before the test, usually several days."
"Apply lotion to your back before the test."
"Eat the foods you're allergic to beforehand."

questions.stem: A client repeatedly asks the LPN/VN for special privileges and says, "The other nurses always let me." What is the best response?
questions.rationale: Clear, consistent limits enforced by the whole team reduce manipulative behavior. The nurse stays calm and nonjudgmental.

options.text: Grant the privilege to avoid conflict
Calmly restate the unit rules, set consistent limits, and share the behavior with the team
Argue with the client about the other nurses
Ignore the client completely

questions.stem: An older adult in long-term care seems withdrawn and sad. Which activity would the LPN/VN expect to support the resident's sense of meaning and connection?
questions.rationale: Reminiscence helps older adults review life experiences, build self-esteem, and connect with others, which can reduce depressive symptoms.

options.text: Confronting the resident about their mood
Encouraging the resident to share memories and photos from their life (reminiscence)
Limiting social activities
Keeping the resident in their room

questions.stem: A parent asks how to soothe a teething 7-month-old. Which suggestion by the LPN/VN is appropriate?
questions.rationale: The FDA warns against benzocaine products in young children because of the risk of methemoglobinemia. Teething jewelry poses choking and strangulation risks, and honey is unsafe before age 1 because of botulism.

options.text: "Rub a numbing gel with benzocaine on the gums."
"Offer a chilled (not frozen) teething ring and gently rub the gums with a clean finger."
"Use a teething necklace."
"Dip the pacifier in honey."

questions.stem: At what age is the first dose of the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine routinely given?
questions.rationale: The first MMR dose is given at 12–15 months and the second at 4–6 years. Infants traveling internationally may receive an early dose at 6–11 months.

options.text: At birth
At 2 months
At 12–15 months
At 11–12 years

questions.stem: A postpartum client who is not immune to rubella will receive the MMR vaccine before discharge. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: MMR is a live vaccine, so pregnancy is avoided for 4 weeks after vaccination. It is safe during breastfeeding.

options.text: "You must stop breastfeeding."
"Avoid becoming pregnant for at least 4 weeks after the vaccine. It is safe while breastfeeding."
"You'll need the vaccine every year."
"You can get pregnant right away."

questions.stem: A client in group therapy on an inpatient unit shares a painful experience. Another member laughs. What should the LPN/VN co-facilitator do?
questions.rationale: Group norms such as respect and confidentiality create a safe environment for sharing. Facilitators address behaviors that violate those norms.

options.text: Ignore the laughter
Address the behavior respectfully and reinforce the group norm of respect and confidentiality
Remove the client who shared
End the group session immediately

questions.stem: For each insulin, indicate its classification by onset and duration.
questions.rationale: Rapid-acting insulins are given with meals. Regular insulin is the only insulin routinely given IV. NPH is cloudy and has a peak. Long-acting insulins provide basal coverage with minimal peak and are not mixed with other insulins.
questions.answer_summary: Rapid: lispro, aspart. Short: regular. Intermediate: NPH. Long: glargine, detemir.

questions.stem: A resident who has been on bed rest for a week after a fall reports pain in the right calf. The LPN/VN notes the right calf is swollen, warm, and red compared with the left. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the resident is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Unilateral swelling, warmth, redness, and pain after immobility suggest DVT. Massage and compression devices on the affected leg could dislodge the clot. Sudden shortness of breath or chest pain may indicate pulmonary embolism and requires emergency response.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: deep vein thrombosis. Actions: keep the leg at rest and do not massage; report to the RN. Monitor: affected leg appearance and size; respiratory status.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Keep the leg at rest and avoid massaging it
Report the findings to the RN promptly
Massage the calf to relieve pain
Apply a sequential compression device to the right leg
Have the resident walk briskly in the hallway

bowtie_groups.label: Parameters to monitor (choose 2)
options: Appearance and size of the affected leg
Respiratory status for signs of pulmonary embolism

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN instruct a client to use a small-volume nebulizer?
questions.rationale: Upright positioning and slow, deep breaths deliver medication to the lower airways. Treatments usually take about 10–15 minutes.

options.text: "Lie flat and breathe rapidly."
"Sit upright, seal your lips around the mouthpiece, and breathe slowly and deeply until the mist stops."
"Hold your breath for the entire treatment."
"Use it only while walking."

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN read a tuberculin skin test?
questions.rationale: Induration, not redness, is measured at 48–72 hours. The threshold for a positive result depends on the client's risk factors.

options.text: Within 12 hours, measuring the redness
At 48–72 hours, measuring the diameter of induration (raised, firm area) in millimeters
At 1 week, noting whether it itches
Only if the client reports symptoms

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is reinforcing home blood pressure monitoring teaching. Which instruction is correct?
questions.rationale: Rest, proper positioning, and avoiding caffeine, exercise, and smoking for 30 minutes beforehand give accurate readings. Crossed legs and clothing under the cuff raise readings.

options.text: "Take your BP right after drinking coffee."
"Sit quietly for 5 minutes with your back supported, feet flat, and arm supported at heart level before measuring."
"Cross your legs during the reading."
"Take it over thick clothing."

questions.stem: Where should the LPN/VN palpate the dorsalis pedis pulse?
questions.rationale: The dorsalis pedis pulse is on the top of the foot. The posterior tibial pulse is behind the medial malleolus, the popliteal behind the knee, and the femoral in the groin.

options.text: Behind the inner ankle bone
On the top of the foot, lateral to the extensor tendon of the great toe
Behind the knee
In the groin

questions.stem: The LPN/VN presses on a client's ankle, and a 4-mm indentation rebounds in about 15 seconds. How should this be documented?
questions.rationale: A common scale rates 1+ as about 2 mm with immediate rebound, 2+ as about 4 mm with rebound in 10–15 seconds, 3+ as about 6 mm, and 4+ as about 8 mm with prolonged rebound. Facilities may use slightly different scales.

options.text: No edema
2+ pitting edema
4+ pitting edema
Nonpitting edema

questions.stem: Which pain assessment tool should the LPN/VN use for a resident with advanced dementia who cannot report pain?
questions.rationale: PAINAD evaluates breathing, vocalization, facial expression, body language, and consolability in people who cannot self-report pain.

options.text: 0–10 numeric rating scale
PAINAD scale (Pain Assessment in Advanced Dementia)
Glasgow Coma Scale
Braden Scale

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN check that a cane is the correct height?
questions.rationale: Correct height allows the client to bear weight through a slightly flexed elbow and supports balance without hunching.

options.text: The handle reaches the client's waist
The handle is level with the client's wrist crease (greater trochanter) when the arm hangs down, allowing about 15–30 degrees of elbow flexion
The handle reaches the client's shoulder
The cane is as tall as possible

questions.stem: Which action helps prevent shoulder subluxation in a client with left-sided hemiplegia?
questions.rationale: Weak shoulder muscles allow the joint to separate. Supporting the arm and avoiding traction on it prevent subluxation and pain.

options.text: Pull the client up by the left arm
Support the left arm on a pillow or armrest and avoid pulling on the affected arm
Let the left arm hang at the side while sitting
Apply a tight sling at all times

questions.stem: A resident with Alzheimer's disease becomes agitated during bathing. Which approach should the LPN/VN use?
questions.rationale: Feeling cold, exposed, and rushed often triggers agitation. Warmth, privacy, choices, and flexibility reduce distress.

options.text: Insist on a full shower immediately
Warm the room, cover the resident with a towel for privacy, offer simple choices, and consider a sponge bath or a different time
Bathe the resident quickly with cold water
Have several staff hold the resident

questions.stem: Before checking a fingerstick glucose, which step is most important for accuracy?
questions.rationale: Food residue, such as fruit juice, can falsely raise readings. Warm water increases blood flow. Wet alcohol and heavy squeezing distort results.

options.text: Wipe the finger with lotion
Wash hands with soap and warm water and dry them thoroughly
Use the first drop of blood after squeezing hard
Leave alcohol wet on the skin

questions.stem: A client with obesity asks about a healthy rate of weight loss. Which response by the LPN/VN is best?
questions.rationale: Gradual weight loss through dietary changes and physical activity is safer and more sustainable than rapid loss.

options.text: "Aim for 10 pounds per week."
"A gradual loss of about 1–2 pounds per week is realistic and more likely to last."
"Stop eating until you reach your goal."
"Weight loss should never be a goal."

questions.stem: A client taking daily oxycodone for cancer pain asks how to prevent constipation. Which regimen should the LPN/VN expect?
questions.rationale: Opioids slow bowel motility, and tolerance to this effect does not develop. A preventive regimen with a stimulant is recommended. Bulk fiber without enough fluid can worsen impaction.

options.text: Fiber supplements alone without extra fluids
A scheduled stool softener with a stimulant laxative, plus fluids as tolerated
No treatment until constipation occurs
Stopping the opioid

questions.stem: A client is upset about urinary leakage 2 weeks after a radical prostatectomy. What should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Temporary stress incontinence is common after prostatectomy. Pelvic floor exercises speed recovery. Severe fluid restriction concentrates urine and irritates the bladder.

options.text: "The leakage is permanent."
"Leakage is common after this surgery and often improves over months. Pelvic floor (Kegel) exercises can help."
"Limit fluids to 500 mL a day."
"Use a catheter permanently."

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce before a screening mammogram?
questions.rationale: Metallic particles in deodorants and powders can appear on images and mimic calcifications.

options.text: "Apply deodorant and powder beforehand."
"Do not use deodorant, powder, or lotion on your breasts or underarms on the day of the exam."
"Fast for 12 hours."
"Drink contrast before the test."

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce before a Pap test?
questions.rationale: These activities can wash away or obscure cervical cells and affect results.

options.text: "Douche the morning of the test."
"Avoid douching, intercourse, tampons, and vaginal medications for about 48 hours before the test."
"Schedule it during heavy menstrual bleeding."
"Use a vaginal cream the night before."

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is reinforcing teaching for a client starting combined oral contraceptives. Which symptom should the client report immediately?
questions.rationale: The ACHES warning signs (Abdominal pain, Chest pain, Headache, Eye problems, Severe leg pain) may signal clots, stroke, or other serious complications. Smoking increases clot risk.

options.text: Mild breast tenderness in the first month
Severe leg pain, chest pain, sudden severe headache, or vision changes
Lighter periods
Mild nausea in the first few weeks

questions.stem: A client is prescribed metronidazole for trichomoniasis. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Metronidazole with alcohol can cause a disulfiram-like reaction with severe nausea, vomiting, and flushing. Partners are treated to prevent reinfection.

options.text: "Alcohol is fine with this medicine."
"Avoid alcohol during treatment and for several days after, and your partner should be treated too."
"Your partner doesn't need treatment."
"You can stop once symptoms improve."

questions.stem: A parent asks what to expect after the child's routine vaccines. Which response by the LPN/VN is accurate?
questions.rationale: Mild local reactions and low-grade fever are common and short-lived. Serious reactions are rare but need prompt care. Aspirin is avoided in children.

options.text: "Soreness, mild swelling at the site, and a low-grade fever are common. Call if your child has a high fever, a seizure, or trouble breathing."
"Any fever means the vaccine didn't work."
"Side effects never occur."
"Give aspirin for fever."

questions.stem: A client with schizophrenia who often forgets oral medication is prescribed a long-acting injectable antipsychotic. Which statement by the client indicates understanding?
questions.rationale: Long-acting injectables improve adherence and reduce relapse. Regular scheduled injections maintain therapeutic levels.

options.text: "I can stop the shots whenever I feel better."
"I'll come to the clinic for my injection on schedule, even when I'm feeling well."
"The shot works for only a day."
"I'll take extra pills along with the shots."

questions.stem: Which finding in a mother 5 weeks after birth should the LPN/VN report to the RN or provider?
questions.rationale: Symptoms lasting more than 2 weeks that affect functioning suggest postpartum depression, which requires evaluation and treatment. Screening tools such as the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale are commonly used.

options.text: Feeling tired from night feedings
Persistent sadness, loss of interest in the baby, and difficulty functioning for more than 2 weeks
Occasional tearfulness during the first week after birth
Enjoying time with the baby

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce about preparing infant formula?
questions.rationale: Overdiluting can cause water intoxication and poor growth, and underdiluting stresses the kidneys. Microwaves create hot spots. Leftover formula can grow bacteria and is discarded.

options.text: "Add extra water to make the formula last longer."
"Follow the label mixing instructions exactly, and don't warm bottles in the microwave."
"Save leftover formula from a feeding for the next day."
"Add cereal to the bottle to help the baby sleep."

questions.stem: A parent asks when and how to start solid foods. Which response by the LPN/VN reflects current guidance?
questions.rationale: Solids are typically introduced around 6 months. Introducing one new food at a time helps identify reactions. Early introduction of peanut products, in an age-appropriate form, may reduce peanut allergy risk. Whole nuts are a choking hazard.

options.text: "Start cereal in the bottle at 2 months."
"Around 6 months, when your baby shows readiness, introduce single-ingredient foods one at a time. Ask your provider about introducing peanut-containing foods early."
"Wait until age 1 to start solids."
"Give whole nuts as a first food."

questions.stem: How should parents protect a 3-month-old from the sun?
questions.rationale: Infants under 6 months have sensitive skin. Shade and clothing are the primary protection, and sunscreen may be used sparingly on small areas when needed.

options.text: "Apply adult sunscreen generously all over."
"Keep the baby in the shade and use lightweight protective clothing and a wide-brimmed hat. Use a small amount of sunscreen only on exposed areas if shade isn't available."
"Brief sunburns build tolerance."
"Use tanning oil."

questions.stem: For each vaccine, indicate whether it is a live attenuated vaccine or a non-live (inactivated or subunit) vaccine.
questions.rationale: Live vaccines are generally avoided during pregnancy and in severely immunocompromised people. Non-live vaccines can usually be given safely, although immune response may be reduced.
questions.answer_summary: Live: MMR, varicella, oral rotavirus. Non-live: IPV, Tdap, hepatitis B.

questions.stem: A resident who had hip surgery 10 days ago suddenly reports sharp chest pain when breathing in and says, "I can't catch my breath." The LPN/VN notes RR 30/min, HR 122/min, SpO2 86% on room air, and anxiety. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the resident is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Sudden pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, tachycardia, and hypoxemia after orthopedic surgery suggest PE, a life-threatening emergency. The resident is kept at rest in an upright position with oxygen while emergency care is summoned. Walking and leg massage could worsen embolization.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: pulmonary embolism. Actions: raise the head of the bed and apply oxygen; call for emergency help and notify the RN. Monitor: RR and SpO2; HR and BP.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Raise the head of the bed and apply oxygen per protocol
Call for emergency help and notify the RN immediately
Walk the resident to relieve anxiety

questions.stem: While completing a preoperative checklist, which finding should the LPN/VN report to the RN before the client goes to surgery?
questions.rationale: Eating within the required fasting period increases aspiration risk under anesthesia. The surgical team must be notified, and surgery may be delayed.

options.text: The client's dentures have been removed
The client says they ate a piece of toast 2 hours ago
The client's ID band is in place
The client voided before transport

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is reinforcing preoperative teaching about coughing after abdominal surgery. Which instruction is correct?
questions.rationale: Splinting reduces pain and stress on the incision, and deep breathing followed by coughing clears secretions and prevents atelectasis and pneumonia.

options.text: "Avoid coughing to protect your incision."
"Hold a pillow firmly against your incision, take a few deep breaths, and then cough."
"Cough only once a day."
"Lie flat while coughing."

questions.stem: A client is getting out of bed for the first time after surgery. Which action should the LPN/VN take first?
questions.rationale: Dangling allows blood pressure to adjust and helps prevent orthostatic hypotension and falls. The nurse assists with a gait belt.

options.text: Have the client stand quickly
Have the client sit on the edge of the bed and dangle the legs for a few minutes, checking for dizziness
Walk the client to the hallway immediately
Let the client walk alone

questions.stem: A client going home after surgery has adhesive wound closure strips over the incision. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Removing strips early can separate the wound edges. Showering is usually allowed, but soaking is avoided until the provider permits it.

options.text: "Pull the strips off after 1 day."
"Let the strips fall off on their own, usually in 7–14 days. Trim loose edges if needed."
"Soak the incision in a bath daily."
"Apply lotion over the strips."

questions.stem: A client with postoperative nausea is ready to begin oral intake. Which order of diet advancement does the LPN/VN expect?
questions.rationale: Gradual advancement based on tolerance and bowel function reduces nausea and vomiting.

options.text: Regular diet, then clear liquids
Ice chips or sips of clear liquids, then full liquids, then soft or regular foods as tolerated
Full liquids only for 2 weeks
Solid foods first

questions.stem: A client is going home after inguinal hernia repair. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Lifting and straining raise intra-abdominal pressure and can cause recurrence. Fiber and fluids prevent constipation.

options.text: "Return to heavy lifting tomorrow."
"Avoid heavy lifting and straining for several weeks as instructed, and prevent constipation."
"Cough forcefully several times a day."
"Limit fluids."

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce after endoscopic sinus surgery?
questions.rationale: Nose blowing and closed-mouth sneezing raise pressure and can cause bleeding. Aspirin and NSAIDs increase bleeding risk unless approved.

options.text: "Blow your nose forcefully to clear the drainage."
"Avoid blowing your nose, and sneeze with your mouth open."
"Bend over to pick up heavy items."
"Take aspirin for pain."

questions.stem: A child has bacterial conjunctivitis. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Bacterial conjunctivitis is contagious. Handwashing and not sharing personal items prevent spread. A separate clean cloth or tissue is used for each eye.

options.text: "Share towels with siblings."
"Wash hands often, use separate towels and washcloths, and give eye drops as prescribed."
"Rub the eyes to remove drainage."
"Use the same tissue for both eyes."

questions.stem: A client with otitis externa (swimmer's ear) asks how to prevent it in the future. Which advice should the LPN/VN give?
questions.rationale: Moisture and trauma to the ear canal promote bacterial and fungal growth. Gently drying the ears and avoiding swabs reduce risk.

options.text: "Clean your ears daily with cotton swabs."
"Keep your ears dry after swimming or bathing, and avoid putting objects in the ear canal."
"Swim without drying your ears."
"Use hairpins to remove wax."

questions.stem: A child is diagnosed with tinea capitis (scalp ringworm). Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Tinea capitis requires oral antifungals because topical agents cannot reach the hair follicles. It spreads through shared items.

options.text: "A cream alone will cure it."
"Give the oral antifungal medication for the full course, and don't share combs, brushes, or hats."
"Shave the child's head."
"Stop the medication when the scalp looks better."

questions.stem: A client with lactose intolerance is concerned about getting enough calcium. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Many calcium sources don't contain lactose. Lactase supplements and hard cheeses or yogurt may also be tolerated.

options.text: "Avoid all calcium."
"Try lactose-free or fortified plant milks, leafy greens, canned salmon with bones, and lactase enzyme products."
"Drink more regular milk to build tolerance."
"Calcium isn't important for adults."

questions.stem: A client following a strict vegan diet asks which supplement is most important. Which response by the LPN/VN is best?
questions.rationale: Without supplementation or fortified foods, people following a vegan diet risk B12 deficiency, which causes anemia and neurological damage.

options.text: "Vitamin C"
"Vitamin B12, since it is found almost exclusively in animal products"
"Sodium"
"Fiber"

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is asked to place a client in semi-Fowler's position. How high should the head of the bed be raised?
questions.rationale: Semi-Fowler's is about 30–45 degrees. Fowler's is about 45–60 degrees, and high-Fowler's is about 60–90 degrees.

options.text: 0–10 degrees
About 30–45 degrees
About 60–90 degrees
Below the level of the feet

questions.stem: Which action ensures safety while the LPN/VN makes an occupied bed?
questions.rationale: The opposite rail prevents the client from rolling out while turned. The bed is lowered and locked when finished.

options.text: Lower both side rails while working
Keep the side rail up on the side opposite where the nurse is working, and raise the bed to a comfortable working height
Leave the bed in its highest position when finished
Have the client stand on the floor barefoot

questions.stem: A client needs a stool specimen for ova and parasites. Which action by the LPN/VN is correct?
questions.rationale: Parasites may be detected best in fresh specimens. Urine, water, and paper can destroy organisms or contaminate the sample. Multiple specimens may be needed.

options.text: Collect stool from the toilet water
Collect a fresh specimen without urine or toilet paper and send it to the lab promptly or in preservative per policy
Refrigerate the specimen for 2 days before sending
Mix the stool with water

questions.stem: When is the best time to change a client's ostomy pouching system?
questions.rationale: Changing when output is low reduces mess and makes it easier to get a good seal. Pouching systems are changed on a regular schedule and when leaking.

options.text: Right after a large meal
Before meals or early in the morning, when stoma output is usually lowest
Only when it leaks
At bedtime after dinner

questions.stem: A client who injects insulin at home asks how to dispose of used needles. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Puncture-resistant containers protect family members and sanitation workers. Local rules for disposal vary.

options.text: "Put them in the regular trash in a plastic bag."
"Use an FDA-cleared sharps container or a heavy-duty plastic container with a tight lid, such as a laundry detergent bottle, and follow local disposal rules."
"Recap them and throw them away."
"Flush them down the toilet."

questions.stem: A client colonized with MRSA is prescribed decolonization before surgery. Which regimen does the LPN/VN expect?
questions.rationale: Decolonization with nasal mupirocin and chlorhexidine bathing reduces the bacterial load and the risk of surgical site infection.

options.text: Oral vancomycin for 6 weeks
Intranasal mupirocin and chlorhexidine body washes for several days as prescribed
No treatment is needed
Alcohol hand rub applied to the nose

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is using the CAGE questionnaire. Which question is part of this screening tool?
questions.rationale: CAGE asks about Cutting down, Annoyance at criticism, Guilt, and needing an Eye-opener in the morning. Two or more yes answers suggest problematic drinking. The AUDIT-C is another common tool.

options.text: "Do you drink more than your friends?"
"Have you ever felt you should Cut down on your drinking?"
"What is your favorite drink?"
"Do you drink only on weekends?"

questions.stem: An 8-month-old cries and clings to the parent when the LPN/VN approaches. How should the nurse interpret this behavior?
questions.rationale: Stranger anxiety typically begins around 6–8 months and shows healthy attachment. Letting the infant warm up while the parent stays close reduces distress.

options.text: As a sign of developmental delay
As normal stranger anxiety. The nurse approaches slowly, talks to the parent first, and does exams on the parent's lap when possible.
As evidence of abuse
As an allergic reaction

questions.stem: A parent asks about the color of a breastfed newborn's stools. Which pattern should the LPN/VN describe as normal?
questions.rationale: This progression shows feeding is adequate and the GI tract is working. Pale or clay-colored stools may indicate biliary obstruction, and blood in the stool needs evaluation.

options.text: Black, sticky stools that continue for 2 weeks
Thick, black meconium for 1–2 days, then greenish transitional stools, then yellow, seedy stools by about day 4–5
Clay-colored stools
Bright red stools

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate whether it is more consistent with true labor or false labor.
questions.rationale: Cervical change is the key sign of true labor. False labor contractions are irregular and often ease with rest, hydration, or position changes.
questions.answer_summary: True: regular and closer contractions, cervical change, intensifying with walking. False: stop with rest, irregular lower abdominal discomfort, no cervical change.

rows.text: Contractions that become regular and closer together
Contractions that stop with rest or a change in position
Irregular contractions felt mainly in the lower abdomen

questions.stem: A client has an itchy poison ivy rash. Which comfort measure should the LPN/VN suggest?
questions.rationale: Cool water and colloidal oatmeal soothe itching. Hot water and scratching worsen itching and increase infection risk.

options.text: Hot showers
Cool compresses or oatmeal baths, and keeping the nails short to avoid scratching
Rubbing alcohol on the rash
Breaking the blisters

questions.stem: How long should the LPN/VN teach school-age children to scrub their hands with soap?
questions.rationale: Scrubbing for at least 20 seconds removes germs effectively. A song helps children time the scrub.

options.text: About 5 seconds
At least 20 seconds, such as humming "Happy Birthday" twice
About 2 minutes
Only rinse with water

questions.stem: Four hours after abdominal surgery, a client is restless. The LPN/VN finds the dressing saturated with bright red blood. HR is 128/min, BP 86/50 mm Hg (was 124/76), and the skin is cool and clammy. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the client is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Active bright red bleeding with tachycardia, hypotension, and cool, clammy skin indicates hemorrhage and shock. Pressure and immediate escalation are needed. The client may need a return to surgery, IV fluids, and blood products. Oral intake and ambulation are unsafe.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: postoperative hemorrhage with hypovolemic shock. Actions: reinforce the dressing and apply pressure; notify the RN and rapid response team. Monitor: vital signs; amount of bleeding.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Reinforce the dressing and apply pressure over the site
Notify the RN and rapid response team immediately
Remove the dressing and leave the incision open
Help the client walk to the bathroom

bowtie_groups.label: Parameters to monitor (choose 2)
options: Amount of bleeding on the dressing

questions.stem: A parent asks when a 7-year-old can stop using a booster seat. Which response by the LPN/VN is correct?
questions.rationale: Booster seats position the seat belt correctly until the child is tall enough. Children under 13 should ride in the back seat.

options.text: "At age 5."
"When your child is about 4 feet 9 inches tall and the adult seat belt fits properly across the upper thighs and chest, usually between ages 8 and 12."
"When your child can buckle the seat belt alone."
"When your child weighs 40 pounds."

questions.stem: When should a child have a first dental visit?
questions.rationale: Early visits allow fluoride varnish, cavity prevention, and parent teaching. Infants are not put to bed with a bottle of milk or juice.

options.text: At age 5
By the first birthday or within 6 months after the first tooth appears
When all baby teeth are in
Only if there is tooth pain

questions.stem: A 10-year-old's BMI is at the 96th percentile for age and sex. How should the LPN/VN interpret this?
questions.rationale: For children, a BMI at or above the 95th percentile is obesity, and the 85th to below the 95th percentile is overweight. Family-centered lifestyle counseling is recommended.

options.text: Healthy weight
Overweight
Obesity
Underweight

questions.stem: The parent of a 7-year-old who wets the bed asks for advice. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Bedwetting is common and often resolves with time. Supportive behavioral measures work best. Punishment and shame worsen the problem.

options.text: "Punish your child for wet nights."
"Limit fluids in the evening, have your child void before bed, consider a bedwetting alarm, and praise dry nights."
"Wake your child every hour."
"Stop all fluids after lunch."

questions.stem: A toddler has hand, foot, and mouth disease. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: This viral illness causes painful mouth sores that can lead to dehydration. It spreads through secretions and stool. Antibiotics are not effective, and aspirin is avoided in children.

options.text: "Give antibiotics."
"Encourage cool fluids to prevent dehydration, and wash hands well, especially after diaper changes."
"Give aspirin for pain."
"It is not contagious."

questions.stem: An older adult with arthritis often cannot reach the bathroom in time. Which intervention should the LPN/VN suggest?
questions.rationale: Functional incontinence results from mobility or environmental barriers rather than bladder problems. Removing barriers and adapting clothing help.

options.text: Restrict fluids
Keep a clear path to the bathroom, provide a bedside commode, and suggest clothing that is easy to remove
Insert an indwelling catheter
Use sedatives at night

questions.stem: An 80-year-old says, "I wake up earlier and sleep more lightly than I used to." How should the LPN/VN respond?
questions.rationale: Aging reduces deep sleep and shifts sleep earlier. Sleep hygiene is preferred over sedatives, which increase fall and confusion risk in older adults.

options.text: "You should start taking a sleeping pill."
"Lighter sleep and waking earlier are common with aging. Let's talk about habits that can help you rest."
"This is a sign of dementia."
"You should nap for several hours each afternoon."

questions.stem: A client on a 2,000-mg sodium restriction is reading a soup label: 800 mg sodium per serving, 2 servings per can. The client plans to eat the whole can. What should the LPN/VN point out?
questions.rationale: Nutrition labels list values per serving. Eating the whole can doubles the amount. Teaching label reading helps clients follow sodium restrictions.

options.text: "That's only 800 mg of sodium."
"The whole can contains 1,600 mg of sodium, most of your daily limit."
"Canned soup has no sodium."
"Servings don't matter."

questions.stem: Which energy-conservation strategy should the LPN/VN reinforce for a client with severe COPD?
questions.rationale: Sitting, pacing activities, and efficient body mechanics reduce oxygen demand and dyspnea. Exhaling during exertion (pursed lips) also helps.

options.text: "Stand while showering."
"Sit while showering and dressing, plan rest periods, and push rather than pull objects."
"Complete all chores in the morning without breaks."
"Carry heavy laundry baskets up stairs quickly."

questions.stem: A client with a cough is waiting in the clinic. Which respiratory hygiene measure should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Masking, covering coughs, hand hygiene, and spacing reduce transmission of respiratory infections in waiting areas.

options.text: "Cough into your hands."
"Wear a mask, cover coughs with a tissue or your elbow, and wash or sanitize your hands afterward."
"Sit close to other clients."
"Remove your mask to talk."

questions.stem: A client is prescribed a low-residue (low-fiber) diet. Which food choice is appropriate?
questions.rationale: Low-residue diets limit fiber and hard-to-digest foods to reduce stool bulk. They may be used during bowel flares or before procedures.

options.text: Raw vegetables and nuts
White rice, eggs, and well-cooked, peeled vegetables
Bran cereal
Popcorn and seeds

questions.stem: A client with chronic constipation asks which breakfast is highest in fiber. Which option should the LPN/VN recommend?
questions.rationale: Whole grains, fruit, and seeds provide fiber. Fiber should be increased gradually with adequate fluids to prevent bloating.

options.text: White toast with butter
Oatmeal topped with berries and a sprinkle of ground flaxseed
Scrambled eggs and bacon
A glazed donut

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is reinforcing teaching for a client doing continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis at home. Which step is most important for preventing peritonitis?
questions.rationale: Touch contamination is the main cause of PD peritonitis. A clean, closed room, hand hygiene, masking, and aseptic connections reduce risk. Dialysate is warmed with a dry heating method approved by the program, not a microwave.

options.text: Performing exchanges in the bathroom with the window open
Washing hands thoroughly, wearing a mask, and using aseptic technique when connecting and disconnecting
Warming the dialysate in the microwave
Skipping exchanges when feeling well

questions.stem: A visitor falls and has an obvious deformity of the forearm. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Splinting in the position found prevents further injury. The nurse checks pulses, sensation, and movement before and after splinting, applies cold, elevates if possible, and arranges medical evaluation.

options.text: Straighten the arm
Immobilize the arm in the position found, including the joints above and below, and check circulation distal to the injury
Have the visitor move the arm to test the injury
Apply heat

questions.stem: A 13-year-old athlete had a concussion during a game. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Returning to play too early risks second impact syndrome. Worsening symptoms may indicate a brain bleed. Screen time and intense cognitive activity are limited early in recovery.

options.text: "Return to play tomorrow if you feel fine."
"Rest from sports and follow a gradual return plan only after a health care provider clears you. Report worsening headache, repeated vomiting, or confusion immediately."
"Play video games for long periods to rest your brain."
"Take aspirin for headache."

questions.stem: A client reports bites and small blood spots on the sheets and is worried about bed bugs. Which information by the LPN/VN is accurate?
questions.rationale: Bed bug bites cause itching but do not transmit disease. Heat treatment of linens and professional extermination are effective. Infestations occur regardless of cleanliness.

options.text: "Bed bugs spread serious diseases like HIV."
"Bed bugs are not known to spread disease. Wash bedding in hot water, dry on high heat, and contact a professional pest control service."
"Spray insecticide directly on your skin."
"Bed bugs only live in dirty homes."

questions.stem: A client says, "They're always watching me." Which response by the LPN/VN is an example of clarifying?
questions.rationale: Clarifying asks the client to explain vague statements to improve understanding. Disagreeing, reassuring, and "why" questions are nontherapeutic.

options.text: "No one is watching you."
"Who do you mean by 'they'?"
"You'll feel better soon."
"Why do you think that?"

questions.stem: A healthy pregnant client asks about exercise. Which response by the LPN/VN reflects current guidance?
questions.rationale: Regular moderate exercise is safe and beneficial in uncomplicated pregnancies. Prolonged supine positioning after the first trimester and activities with fall or abdominal trauma risk are avoided.

options.text: "Avoid all exercise during pregnancy."
"Aim for about 150 minutes of moderate activity per week, such as walking or swimming, and avoid contact sports and activities with a high risk of falling."
"Start a new high-intensity sport now."
"Exercise only while lying flat on your back."

questions.stem: A multiparous client on postpartum day 1 reports strong cramping during breastfeeding. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Afterpains result from uterine contractions stimulated by oxytocin during breastfeeding. They are often stronger in multiparous clients. A full bladder worsens them.

options.text: "Stop breastfeeding."
"Empty your bladder, lie on your stomach with a small pillow, and take your prescribed pain medication about 30–60 minutes before feeding."
"Apply heat directly to your perineum."
"This means something is wrong."

questions.stem: A parent asks why erythromycin ointment is placed in the newborn's eyes. Which response by the LPN/VN is accurate?
questions.rationale: Erythromycin prophylaxis prevents gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum, which can cause blindness. It is required in many states.

options.text: "It prevents jaundice."
