"It helps prevent a serious eye infection caused by gonorrhea that can be passed during birth."
"It improves vision."
"It prevents bleeding."

questions.stem: Several residents in a long-term care facility have sudden vomiting and diarrhea. Norovirus is suspected. Which action should the LPN/VN expect?
questions.rationale: Norovirus is very contagious and resists alcohol. Soap-and-water handwashing, bleach-based disinfection, contact precautions, and excluding ill staff limit outbreaks.

options.text: Clean surfaces with alcohol wipes only
Clean with a disinfectant effective against norovirus (such as a bleach solution), and exclude ill staff from work until at least 48 hours after symptoms end
Allow ill staff to keep working if they wear masks
Use hand sanitizer instead of soap and water

questions.stem: For each food, indicate the minimum safe internal cooking temperature recommended by the USDA.
questions.rationale: Poultry (including ground) and leftovers require 165°F. Ground meats other than poultry require 160°F. Whole cuts of beef, pork, and lamb, and fish, require 145°F (with a 3-minute rest for meats). A food thermometer is the only reliable check.
questions.answer_summary: 145°F: salmon, pork chops (whole cuts, with rest). 160°F: ground beef. 165°F: chicken, ground turkey, reheated leftovers.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old will be hospitalized for 2 weeks. Which intervention best supports the child's developmental needs?
questions.rationale: School-age children are in Erikson's stage of industry vs. inferiority. Continuing schoolwork, peer contact, and a sense of accomplishment support coping.

options.text: Keep the child isolated from peers
Arrange schoolwork, allow contact with friends, and give the child age-appropriate choices and tasks
Treat the child like a toddler
Discourage questions about treatment

questions.stem: A resident with new dentures is eating less and says food "doesn't taste right." Which action by the LPN/VN is most appropriate?
questions.rationale: Poorly fitting dentures cause sores and pain that reduce intake, which increases malnutrition risk. A dental referral may be needed.

options.text: Document that the resident is a picky eater
Check the fit of the dentures and the mouth for sores, and report the findings to the RN
Switch the resident to a liquid diet without an order
Remove the dentures permanently

questions.stem: The LPN/VN finds a visitor collapsed in the hallway. The visitor is unresponsive and is not breathing normally (only occasional gasps). Complete the diagram by choosing the condition, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take first, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Gasping (agonal breathing) is not normal breathing and indicates cardiac arrest. Healthcare providers check for a pulse for no more than 10 seconds. CPR begins with compressions (C-A-B), and an AED is used as soon as it arrives.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: cardiac arrest. Actions: call for help and get an AED; begin chest compressions immediately. Monitor: responsiveness and breathing; AED rhythm analysis.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take first (choose 2)
options: Call for help, activate the emergency response, and send for an AED
Check for a pulse for 30 seconds before doing anything
Give the visitor sips of water

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce about bathing an infant?
questions.rationale: The wrist and elbow are more sensitive to heat than the fingertips. About 100°F (38°C) is appropriate. Constant supervision prevents drowning.

options.text: "Test the water with your fingertips; hot is fine."
"Test the water with your wrist or elbow to make sure it feels warm, not hot, and keep one hand on the baby at all times."
"Fill the tub to the baby's chest."
"Leave the baby briefly to grab a towel."

questions.stem: A parent plans to buy a baby walker to help an infant learn to walk. What should the LPN/VN advise?
questions.rationale: The American Academy of Pediatrics advises against baby walkers because of injury risk. They do not help children walk sooner.

options.text: "Walkers help babies walk earlier."
"Baby walkers are not recommended because they cause falls down stairs and other injuries. A stationary activity center is safer."
"Walkers are safe if used near stairs."
"Use the walker in the kitchen near the stove."

questions.stem: A breastfeeding mother asks whether to offer her infant a pacifier at sleep time. Which response by the LPN/VN reflects current guidance?
questions.rationale: Pacifier use during sleep is associated with lower SIDS risk. It should not be attached to cords, and honey is unsafe before age 1.

options.text: "Never use a pacifier."
"Offering a pacifier at nap and bedtime may reduce the risk of SIDS. Wait until breastfeeding is well established, usually about 3–4 weeks."
"Tie the pacifier around the baby's neck."
"Dip it in honey so the baby takes it."

questions.stem: A 2-year-old drinks about 40 oz of cow's milk daily, eats little solid food, and is pale. What concern should the LPN/VN report?
questions.rationale: Too much cow's milk displaces iron-rich foods and can cause GI blood loss and iron deficiency. Toddlers typically need about 16–24 oz per day.

options.text: Vitamin C toxicity
Iron deficiency anemia from excessive milk intake
Hypercalcemia only
Lactose intolerance

questions.stem: An older adult reports cloudy, blurred vision, faded colors, and trouble with glare from headlights at night. Which condition should the LPN/VN recognize as a likely cause?
questions.rationale: Clouding of the lens causes blurred vision, glare, faded colors, and poor night vision. The finding is reported for an eye evaluation.

options.text: Cataracts
Macular degeneration
Retinal detachment
Conjunctivitis

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce for a client using a sitz bath?
questions.rationale: Warm water promotes circulation and comfort. Vasodilation can cause dizziness, so the client rises slowly with help available.

options.text: "Use very hot water for 1 hour."
"Use warm water and soak for about 15–20 minutes, then pat the area dry. Call for help if you feel dizzy."
"Add bubble bath."
"Stand up quickly when finished."

questions.stem: Which action is correct when the LPN/VN applies a warm compress?
questions.rationale: Prolonged or direct heat can cause burns, especially with impaired sensation or circulation. Heat is avoided with active bleeding or acute inflammation.

options.text: Leave it on overnight
Check the skin frequently, limit application to about 20–30 minutes, and use extra caution over areas with decreased sensation
Apply it directly over an area of active bleeding
Have the client lie on the heating pad

questions.stem: A client just drank a cup of hot coffee. What should the LPN/VN do before taking an oral temperature?
questions.rationale: Recent intake of hot or cold substances or smoking alters oral temperature readings.

options.text: Take the temperature immediately
Wait about 15–30 minutes after hot or cold drinks, eating, or smoking
Take it with the client's mouth open
Subtract 1 degree from the reading

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is drawing blood. How long can the tourniquet generally remain in place?
questions.rationale: Prolonged tourniquet time causes hemoconcentration and can falsely alter lab values, such as potassium. It is also uncomfortable.

options.text: 5 minutes
No longer than about 1 minute
Until the end of the shift
15 minutes

questions.stem: Where should the LPN/VN perform a heel stick on a newborn?
questions.rationale: The sides of the heel avoid the calcaneus, nerves, and arteries in the center and back. Warming the heel first improves blood flow.

options.text: The center of the heel
The medial or lateral side of the plantar surface of the heel
The back of the heel
The ball of the foot

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN collect a routine urine specimen from an infant who is not toilet trained?
questions.rationale: Bags are used for routine specimens. Cultures usually require catheterization for accuracy. The bag is removed promptly to prevent skin irritation.

options.text: Squeeze the diaper into a cup
Clean the perineum, apply a pediatric urine collection bag, and check it frequently
Give the infant large amounts of water first
Collect urine from the bath water

questions.stem: When should the LPN/VN label a blood specimen?
questions.rationale: Labeling at the bedside right after collection prevents mislabeling, which can cause wrong treatment or fatal transfusion errors.

options.text: Before entering the room, to save time
At the bedside, in the client's presence, immediately after collection, using two identifiers
At the nurses' station after collecting several specimens
The lab will label it

questions.stem: A client taking insulin reports nightmares, damp sheets, and a morning headache. What does the LPN/VN suspect?
questions.rationale: Night sweats, nightmares, restlessness, and morning headache suggest nocturnal hypoglycemia. Bedtime or overnight glucose checks and insulin adjustment may be needed.

options.text: Sleep apnea
Nighttime hypoglycemia
Hyperglycemia
A viral illness

questions.stem: A client is NPO before surgery and reports a dry mouth. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Oral care relieves dryness and reduces bacteria while keeping the client NPO. Candy and swallowed fluids break NPO status.

options.text: Give a glass of water
Provide frequent mouth care, such as brushing, rinsing without swallowing, and applying lip moisturizer
Offer hard candy
Tell the client nothing can be done

questions.stem: A client uses a cool-mist humidifier at home for dry airways. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Standing water can grow organisms that are then inhaled. Regular cleaning and distilled water reduce this risk.

options.text: "Change the water once a month."
"Empty and clean the humidifier regularly, as directed by the manufacturer, and use distilled water to prevent mold and bacteria."
"Add bleach to the water while it runs."
"Never clean it."

questions.stem: A client is going home after knee arthroscopy. Which finding should the client report immediately?
questions.rationale: Calf pain, warmth, and swelling may indicate DVT. Mild swelling and minor drainage are expected, and ice and elevation are recommended.

options.text: Mild swelling around the knee
Pain, warmth, and swelling in the calf
Small amount of drainage on the dressing
Stiffness that improves with prescribed exercises

questions.topic: Bowel program in spinal cord injury
questions.stem: Which intervention should the LPN/VN include in a bowel program for a client with a spinal cord injury?
questions.rationale: Clients with spinal cord injury may not feel the urge to defecate. A scheduled program using the gastrocolic reflex and prescribed stimulation promotes regular evacuation and prevents impaction and autonomic dysreflexia.

options.text: Offer toileting only when the client feels the urge
Perform the program at the same time daily, often after a meal, using a suppository or digital stimulation as prescribed
Restrict fluids and fiber
Use daily enemas indefinitely

questions.stem: A client who drinks heavily every day was admitted for surgery. When should the LPN/VN expect early withdrawal symptoms such as tremors and anxiety to begin?
questions.rationale: Early withdrawal begins within hours. Seizures may occur around 12–48 hours, and delirium tremens typically at 48–96 hours. Accurate alcohol histories allow early monitoring.

options.text: After 2 weeks
About 6–24 hours after the last drink
Only after 5 days
Immediately after the last drink

questions.stem: Which strategy should the LPN/VN suggest to the parent of a child with ADHD?
questions.rationale: Structure, clear single-step directions, and immediate positive reinforcement support children with attention difficulties.

options.text: "Give several instructions at once."
"Keep a consistent routine, give one short instruction at a time, and praise positive behavior right away."
"Remove all structure."
"Punish every mistake."

questions.stem: A pregnant client with a normal prepregnancy BMI asks how much weight she should gain. Which response by the LPN/VN is correct?
questions.rationale: National Academy of Medicine guidelines recommend 25–35 lb for a normal BMI. Recommendations are lower for overweight and obese BMIs and higher for underweight BMIs.

options.text: "About 5–10 pounds."
"About 25–35 pounds over the whole pregnancy."
"About 50–60 pounds."
"You shouldn't gain weight."

questions.stem: Which observation indicates that a newborn is latched correctly during breastfeeding?
questions.rationale: A deep latch allows effective milk transfer and prevents nipple trauma. Clicking, dimpled cheeks, and persistent pain suggest a shallow latch.

options.text: The newborn's lips are tucked in, and there are clicking sounds
The newborn's mouth is wide open, the lips are flanged outward, much of the areola is in the mouth, and swallowing is audible
Only the nipple is in the newborn's mouth
The mother reports sharp pain throughout the feeding

questions.stem: A breastfed newborn weighed 3,500 g at birth and weighs 3,290 g on day 3. The parents are worried. How should the LPN/VN respond?
questions.rationale: Newborns commonly lose up to about 7–10% of birth weight in the first days. Here the loss is 210 g ÷ 3,500 g = 6%. Loss above about 10%, or poor output, should be reported.

options.text: "Your baby is severely dehydrated."
"A weight loss of about 6% in the first few days is common. Most babies regain birth weight by 10–14 days."
"You need to switch to formula immediately."
"This means breastfeeding has failed."

questions.stem: For which client should the LPN/VN question an order for ice packs?
questions.rationale: Cold causes vasoconstriction and can trigger vasospasm and ischemia in clients with Raynaud's phenomenon or impaired circulation.

options.text: A client with an ankle sprain 2 hours ago
A client with Raynaud's phenomenon who needs ice applied to the hands
A client with a bruise after a fall
A client with swelling after dental surgery

questions.stem: For each situation, indicate whether heat or cold therapy is generally more appropriate.
questions.rationale: Cold reduces swelling, bleeding, and acute pain through vasoconstriction. Heat increases blood flow and relaxes muscles for chronic pain and stiffness.
questions.answer_summary: Heat: chronic muscle spasm, arthritis stiffness, menstrual cramps. Cold: acute sprain, postoperative swelling, nosebleed.

rows.text: Ankle sprain within the first 24 hours

questions.stem: During a blood draw, a client suddenly becomes pale and sweaty, says "I feel faint," and briefly loses consciousness while sitting in a chair. HR is 48/min, and BP is 82/50 mm Hg. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the client is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: A vasovagal reaction causes sudden bradycardia and hypotension, reducing blood flow to the brain. Lying flat with legs raised restores cerebral perfusion. The client should recover within a minute or two. Oral fluids are given only when fully alert, and persistent unresponsiveness requires emergency response.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: vasovagal syncope. Actions: stop the procedure, lie the client down, and raise the legs; stay with the client and call the RN. Monitor: LOC; HR and BP.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Stop the procedure, lower the client to a lying position, and raise the legs
Stay with the client and call for the RN
Give fluids while the client is still unconscious
Leave the client to get help

questions.stem: Which action is correct when the LPN/VN provides care for a healed gastrostomy tube site?
questions.rationale: Gentle cleaning and keeping the site dry prevent skin breakdown and infection. The external bolster should not be too tight, which can cause pressure injury.

options.text: Clean the site daily with soap and water, dry it well, and check for redness or leakage
Apply a thick layer of petroleum jelly under the bolster
Pull the tube tight against the skin
Leave a wet dressing on the site

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is removing a nasogastric tube. What should the client be instructed to do as the tube is withdrawn?
questions.rationale: Holding the breath closes the epiglottis and reduces the risk of aspirating secretions from the tube. The tube is clamped or kinked during removal.

options.text: Take slow, deep breaths in
Take a deep breath and hold it while the tube is withdrawn smoothly
Swallow repeatedly
Talk continuously

questions.stem: A client has copious oral secretions and difficulty swallowing. Which device should the LPN/VN use to clear the mouth?
questions.rationale: A Yankauer suction removes secretions from the mouth and oropharynx. The nurse avoids stimulating the gag reflex.

options.text: A sterile tracheal suction catheter inserted deep into the trachea
A rigid Yankauer (tonsil-tip) suction device
A bulb syringe for adults
A tongue blade

questions.stem: Which instruction is correct for using a dry powder inhaler?
questions.rationale: Dry powder inhalers depend on a fast, deep breath to pull the powder into the lungs. Exhaling into the device introduces moisture that clumps the powder. They are not shaken and do not use spacers.

options.text: "Shake the inhaler well before each use."
"Breathe out away from the device, seal your lips around it, and breathe in quickly and deeply."
"Exhale into the inhaler before breathing in."
"Use a spacer with it."

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN position the ear when taking a tympanic temperature on an adult?
questions.rationale: Straightening the ear canal allows the probe to sense tympanic membrane temperature. In young children under 3, the pinna is pulled down and back.

options.text: Pull the pinna down and back
Pull the pinna up and back, then insert the probe snugly toward the eardrum
Insert the probe without moving the ear
Push the tragus forward

questions.stem: When should the LPN/VN recommend inserting a vaginal cream?
questions.rationale: Lying down after insertion prevents leakage and allows absorption. A panty liner may be worn.

options.text: In the morning before walking
At bedtime, then remaining lying down to help the medication stay in place
Right before exercising
While standing

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN measure a liquid medication in a medicine cup?
questions.rationale: Reading the bottom of the meniscus at eye level gives an accurate measurement. Oral syringes are more precise for small doses.

options.text: Hold the cup above eye level
Place the cup on a flat surface and read the bottom of the meniscus at eye level
Read the top of the liquid
Estimate the amount

questions.stem: Which action is correct when the LPN/VN applies nitroglycerin ointment?
questions.rationale: Rubbing alters absorption, and bare-hand contact can give the nurse a headache or hypotension, so gloves are worn. Rotating sites prevents skin irritation.

options.text: Rub the ointment into the skin with bare fingers
Measure the dose on the dosing paper, apply it to a hairless area without rubbing it in, remove the previous dose, and rotate sites
Apply it to the same site every time
Apply it over a hairy area of the chest

questions.stem: Which syringe should the LPN/VN use to administer U-100 insulin?
questions.rationale: Insulin syringes are calibrated in units that match U-100 insulin. Using other syringes increases the risk of dosing errors.

options.text: A 3-mL syringe
A U-100 insulin syringe marked in units
A tuberculin syringe marked in mL
A 10-mL syringe

questions.stem: Which home safety instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce about smoke detectors?
questions.rationale: Working smoke alarms greatly reduce fire deaths. Monthly testing and proper placement are recommended, and carbon monoxide detectors are also important.

options.text: "Test them once a year."
"Test smoke detectors monthly and replace batteries as recommended, and have alarms on every level and near sleeping areas."
"Remove the batteries when cooking."
"One detector is enough for any home."

questions.stem: A client asks how to dispose of unused opioid pain pills at home. What is the best recommendation by the LPN/VN?
questions.rationale: Take-back programs prevent misuse and accidental poisoning. The FDA lists specific medications that may be flushed when take-back options are not available.

options.text: "Keep them in case you need them later."
"Use a drug take-back program or authorized collection site. If none is available, follow the FDA's instructions for your specific medication."
"Give them to a friend in pain."
"Throw them in the trash in the original bottle."

questions.stem: A family member wants to visit a client on contact precautions for MRSA. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Visitors follow facility precautions to protect themselves and other clients. Teaching proper hand hygiene and PPE use is part of infection control.

options.text: Tell the family member visits are not allowed
Teach the family member to perform hand hygiene and wear a gown and gloves as per facility policy
Allow the visit with no precautions
Have the family member wear only a mask

questions.stem: The parent of a 2-year-old says the child wants to eat only macaroni for days at a time. What should the LPN/VN tell the parent?
questions.rationale: Toddlers' growth slows and appetite decreases. They assert independence through food choices. Repeated exposure without pressure supports healthy eating.

options.text: "This is a serious eating disorder."
"Food jags are common in toddlers. Keep offering a variety of healthy foods in small portions without forcing, and use finger foods."
"Force your child to eat vegetables first."
"Give dessert as a reward for eating."

questions.stem: A 4-year-old is afraid of "monsters" at bedtime. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer the parents?
questions.rationale: Preschoolers have vivid imaginations and magical thinking. Routines, reassurance, and a night-light help them feel secure.

options.text: "Tell your child monsters aren't real and turn off all lights."
"Keep a consistent bedtime routine, use a night-light, and acknowledge the fear while reassuring your child they are safe."
"Let your child watch scary movies to get used to it."
"Punish your child for getting out of bed."

questions.stem: A 15-year-old is often tired at school and uses a phone in bed late at night. Which information should the LPN/VN share?
questions.rationale: Adolescents' circadian rhythms shift later, and screen light delays sleep further. Adequate sleep supports learning, mood, and safety.

options.text: "Teens need only about 5 hours of sleep."
"Teens need about 8–10 hours of sleep. Turning off screens an hour before bed can improve sleep."
"Drink energy drinks in the evening."
"Sleep in until noon on school days."

questions.stem: A widowed older adult living alone says, "I haven't talked to anyone in days." Which action by the LPN/VN is most helpful?
questions.rationale: Social isolation increases the risk of depression, cognitive decline, and poor health. Community resources and social engagement promote well-being. The nurse also screens for depression.

options.text: Tell the client to stop complaining
Explore interests and connect the client with resources such as senior centers, faith communities, or phone check-in programs
Suggest moving to a nursing home right away
Ignore the comment

questions.stem: A pregnant client says her prenatal vitamin with iron makes her constipated. What should the LPN/VN suggest?
questions.rationale: Iron and pregnancy hormones slow bowel motility. Dietary measures and activity are first-line. Stool softeners may be recommended by the provider.

options.text: "Stop taking the vitamin."
"Increase fluids and fiber, stay active, and talk with your provider if it continues."
"Take a stimulant laxative daily without asking."
"Take the vitamin with milk."

questions.stem: A pregnant client wakes at night with painful calf cramps. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Dorsiflexion stretches the calf muscle and relieves the cramp. A calf that is red, warm, and swollen could indicate DVT and should not be massaged.

options.text: "Point your toes toward the bed."
"Straighten your leg and gently flex your foot upward (dorsiflex) toward your knee."
"Massage the calf vigorously if it is red and swollen."
"Stop drinking fluids in the evening."

questions.stem: A postpartum client reports painful hemorrhoids. Which comfort measure should the LPN/VN suggest?
questions.rationale: Witch hazel pads, sitz baths, and stool softeners relieve discomfort and prevent straining. Side-lying reduces pressure.

options.text: "Sit on a donut cushion for long periods."
"Use witch hazel pads or prescribed topical products, take sitz baths, and avoid straining with a stool softener as prescribed."
"Apply heat packs directly for hours."
"Limit fluids."

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce about swaddling a newborn?
questions.rationale: Tight leg wrapping increases the risk of hip dysplasia. Swaddled infants must sleep on their backs, and swaddling stops when rolling begins to reduce the risk of suffocation.

options.text: "Wrap the legs straight and tight together."
"Keep the swaddle snug around the chest but loose around the hips so the legs can bend, place the baby on the back, and stop swaddling when the baby starts trying to roll."
"Place a swaddled baby on the stomach to sleep."
"Cover the baby's face with the blanket."

questions.stem: A newborn is going home with mild jaundice. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Frequent feeding promotes bilirubin excretion through stool. Worsening jaundice, lethargy, or poor feeding require evaluation. Water and direct sun exposure are not recommended.

options.text: "Give the baby water between feedings."
"Feed often (8–12 times a day for breastfed babies), watch the number of wet and dirty diapers, and call if the yellow color spreads or the baby is very sleepy or feeding poorly."
"Place the baby in direct sunlight for hours."
"Jaundice never needs follow-up."

questions.stem: A client feels overwhelmed by anxiety. Which grounding technique can the LPN/VN coach?
questions.rationale: Grounding focuses attention on present sensory experiences, which reduces anxiety and dissociation. Slow breathing can also help.

options.text: Encourage the client to think about worst-case outcomes
The 5-4-3-2-1 technique: name 5 things you see, 4 you can touch, 3 you hear, 2 you smell, and 1 you taste
Ask the client to hold their breath as long as possible
Tell the client to ignore the feeling

questions.stem: A resident with advanced dementia repeatedly asks for her husband, who died several years ago. Which response by the LPN/VN is most appropriate?
questions.rationale: Repeatedly reorienting to a painful fact can cause renewed grief. Validating emotions and redirecting provide comfort and preserve dignity.

options.text: "Your husband died years ago. You know that."
"You're thinking about your husband. Tell me about him." Then gently redirect to a comforting activity.
"He'll be here soon," and walk away
Ignore the question

questions.stem: For each finding in a 2-month-old, indicate whether it is normal or a sign of respiratory distress to report.
questions.rationale: Infants normally breathe with the diaphragm at about 30–60 breaths/min and may have short pauses. Flaring, grunting, and retractions indicate increased work of breathing.
questions.answer_summary: Normal: brief periodic breathing, abdominal breathing, RR 45. Distress: nasal flaring, grunting, retractions.

rows.text: Periodic breathing with pauses under 10 seconds

questions.stem: An older resident suddenly reports severe pain in the right eye, blurred vision with rainbow halos around lights, headache, and nausea. The right eye is red, and the pupil is mid-dilated. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the resident is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Sudden eye pain, halos, a red eye, and a mid-dilated pupil with nausea suggest acute angle-closure glaucoma, which can cause blindness within hours without treatment. Anticholinergics and dark environments dilate the pupil and can worsen the angle closure.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: acute angle-closure glaucoma. Actions: notify the RN immediately; hold anticholinergic PRN medications. Monitor: eye pain and vision; nausea and vomiting.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Notify the RN immediately for urgent eye evaluation
Hold any PRN anticholinergic medications such as diphenhydramine until the provider is consulted
Patch the eye and recheck tomorrow
Encourage the resident to sit in a dark room for hours

questions.stem: Where should the LPN/VN place AED pads on an adult?
questions.rationale: This anterolateral placement allows current to pass through the heart. The chest is exposed and dried, pads are placed away from implanted devices, and no one touches the client during analysis and shock.

options.text: Both pads on the left side of the chest
One pad below the right collarbone and one on the left side of the chest below the armpit
One pad on the abdomen and one on the back of the neck
Over clothing

questions.stem: A person is unresponsive but breathing normally, with no suspected spinal injury. How should the LPN/VN position the person while waiting for EMS?
questions.rationale: The recovery position keeps the airway open and allows fluids to drain from the mouth. The nurse continues to monitor breathing.

options.text: Supine with the head flat
In the recovery (side-lying) position
Prone
Sitting upright against a wall

questions.stem: A young adult has painful leg muscle cramps after working outdoors in the heat but is alert, with a normal temperature. What should the LPN/VN recommend?
questions.rationale: Heat cramps result from fluid and electrolyte loss. Rest, cooling, stretching, and electrolyte replacement relieve them. Worsening symptoms may indicate heat exhaustion.

options.text: "Keep working to walk it off."
"Rest in a cool place, gently stretch the muscles, and drink fluids containing electrolytes."
"Apply heat packs."
"Take salt tablets with no water."

questions.stem: A hiker is brought into a lodge shivering and confused after falling into a cold stream. What should the LPN/VN do first?
questions.rationale: Removing wet clothing stops ongoing heat loss. Gradual rewarming of the core is preferred. Rubbing and alcohol are harmful, and rapid immersion can cause dangerous circulatory changes.

options.text: Rub the arms and legs vigorously
Remove wet clothing, cover the person with dry blankets, and warm the core, while calling for emergency help
Give alcohol to warm the body
Place the person in a hot bath immediately

questions.stem: A resident is stung by a bee and has no signs of allergic reaction. The stinger is visible in the skin. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Prompt removal limits venom delivery, and squeezing can inject more venom. The nurse watches for signs of anaphylaxis.

options.text: Squeeze the stinger out with the fingers
Scrape the stinger out with a flat edge, wash the area, and apply a cold pack
Leave the stinger in
Apply heat

questions.stem: A child is bitten on the hand by a neighbor's dog. What should the LPN/VN advise first?
questions.rationale: Thorough washing reduces infection and rabies risk. Evaluation determines the need for antibiotics, tetanus prophylaxis, and rabies prophylaxis. Hand bites are at high risk for infection.

options.text: "Cover it and ignore it."
"Wash the wound thoroughly with soap and running water for several minutes, then seek medical evaluation. The bite may need to be reported."
"Apply butter to the bite."
"Close the wound tightly with tape."

questions.stem: A 12-year-old's permanent front tooth is knocked out during a game. What should the LPN/VN advise?
questions.rationale: Touching or scrubbing the root damages the cells needed for reattachment. Keeping the tooth moist in milk or saliva and getting dental care within about an hour improves the chance of saving it. Baby teeth are not reimplanted.

options.text: "Scrub the root clean and wrap the tooth in a dry tissue."
"Hold the tooth by the crown, rinse gently if dirty, and reinsert it if possible, or store it in milk and see a dentist immediately."
"Throw the tooth away."
"Wait a few days to see a dentist."

questions.stem: How often should adults receive a tetanus-diphtheria (Td or Tdap) booster?
questions.rationale: Routine boosters are recommended every 10 years. For dirty or contaminated wounds, a booster is given if more than 5 years have passed since the last dose.

options.text: Every year
Every 10 years, with an earlier dose for certain wounds if more than 5 years have passed
Only once in a lifetime
Every 2 years

questions.stem: Which client meets USPSTF criteria for annual lung cancer screening with low-dose CT?
questions.rationale: USPSTF recommends annual screening for adults aged 50–80 with a 20 pack-year or greater history who currently smoke or quit within the past 15 years.

options.text: A 35-year-old who has never smoked
A 62-year-old with a 25 pack-year history who quit smoking 8 years ago
A 45-year-old with a 5 pack-year history
An 85-year-old who quit 30 years ago

questions.stem: At what age does the USPSTF recommend osteoporosis screening with a bone density test for women without extra risk factors?
questions.rationale: Screening is recommended for all women 65 and older, and for younger postmenopausal women at increased risk.

options.text: Age 40
Age 65
Age 80
Only after a fracture

questions.stem: The daughter of an older adult reports new dents on her father's car and that he got lost driving to a familiar store. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Getting lost and minor crashes may indicate cognitive or visual decline. Evaluation and planning help protect safety while respecting the client's dignity.

options.text: Tell the family this is normal aging
Report the concerns to the RN or provider for evaluation of driving safety and cognition, and discuss transportation alternatives
Take the car keys without discussion
Suggest he drive only at night

questions.stem: A parent notices a flat spot on the back of the 3-month-old's head. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Back-sleeping is still required to reduce SIDS risk. Awake tummy time and position changes relieve pressure on the back of the head. Positioners and prolonged car seat time are unsafe or worsen flattening.

options.text: "Place your baby on the stomach to sleep."
"Give supervised tummy time while your baby is awake, and alternate the direction your baby's head faces in the crib."
"Use a positioning pillow in the crib."
"Keep your baby in the car seat for naps."

questions.stem: A 3-year-old has a temperature of 101.5°F (38.6°C) but is drinking well and playful. What should the LPN/VN advise the parent?
questions.rationale: Treating fever is for comfort. Alcohol rubs and cold baths can cause shivering and toxicity, aspirin risks Reye's syndrome, and bundling traps heat. Parents should call for concerning signs such as lethargy or dehydration.

options.text: "Give a cold alcohol rub."
"Fever itself isn't harmful. You can give weight-based acetaminophen or ibuprofen for comfort, offer fluids, and dress your child lightly."
"Give aspirin."
"Wrap your child in blankets."

questions.stem: Which approach is most likely to help a 2-year-old take an oral medication?
questions.rationale: Toddlers seek autonomy. Limited choices increase cooperation, and praise reinforces it. Calling medicine candy risks accidental ingestion, and mixing it in large volumes risks an incomplete dose.

options.text: "Tell the child it's candy."
"Offer a simple choice, such as the cup or the syringe, then give praise afterward."
"Mix it into a full bottle of milk."
"Pinch the child's nose to force the mouth open."

questions.stem: A 16-year-old says, "Vaping is safe because it's just water vapor." Which response by the LPN/VN is most accurate?
questions.rationale: E-cigarette aerosol is not just water vapor. Nicotine affects adolescent attention and learning, and vaping has been linked to lung injury.

options.text: "You're right, it's harmless."
"Most vapes contain nicotine, which is highly addictive and affects the developing brain, and the aerosol contains harmful chemicals that can injure the lungs."
"Vaping helps teens focus."
"Only cigarettes contain nicotine."

questions.stem: A pregnant client has a cat. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Toxoplasma can be transmitted through cat feces and can cause serious fetal harm. Avoiding undercooked meat and washing produce also reduce risk.

options.text: "Get rid of the cat immediately."
"Have someone else change the litter box if possible. If you must do it, wear gloves, change it daily, and wash your hands well."
"Change the litter box weekly without gloves."
"Let the cat sleep on your pillow."

questions.stem: A client gave birth vaginally 6 hours ago and has not voided. The fundus is above the umbilicus and deviated to the right. What should the LPN/VN do first?
questions.rationale: A full bladder displaces the uterus and prevents contraction, increasing the risk of hemorrhage. Helping the client void (or catheterizing if prescribed) is the priority. The fundus is then reassessed.

options.text: Massage the fundus vigorously and document
Assist the client to the bathroom to void and report the findings to the RN
Restrict fluids
Wait until the next shift

questions.stem: The LPN/VN needs to clear a newborn's airway with a bulb syringe. Which technique is correct?
questions.rationale: Suctioning the mouth first prevents aspiration if the newborn gasps when the nose is stimulated. The bulb is compressed before insertion so secretions aren't pushed farther in.

options.text: Suction the nose first, then the mouth
Compress the bulb before insertion, and suction the mouth first, then the nose
Insert the bulb deep into the throat
Compress the bulb after insertion into the nostril

questions.stem: A client with depression and past suicidal thoughts is being discharged with a safety plan. Which element should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Safety plans identify triggers, coping skills, supports, professional contacts, and crisis resources such as the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. Reducing access to lethal means lowers risk.

options.text: "Keep all your medications in one large bottle at your bedside."
"Know your warning signs, use your coping strategies, reach out to supportive contacts, remove access to lethal means, and call or text 988 in a crisis."
"Only call your provider during office hours."
"Avoid telling your family."

questions.stem: A client with severe depression stays in bed all day. Which approach by the LPN/VN is most helpful?
questions.rationale: Small, attainable goals build a sense of accomplishment and gradually increase activity. Overwhelming expectations can worsen feelings of failure.

options.text: Insist the client join every unit activity immediately
Help the client set a small, achievable goal, such as showering or walking to the day room, and give positive feedback
Allow the client to stay in bed indefinitely
Tell the client to cheer up

questions.stem: Which technique should the LPN/VN use to irrigate a wound?
questions.rationale: Safe irrigation pressure (about 4–15 psi) removes debris without damaging tissue. Room- or body-temperature solution and cleaning from clean to dirty reduce contamination.

options.text: Use a bulb syringe with forceful pressure directly into the wound bed
Use a 35-mL syringe with a 19-gauge angiocatheter (or per policy) to deliver gentle, steady pressure, from the cleanest to the dirtiest area
Pour irrigant from a height of several feet
Irrigate with cold tap water

questions.stem: A client with cold hands and Raynaud's phenomenon has a pulse oximetry reading that won't register on the finger. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Poor peripheral perfusion causes unreliable readings. Alternate sites and confirming that the oximeter's pulse matches the client's heart rate improve accuracy.

options.text: Document a reading of 0%
Warm the hand or use an alternate site, such as an earlobe or forehead sensor, and compare the pulse reading with the actual heart rate
Squeeze the finger tightly
Assume the client is hypoxic and start oxygen at 15 L/min

questions.stem: For each milestone, indicate the age at which it is typically first achieved.
questions.rationale: Development follows predictable patterns from head to toe and from simple to complex. Missing milestones warrants developmental screening.
questions.answer_summary: 2 months: social smile, lifts head prone. 6 months: transfers objects, rolls both ways. 12 months: meaningful mama/dada, cruising.

rows.text: Lifts head when lying on the stomach
Transfers objects from hand to hand
Rolls from front to back and back to front

questions.stem: A breastfeeding mother is prescribed a new medication and asks whether it is safe for her baby. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Many medications are compatible with breastfeeding. Resources such as LactMed guide decisions, and stopping breastfeeding unnecessarily can harm both mother and baby.

options.text: Tell her to stop breastfeeding while taking any medication
Encourage her to confirm with the provider or pharmacist, who can check lactation safety resources, and to watch the baby for changes in feeding or sleep
Tell her all medications are safe
Suggest she pump and discard milk forever

questions.stem: In the facility parking lot, a worker is cut on the thigh by broken glass. Bright red blood is spurting from the wound. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the worker is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Spurting bright red blood indicates arterial bleeding, which can be fatal within minutes. Direct pressure, wound packing, or a tourniquet (with the time noted) are the steps taught in Stop the Bleed training. Removing dressings disrupts clot formation.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: life-threatening arterial bleeding. Actions: firm direct pressure, adding a tourniquet if needed; call 911 and get help. Monitor: bleeding control; signs of shock.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Apply firm, direct pressure with a clean cloth, and use a tourniquet 2–3 inches above the wound if bleeding is not controlled
Call 911 and send someone for help and a bleeding control kit
Remove the dressing repeatedly to check the wound
Have the worker walk to the emergency department

bowtie_groups.label: Parameters to monitor (choose 2)
options: Signs of shock such as pale, cool skin, rapid pulse, and confusion

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce to prevent window falls in young children?
questions.rationale: Screens keep insects out but do not stop falls. Window stops, guards, and moving climbable furniture prevent serious injuries.

options.text: "Window screens will keep children from falling."
"Install window guards or stops that limit openings to 4 inches, and keep furniture away from windows."
"Open windows from the bottom only."
"Let children play on window sills if you are in the house."

questions.topic: Infant crying and abusive head trauma
questions.stem: A tired parent says the 6-week-old cries for hours every evening. Which guidance should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Peak crying commonly occurs around 6–8 weeks. Teaching coping strategies and never shaking a baby helps prevent abusive head trauma.

options.text: "Shake the baby gently to calm them."
"Check basic needs, try swaddling, rocking, or shushing, and if you feel overwhelmed, place the baby safely in the crib and step away for a few minutes. Never shake a baby."
"Give honey to soothe the baby."
"Crying means the baby is sick."

questions.stem: How much calcium is recommended daily for most adolescents aged 9–18?
questions.rationale: Adolescence is a key period for building peak bone mass. Many teens do not meet calcium and vitamin D recommendations.

options.text: About 500 mg
About 1,300 mg
About 3,000 mg
Calcium isn't needed during adolescence

questions.stem: An adult asks how much exercise is recommended. Which response by the LPN/VN is correct?
questions.rationale: U.S. guidelines recommend at least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity weekly, or 75 minutes of vigorous activity, plus strength training.

options.text: "10 minutes a week is enough."
"At least 150 minutes of moderate activity per week, plus muscle-strengthening activities on 2 or more days."
"Only high-intensity exercise counts."
"Exercise daily until exhausted."

questions.stem: A married couple in a long-term care facility requests private time together. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Older adults have the right to intimacy and privacy. Nurses provide a respectful environment while considering capacity to consent.

options.text: Tell them it isn't allowed at their age
Respect their request, arrange privacy, and support their right to intimacy
Ask other residents' opinions
Report the request to their children

questions.stem: A resident with dysphagia is prescribed mildly thick liquids. Which action by the LPN/VN is correct?
questions.rationale: Thin liquids increase aspiration risk. All liquids must match the speech-language pathologist's recommendation, often described using the IDDSI framework.

options.text: Offer thin water between meals
Prepare all liquids, including water and supplements, to the prescribed consistency, and keep the resident upright while drinking
Add thickener only to milk
Let the resident choose the consistency each time

questions.stem: A client who takes insulin asks about drinking alcohol at a party. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Alcohol blocks the liver's release of glucose, which can cause hypoglycemia hours later. Hypoglycemia can also be mistaken for intoxication.

options.text: "Alcohol raises your blood sugar, so skip your insulin."
"Drink only in moderation, never on an empty stomach, and check your glucose because alcohol can cause delayed low blood sugar, even overnight."
"Drink as much as you like."
"Alcohol has no effect on diabetes."

questions.stem: A client receives continuous tube feedings and oral phenytoin suspension through the tube. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Enteral formulas bind phenytoin and lower blood levels. Holding feedings around the dose, flushing, and monitoring levels maintain therapeutic effect.

options.text: Mix the phenytoin into the feeding bag
Follow the prescribed protocol, which often includes holding the feeding before and after the dose and flushing the tube, because feedings can reduce phenytoin absorption
Give the phenytoin without flushing
Double the dose

questions.stem: A client is going home after a cystoscopy. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Mild hematuria and dysuria are expected. Fluids flush the bladder. Fever, clots, or retention suggest infection, bleeding, or obstruction.

options.text: "Limit fluids for 24 hours."
"Pink urine and mild burning are common for a day or two. Drink extra fluids, and call if you have a fever, clots, or can't urinate."
"Report any pink urine immediately."
"Avoid urinating for 8 hours."

questions.stem: A client has an acutely painful, swollen big toe from gout. Which comfort measure should the LPN/VN use?
questions.rationale: Inflamed gouty joints are extremely sensitive. Rest, cold, elevation, and avoiding pressure relieve pain alongside prescribed medications.

options.text: Apply heat and encourage walking
Rest and elevate the foot, apply ice, and use a bed cradle to keep linens off the toe
Massage the joint
Wrap the toe tightly

questions.stem: A client with right-sided weakness after a stroke is learning to put on a shirt. What should the LPN/VN teach?
questions.rationale: Dressing the affected limb first and undressing it last makes the task easier. Adaptive clothing and encouraging independence support recovery.

options.text: "Dress the left (strong) arm first."
"Dress the right (weak) arm first, and undress the left (strong) arm first."
"Only wear clothing with small buttons."
"Have staff dress you completely."

questions.stem: When repositioning a bedbound client onto the side, which position reduces pressure over the trochanter and sacrum?
questions.rationale: A 30-degree tilt avoids direct pressure on the hip bone and sacrum, lowering pressure injury risk compared with full side-lying.

options.text: A 90-degree side-lying position
A 30-degree lateral tilt supported with pillows
Prone
Semi-Fowler's with knees straight

questions.stem: Which joint protection strategy should the LPN/VN reinforce for a client with rheumatoid arthritis?
questions.rationale: Distributing load to stronger, larger joints and using adaptive equipment reduce stress on inflamed small joints and help prevent deformity.

options.text: "Carry heavy bags with your fingers."
"Use larger joints for tasks, such as carrying a bag on your forearm, and use assistive devices like jar openers."
"Avoid all activity."
"Grip objects tightly for long periods."

questions.stem: A resident with Alzheimer's disease becomes more confused and agitated in the late afternoon. Which intervention should the LPN/VN include?
questions.rationale: Sundowning is worsened by fatigue, shadows, and disrupted routines. Environmental and routine adjustments reduce symptoms.

options.text: Dim all lights in the afternoon
Increase lighting in the late afternoon, keep a predictable routine, limit caffeine and daytime napping, and offer calm activities
Schedule baths and appointments for early evening
Apply restraints

questions.stem: A client who just received bad news is sitting alone and crying. Which response by the LPN/VN demonstrates the technique of offering self?
questions.rationale: Offering self communicates availability and support without placing demands on the client.

options.text: "Why are you crying?"
"I'll sit with you for a while."
"Everything will be okay."
"You need to be strong."

questions.stem: A client at 20 weeks' gestation reports sharp, brief pain on the side of the lower abdomen when she stands up quickly. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Stretching of the round ligaments causes brief, sharp pain with movement. Pain that is persistent or accompanied by bleeding, fever, or contractions should be reported.

options.text: "Go to the emergency department right away."
"This is likely round ligament pain. Change positions slowly and bend your hips toward your belly when the pain occurs."
"Take aspirin for the pain."
"Stay in bed for the rest of your pregnancy."

questions.stem: A client in the third trimester reports frequent heartburn. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Progesterone relaxes the lower esophageal sphincter, and the growing uterus pushes up on the stomach. Sodium bicarbonate can cause fluid retention and alkalosis, so antacids should be approved by the provider.

options.text: "Lie down right after eating."
"Eat small, frequent meals, avoid spicy and fatty foods, and stay upright for a while after eating."
"Drink large amounts of fluid with meals."
"Take baking soda for relief."

questions.stem: A breastfeeding client on day 3 reports sore nipples. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer first?
questions.rationale: A shallow latch is the most common cause of sore nipples. Soap dries the skin, and limiting feedings reduces milk supply.

options.text: "Stop breastfeeding for a week."
"Check that the baby is latching deeply, vary nursing positions, apply a little expressed breast milk to the nipples, and let them air dry."
"Wash your nipples with soap before each feeding."
"Limit feedings to 5 minutes."

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce for parents of an uncircumcised newborn boy?
questions.rationale: The foreskin is naturally attached in infancy and separates over years. Forcible retraction causes pain, bleeding, and scarring.

options.text: "Pull back the foreskin daily to clean underneath."
"Clean the outside of the penis with water during baths, and do not force the foreskin back."
"Use cotton swabs under the foreskin."
"Apply powder under the foreskin."

questions.stem: Which technique is correct for removing contaminated gloves?
questions.rationale: The "glove-to-glove, skin-to-skin" technique prevents touching contaminated surfaces with bare hands. Hand hygiene follows.

options.text: Pull both gloves off by the fingertips at once
Grasp the outside of one glove at the wrist and peel it off, hold it in the gloved hand, then slide a bare finger inside the other glove to peel it off over the first
Remove gloves with your teeth
Wash gloved hands and reuse the gloves

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN move a client in a wheelchair down a steep ramp?
questions.rationale: Backing down keeps the client from pitching forward out of the chair and gives the nurse better control.

options.text: Go down forward, letting the chair roll
Go down backward, walking behind the chair while looking over the shoulder
Push the chair down quickly
Remove the client from the chair

questions.stem: An 86-year-old is starting an opioid for fracture pain. Which approach should the LPN/VN expect?
questions.rationale: Older adults are more sensitive to opioids because of reduced clearance. Untreated pain also causes harm, including delirium and immobility, so careful dosing and monitoring are needed.

options.text: Start with the highest dose
Start with a low dose, increase slowly, and monitor closely for sedation, confusion, constipation, and falls
Avoid all pain treatment
Give opioids only when pain is 10/10

questions.stem: A client with a severe penicillin allergy and diabetes asks whether a medical alert bracelet is needed. What should the LPN/VN say?
questions.rationale: Medical ID informs care in emergencies, such as unexplained unconsciousness from hypoglycemia, and helps prevent exposure to allergens.

options.text: "It's unnecessary."
"Yes. A medical alert ID gives emergency responders critical information if you can't speak for yourself."
"Only if you are over 65."
"Just tell your friends."

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate whether it is more typical of a right-hemisphere or left-hemisphere stroke.
questions.rationale: Understanding hemisphere-specific deficits guides safety planning. Clients with right-hemisphere strokes need close supervision because of impulsivity and poor judgment. Clients with left-hemisphere strokes need communication support.
questions.answer_summary: Right hemisphere: left neglect, impulsivity, spatial-perceptual deficits. Left hemisphere: aphasia, right-sided weakness, slow and cautious behavior.

rows.text: Neglect of the left side of the body
Impulsive behavior and poor safety awareness
Difficulty judging distances and spatial relationships

questions.stem: At a summer camp, a 14-year-old with type 1 diabetes has been vomiting for several hours. The camper has deep, rapid breathing, fruity breath, and is drowsy. A fingerstick glucose reads 486 mg/dL, and urine ketones are large. The camper admits skipping insulin doses. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the camper is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Hyperglycemia with ketones, vomiting, Kussmaul respirations, fruity breath, and drowsiness indicate DKA, which requires hospital treatment. Exercise can worsen ketosis, and vomiting with ketones means the camper cannot safely manage at camp. Insulin should never simply be withheld.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: diabetic ketoacidosis. Actions: call emergency services; notify the health supervisor and parents and follow the diabetes plan. Monitor: LOC; breathing pattern and dehydration.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Call emergency services for transport to the hospital
Notify the camp's health supervisor and the camper's parents, and follow the diabetes emergency plan
Give extra food to settle the stomach
Have the camper exercise to lower glucose

bowtie_groups.label: Parameters to monitor (choose 2)
options: Breathing pattern and signs of dehydration

questions.stem: Which language milestone does the LPN/VN expect in a typically developing 2-year-old?
questions.rationale: By age 2, most children use about 50 or more words and two-word phrases. Absence of words or phrases warrants developmental evaluation.

options.text: Speaking in full paragraphs
Using two-word phrases such as "more milk"
Using no words at all
Reading simple books

questions.stem: Which toy is most appropriate for a 4-year-old hospitalized for several days?
questions.rationale: Preschoolers engage in imaginative, cooperative play. Pretend play also helps them work through hospital fears.

options.text: A rattle
Dress-up clothes and puppets for pretend play
A complex video game for teens
A 1,000-piece puzzle

questions.stem: Which vaccine does the LPN/VN expect a healthy 16-year-old to receive if on schedule?
questions.rationale: MenACWY is given at 11–12 years with a booster at 16. Rotavirus is for infants, and DTaP and hepatitis B series begin in infancy.

options.text: Rotavirus
A meningococcal conjugate (MenACWY) booster
The first dose of DTaP
The first dose of hepatitis B

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce to prevent scald burns in toddlers?
questions.rationale: Toddlers can grab handles and pull tablecloths, spilling hot liquids. Keeping hot items out of reach prevents scalds.

options.text: "Let your toddler help stir hot soup."
"Turn pot handles toward the back of the stove, use back burners, and keep hot drinks away from table edges."
"Hold your toddler while drinking hot coffee."
"Use tablecloths that hang over the edge."

questions.stem: An older adult says food "tastes bland" and is eating less. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Taste and smell decline with age and with some medications. Herbs and spices enhance flavor without excess sodium. Oral problems and medications should also be reviewed.

options.text: "Add extra salt to everything."
"Try herbs, spices, lemon, and a variety of textures and colors to make food more appealing."
"Skip meals if food isn't enjoyable."
"Eat only sweets."

questions.stem: A resident at high risk for falls and with osteoporosis is prescribed hip protectors. Which statement by the LPN/VN explains their purpose?
questions.rationale: Hip protectors absorb and redirect impact. They do not prevent falls, so other fall prevention measures continue.

options.text: "They keep you from falling."
"They are padded garments that reduce the risk of hip fracture if you fall."
"They are worn only at night."
"They replace the need for fall precautions."

questions.stem: Which peripheral IV site should the LPN/VN (if within scope) or RN generally select first for a client needing several days of IV therapy?
questions.rationale: Starting distally preserves proximal veins for future use. Forearm sites avoid joint flexion, and the nondominant arm maintains function. Fistula arms and leg veins in adults are avoided.

options.text: The antecubital fossa of the dominant arm
A distal vein on the forearm of the nondominant arm, avoiding areas of joint flexion
A vein in the leg
A vein on the arm with an AV fistula

questions.stem: How often should primary continuous IV administration tubing not used for blood, lipids, or parenteral nutrition generally be changed?
questions.rationale: CDC and INS guidance supports changing primary continuous tubing no more often than every 96 hours. Tubing for blood, lipids, and PN is changed more frequently.

options.text: Every 8 hours
No more often than every 96 hours but at least every 7 days, per facility policy
Every shift
Never

questions.stem: A client is receiving oxygen at 5 L/min by nasal cannula and reports a dry nose and throat. What should the LPN/VN consider?
questions.rationale: Humidification is often used at higher flow rates to reduce drying of the mucous membranes. Petroleum products are flammable with oxygen.

options.text: Turning off the oxygen
Asking the RN about adding humidification per policy, and applying a water-soluble lubricant to the nares
Using petroleum jelly in the nostrils
Increasing the flow to 10 L/min

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is removing interrupted sutures. Which technique is correct?
questions.rationale: Removing alternate sutures first allows the nurse to check wound integrity. The suture is cut close to the skin and pulled out so the exposed portion doesn't pass through tissue. Adhesive strips are applied as ordered.

options.text: Pull the knot through the tissue
Remove every other suture first, check that the wound edges stay together, then remove the rest
Remove all sutures quickly without checking the wound
Cut the suture on both sides of the knot

questions.stem: Where should the LPN/VN perform chest percussion during chest physiotherapy?
questions.rationale: Cupped-hand percussion over the rib cage loosens secretions. The spine, kidneys, and other sensitive areas are avoided, and a thin layer of cloth protects the skin.

options.text: Over the spine and kidneys
Over the rib cage of the lung segment being drained, avoiding the spine, sternum, breasts, and kidneys
Directly over the stomach
Over bare skin with an open palm slap

questions.stem: The LPN/VN presses on a client's fingernail bed and releases it. Color returns in 5 seconds. How should this be interpreted?
questions.rationale: Normal capillary refill is generally under 2–3 seconds. Delayed refill can indicate dehydration, shock, or peripheral vascular problems. Cold temperature can also slow refill.

options.text: Normal
Delayed capillary refill, which may indicate poor perfusion and should be reported
A sign of fluid overload
A sign of hypertension

questions.stem: A client with a colostomy created 3 weeks ago asks why the pouch opening needs to be measured again. What should the LPN/VN explain?
questions.rationale: Postoperative edema resolves over several weeks. A properly fitted opening prevents leakage and skin irritation.

options.text: "Stomas never change size."
"The stoma shrinks as swelling goes down over the first 6–8 weeks, so the opening needs re-measuring to fit well and protect your skin."
"You only need to measure once a year."
"Larger openings are always better."

questions.stem: During a cleansing enema, the client reports strong cramping. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Cramping often means the fluid is flowing too fast. Lowering the bag slows the flow, and slow breathing helps the client relax.

options.text: Increase the flow rate to finish quickly
Lower the bag or clamp the tubing briefly, have the client take slow deep breaths, then resume slowly
Remove the tube and stop permanently
Raise the bag higher

questions.stem: The LPN/VN needs to measure an infant's urine output. The wet diaper weighs 42 g, and the same type of dry diaper weighs 15 g. What is the urine output?
questions.rationale: Each gram of weight gained by the diaper equals about 1 mL of urine: 42 − 15 = 27 mL.

options.text: 15 mL
27 mL
42 mL
57 mL

questions.stem: After a client has a seizure, which information is most important for the LPN/VN to document?
questions.rationale: Detailed observations help the provider classify the seizure type and guide treatment.

options.text: The client's favorite food
When it began, how long it lasted, body parts involved and movements, level of consciousness, and the client's condition afterward
Only that a seizure occurred
The names of visitors present

questions.topic: Temperature regulation in spinal cord injury
questions.stem: A client with a high spinal cord injury is going outdoors on a hot day. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Loss of sympathetic control below the injury impairs sweating and vasoconstriction, increasing the risk of hyperthermia and hypothermia.

options.text: "Your body will sweat normally to cool down."
"Your body may not regulate temperature well, so avoid extreme heat, dress appropriately, and stay hydrated."
"Stay in the sun as long as you like."
"Heat doesn't affect people with spinal cord injuries."

questions.topic: Skin folds in clients with obesity
questions.stem: Which intervention should the LPN/VN use to protect the skin folds of a client with obesity?
questions.rationale: Moisture and friction in skin folds lead to irritation and fungal infections. Keeping folds clean and dry, with moisture-wicking fabric, protects the skin.

options.text: Apply heavy powder in all folds
Cleanse and dry the folds thoroughly and use moisture-wicking textiles between skin folds as available
Leave the folds moist to prevent dryness
Use tight bandages in the folds

questions.stem: A client in recovery from alcohol use disorder is preparing for discharge. Which strategy should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Relapse prevention includes recognizing high-risk situations, developing coping skills, and maintaining supports such as mutual-help groups and counseling.

options.text: "Go back to your usual bar to show you're strong."
"Identify your triggers, such as certain people, places, and emotions, plan how to cope, and stay connected to a support group."
"Keep alcohol at home just in case."
"Avoid telling anyone about your recovery."

questions.stem: A resident whose wife died 4 months ago says he still feels sad on some days but is eating, sleeping, and attending activities. How should the LPN/VN interpret this?
questions.rationale: Grief comes in waves and can last a year or longer while daily function continues. Persistent inability to function or suicidal thoughts would require evaluation.

options.text: As major depression that needs immediate medication
As a normal grief response. The nurse continues to offer support and watches for signs of complicated grief or depression.
As a sign he didn't love his wife
As a reason to restrict his activities

questions.stem: A client in her first trimester asks whether she can use the hot tub at her gym. What should the LPN/VN advise?
questions.rationale: Maternal hyperthermia in early pregnancy is associated with neural tube defects. Warm (not hot) baths are acceptable.

options.text: "Hot tubs are completely safe."
"Avoid hot tubs and saunas, especially in the first trimester, because raising your core temperature can harm the developing baby."
"Use it only once a day."
"Hot tubs help prevent morning sickness."

questions.stem: A client asks when she can resume intercourse after a vaginal birth with a small tear. Which response by the LPN/VN is appropriate?
questions.rationale: Healing and comfort guide timing. Ovulation can occur before the first period, so contraception planning is important.

options.text: "Tonight is fine."
"Many providers suggest waiting until the tear has healed and bleeding has stopped, often around 4–6 weeks. You can get pregnant before your period returns, so discuss contraception."
"You must wait 1 year."
"Breastfeeding prevents pregnancy, so no contraception is needed."

questions.stem: A parent notices that when the newborn is startled, the baby throws the arms out and then brings them back in. What should the LPN/VN explain?
questions.rationale: A symmetric Moro reflex is normal. An asymmetric response may indicate a fracture (such as a clavicle) or nerve injury. Persistence beyond about 6 months warrants evaluation.

options.text: "This is a seizure."
"This is the Moro (startle) reflex, which is normal in newborns and usually disappears by about 4–6 months."
"This means your baby is cold."
"This is a sign of hearing loss."

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate whether it is subjective or objective data.
questions.rationale: Subjective data are the client's reported feelings and perceptions. Objective data are observed or measured by the nurse. Both are documented accurately.
questions.answer_summary: Subjective: dizziness, nausea, pain rating (what the client reports). Objective: BP, vomitus, grimacing (what the nurse observes or measures).

questions.stem: A resident with a history of hypertension reports a sudden severe headache and blurred vision. The LPN/VN measures BP 212/124 mm Hg (confirmed on recheck) and notes the resident is newly confused. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the resident is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Severely elevated BP with neurological symptoms indicates target-organ damage and requires controlled BP reduction in an acute care setting. Doubling medication without an order can cause a dangerous drop in BP, and caffeine raises BP.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: hypertensive emergency. Actions: notify the RN and provider immediately; keep the resident at rest with HOB elevated and stay. Monitor: BP; neurological status.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Notify the RN and provider immediately and prepare for emergency transfer
Keep the resident at rest with the head of the bed elevated and stay with the resident
Give a double dose of the resident's usual antihypertensive without an order
Have the resident walk to relieve the headache
Offer a cup of strong coffee

questions.stem: A parent asks when a formula-fed infant can switch to whole cow's milk. Which response by the LPN/VN is correct?
questions.rationale: Cow's milk before 12 months can cause iron deficiency and does not meet infant nutritional needs. Whole milk is recommended from 12 to 24 months unless otherwise advised.

options.text: "At 4 months."
"At about 12 months. Until then, use iron-fortified formula."
"As soon as the baby starts solid foods."
"At 2 years."

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce about bicycle helmets for a school-age child?
questions.rationale: Properly fitted helmets greatly reduce the risk of head injury. The helmet sits about two fingerbreadths above the eyebrows, and the chin strap is snug.

options.text: "Helmets are only needed on busy streets."
"Wear a properly fitted helmet every ride. It should sit level on the forehead and be buckled snugly."
"A helmet can be worn tilted back on the head."
"Older children don't need helmets."

questions.stem: A 16-year-old asks the LPN/VN whether their parents will be told about STI testing. Which response is most appropriate?
questions.rationale: Most states allow minors to consent to STI services. Explaining confidentiality, and its limits such as safety concerns, encourages teens to seek care.

options.text: "Your parents must be told everything."
"In most states, teens can consent to STI testing and treatment confidentially. Let me connect you with the provider to discuss what stays private."
"I can't talk to you without your parents."
"You're too young to be tested."

questions.stem: A 70-year-old asks which flu vaccine is best. Which response by the LPN/VN reflects current CDC preference?
questions.rationale: Older adults have weaker immune responses, and these enhanced vaccines provide better protection. The nasal spray is not recommended for adults 50 and older.

options.text: "Only the nasal spray vaccine."
"For adults 65 and older, a high-dose, adjuvanted, or recombinant flu vaccine is preferred when available."
"Older adults don't need flu vaccines."
"Get the vaccine every 5 years."

questions.stem: A client weighs 70 kg and is 1.75 m tall. What is the client's BMI, and how is it classified?
questions.rationale: BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height (m)². 1.75 × 1.75 = 3.06, and 70 ÷ 3.06 ≈ 22.9. A normal BMI is 18.5–24.9.

options.text: 18.0, underweight
22.9, normal weight
28.5, overweight
31.2, obese

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN help position an adult for a lumbar puncture?
questions.rationale: Flexing the spine widens the spaces between the lumbar vertebrae, which allows needle insertion.

options.text: Prone with arms overhead
Side-lying with the knees drawn up to the chest and the chin tucked (fetal position), or sitting and leaning forward
Supine with legs straight
Trendelenburg

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is preparing a client for a pelvic examination. Which position is used?
questions.rationale: Lithotomy position gives access to the perineum. The nurse provides draping for privacy and helps the client move both legs together to prevent strain.

options.text: Prone
Lithotomy: supine with the hips and knees flexed and the feet in stirrups
Left Sims'
High-Fowler's

questions.stem: Which technique is correct when the LPN/VN collects a throat culture?
questions.rationale: Touching other mouth structures contaminates the specimen with normal flora. A tongue depressor and good lighting help. Gagging is expected.

options.text: Swab the tongue and cheeks
Swab the tonsils and posterior pharynx without touching the tongue, lips, or teeth
Have the client gargle into a cup
Swab only the front teeth

questions.stem: How often should an adult with diabetes generally have a dilated eye exam?
questions.rationale: Diabetic retinopathy may cause no symptoms until it is advanced. Regular exams allow early treatment to prevent vision loss.

options.text: Only when vision changes
At least yearly (or as advised by the eye care provider)
Every 10 years
Never, if glucose is controlled

questions.stem: A client receiving chemotherapy has a poor appetite and is losing weight. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Small, nutrient-dense, frequent meals maximize intake. Fluids between meals prevent early fullness. Nutritional supplements may help.

options.text: "Eat three large meals."
"Eat small, frequent, high-calorie, high-protein snacks and meals, and eat when you feel best, often in the morning."
"Drink fluids with meals to fill up."
"Skip meals when nauseated."

questions.stem: A client asks when to collect urine for a home pregnancy test for the most accurate result. Which response by the LPN/VN is best?
questions.rationale: First-morning urine is the most concentrated, which improves detection of hCG early in pregnancy. Dilute urine can cause false negatives.

options.text: "Any time after drinking lots of water."
"First-morning urine is best, because it has the highest concentration of hCG."
"At bedtime."
"After exercise."

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is applying an arm sling. Which positioning is correct?
questions.rationale: Keeping the hand slightly elevated reduces swelling, and padding prevents pressure at the neck. The nurse checks circulation in the fingers.

options.text: Hand hanging lower than the elbow
Elbow flexed about 90 degrees with the hand slightly higher than the elbow, and the strap padded at the neck
Arm fully extended
Sling tied tightly around the wrist

questions.stem: During a neurological check, the LPN/VN asks the client to squeeze both hands. What is the purpose of this test?
questions.rationale: Unequal grip strength can signal stroke, increasing ICP, or spinal cord problems. The nurse reports new asymmetry immediately.

options.text: To test hearing
To compare motor strength on both sides, since new one-sided weakness may indicate a neurological change
To test vision
To measure pain

questions.stem: Which dressing is commonly used for a clean, shallow stage 2 pressure injury with minimal drainage?
questions.rationale: Moist wound healing promotes epithelialization. Hydrocolloids and foams protect the wound and can stay in place several days. Pressure relief remains essential.

options.text: A dry gauze dressing changed every hour
A hydrocolloid or foam dressing, as prescribed, that maintains a moist wound environment
No dressing, with the wound left open to dry
A heating pad over the wound

questions.stem: A client says, "I can't sleep at night because I keep worrying about my job." Which response by the LPN/VN is an example of restating?
questions.rationale: Restating repeats the main idea of the client's message, showing the nurse is listening and encouraging the client to continue.

options.text: "You shouldn't worry so much."
"You're having trouble sleeping because you're worried about your job."
"Have you tried warm milk?"
"Why are you worried?"

questions.stem: A client with an uncomplicated pregnancy asks how often she will have prenatal visits. Which response by the LPN/VN reflects a typical schedule?
questions.rationale: Increasing frequency later in pregnancy allows monitoring for complications such as preeclampsia and changes in fetal growth. Schedules are adjusted for risk.

options.text: "Once per trimester."
"About every 4 weeks until 28 weeks, every 2 weeks from 28 to 36 weeks, then weekly until birth."
"Weekly from the start."
"Only at 20 weeks and at delivery."

questions.stem: How should a pregnant client wear a seat belt?
questions.rationale: Correct seat belt use protects both the pregnant person and the fetus. A belt across the uterus can cause placental abruption in a crash.

options.text: "Don't wear a seat belt during pregnancy."
"Place the lap belt low, across the hips and below the belly, and the shoulder belt across the chest and to the side of the belly."
"Place the lap belt across the top of the belly."
"Wear only the lap belt."

questions.stem: Which symptom should a postpartum client be taught to report immediately after discharge?
questions.rationale: These may indicate pulmonary embolism, preeclampsia, stroke, or hemorrhage. Warning sign education (such as AWHONN's POST-BIRTH) helps prevent maternal deaths.

options.text: Mild afterpains during breastfeeding
Chest pain, trouble breathing, severe headache, or soaking a pad in an hour or less
Lochia changing from red to pinkish-brown
Feeling tired

questions.stem: A newborn's axillary temperature is 96.8°F (36.0°C). What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: A normal newborn axillary temperature is about 97.7–99.5°F (36.5–37.5°C). Cold stress increases oxygen and glucose use and can cause hypoglycemia and respiratory distress.

options.text: Document it as normal
Place the newborn skin-to-skin or under a radiant warmer, recheck the temperature, check blood glucose per protocol, and report to the RN
Give the newborn a bath
Remove the hat to recheck the temperature

questions.stem: A client uses a space heater at home. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Space heaters are a leading cause of home heating fires. Clearance, direct wall outlets, and turning heaters off when unattended reduce risk.

options.text: "Place it near curtains to warm the room faster."
"Keep it at least 3 feet from anything that can burn, plug it directly into the wall, and turn it off when you leave or go to sleep."
"Use an extension cord to reach the bed."
"Dry clothes on the heater."
