questions.stem: The LPN/VN uses a shared blood glucose meter on a unit. Which action is required between clients?
questions.rationale: Shared meters have been linked to hepatitis B outbreaks. Single-use lancets and meter disinfection between clients are required.

options.text: Wipe the meter with a dry tissue
Clean and disinfect the meter with an approved disinfectant according to the manufacturer's instructions
No cleaning is needed if the lancet is changed
Store the meter in a pocket

questions.stem: A client is going home with a PICC line for IV antibiotics. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Keeping the site dry and recognizing signs of infection or thrombosis prevent complications. Swimming and BP measurements on the PICC arm are avoided.

options.text: "Swim to keep the arm active."
"Keep the dressing clean and dry, cover it with a waterproof cover when showering, and report redness, swelling, fever, or arm pain."
"Change the dressing yourself daily without training."
"Have your BP taken on the PICC arm."

questions.stem: Which intervention best reduces a hospitalized 2-year-old's distress?
questions.rationale: Toddlers depend on routines and attachment figures. Parental presence and familiar items reduce separation anxiety and regression.

options.text: Limiting parent visits to 1 hour
Encouraging a parent to stay, keeping home routines such as naps and bedtime rituals, and letting the child have a favorite toy
Changing caregivers frequently
Explaining procedures a week in advance

questions.stem: For each description, indicate the pressure injury stage.
questions.rationale: Stage 1 is intact skin with nonblanchable erythema or color change. Stage 2 is partial-thickness loss or an intact blister. Stage 3 is full-thickness loss with visible fat, which may include slough that doesn't hide the base. Deep tissue injury and unstageable categories also exist.
questions.answer_summary: Stage 1: intact nonblanchable redness, discoloration with warmth and firmness in dark skin. Stage 2: intact blister, shallow pink open wound. Stage 3: full-thickness wounds with visible fat.

rows.text: Intact skin with nonblanchable redness over the sacrum
Intact, serum-filled blister on the heel
Shallow open wound with a pink, moist bed and no slough
Area of persistent purplish discoloration, warmth, and firmness on intact skin in a client with dark skin
Full-thickness wound with visible subcutaneous fat, no bone or tendon
Deep crater with fat visible and some slough that does not obscure the wound base

questions.stem: Two hours after the first dose of oral amoxicillin, a resident develops an itchy, raised rash on the trunk and arms. The resident is breathing comfortably, has no lip or tongue swelling, and has stable vital signs. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the resident is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Hives after a new antibiotic suggest an allergic reaction that could progress to anaphylaxis. The drug is held, the provider may prescribe an antihistamine and an alternative antibiotic, and the allergy is documented to prevent future exposure.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: mild allergic drug reaction (urticaria). Actions: hold the next dose and notify the RN and provider; document the allergy and update the record and band. Monitor: breathing and swelling for progression; rash extent.

bowtie_groups.label: Condition (choose 1)
options: Normal medication side effect that needs no action

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Hold the next dose and notify the RN and provider
Document the reaction and ensure the allergy is added to the record and allergy band
Give the next dose early to build tolerance
Ignore the rash since breathing is normal

bowtie_groups.label: Parameters to monitor (choose 2)
options: Breathing, voice, and swelling of the lips or tongue for progression
Extent and appearance of the rash

questions.stem: A parent asks how to tell whether a toy is safe for a 10-month-old. Which guidance should the LPN/VN give?
questions.rationale: Objects small enough to fit through a toilet paper roll can block a young child's airway. Balloons, button batteries, and magnets are especially dangerous.

options.text: "Any toy labeled for ages 5 and up is fine."
"If a toy or part fits through a toilet paper tube, it is small enough to be a choking hazard."
"Balloons are safe for babies."
"Small magnets are safe if supervised."

questions.stem: The parent of a 3-year-old is worried because the child sometimes repeats words ("I-I-I want juice"). What should the LPN/VN explain?
questions.rationale: Developmental disfluency is common between ages 2 and 5. Persistent stuttering, visible struggle, or distress warrants speech evaluation.

options.text: "This is a serious speech disorder that needs immediate therapy."
"Brief repetitions are common as preschoolers' language develops quickly. Be patient, don't rush or finish sentences, and mention it to the provider if it persists or worsens."
"Punish your child for stuttering."
"Ask your child to speak faster."

questions.stem: Which strategy should the LPN/VN recommend to a family concerned about their school-age child's weight?
questions.rationale: Family-based lifestyle changes are most effective and avoid singling out the child. Children need at least 60 minutes of physical activity daily.

options.text: "Put your child on a strict diet alone."
"Make healthy changes as a family, such as regular physical activity, fewer sugary drinks, and limited recreational screen time."
"Use food as a reward for good grades."
"Skip breakfast to cut calories."

questions.stem: Which safety message is most important for the LPN/VN to reinforce with a newly licensed 16-year-old driver?
questions.rationale: Motor vehicle crashes are a leading cause of death for teens. Seat belts, avoiding distraction and impairment, and limiting teen passengers reduce risk.

options.text: "Seat belts are optional on short trips."
"Always wear a seat belt, never text or use your phone while driving, and never drive after using alcohol or drugs."
"Driving with several friends in the car is safest."
"Speeding is fine if the road is empty."

questions.stem: An older adult with osteoarthritis and a history of falls asks about exercise. Which activity should the LPN/VN suggest to improve balance?
questions.rationale: Tai chi improves balance, strength, and flexibility and reduces falls in older adults. It is also gentle on arthritic joints.

options.text: Competitive running
Tai chi
Heavy weightlifting without instruction
Complete rest

questions.stem: Which technique helps the LPN/VN obtain the most accurate respiratory rate in an adult?
questions.rationale: Clients often change their breathing when aware it is being counted. Counting for 30–60 seconds (a full minute if irregular) improves accuracy.

options.text: Tell the client, "I'm going to count your breathing now."
Count respirations while appearing to take the pulse, so the client doesn't change their breathing
Count for 10 seconds and multiply by 6
Count only when the client is talking

questions.stem: When measuring blood pressure manually, what does the first clear tapping sound the LPN/VN hears as the cuff deflates represent?
questions.rationale: The first Korotkoff sound marks the systolic pressure, and the point at which sounds disappear marks the diastolic pressure in adults.

options.text: The diastolic pressure
The systolic pressure
The pulse pressure
The mean arterial pressure

questions.stem: A client's temperature is 38.0°C. What is this in Fahrenheit?
questions.rationale: °F = (°C × 9/5) + 32 = (38 × 1.8) + 32 = 68.4 + 32 = 100.4°F. This value is often used as the threshold for fever.

questions.stem: What is the maximum volume generally recommended for an IM injection into an adult's deltoid muscle?
questions.rationale: The deltoid is a small muscle and is used mainly for vaccines and small volumes. Larger volumes go into the ventrogluteal or vastus lateralis sites.

options.text: 0.1 mL
About 1 mL (up to 2 mL in some well-developed adults per policy)
5 mL
10 mL

questions.stem: Which technique is correct for an intradermal injection such as a tuberculin skin test?
questions.rationale: A visible bleb confirms intradermal placement. Massaging can spread the solution and alter the result.

options.text: Insert the needle at 90 degrees and massage the site
Insert the needle bevel up at about 5–15 degrees, inject slowly to form a small bleb, and do not massage the site
Aspirate before injecting
Inject into the deltoid muscle

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN mix a vial of NPH insulin before drawing it up?
questions.rationale: Shaking creates bubbles that make accurate dosing difficult. NPH is a suspension that must be resuspended gently.

options.text: Shake the vial vigorously
Roll the vial gently between the palms until the solution is uniformly cloudy
Microwave the vial briefly
No mixing is needed

questions.stem: Which instruction is correct for using a steroid nasal spray?
questions.rationale: Aiming away from the septum reduces irritation and nosebleeds. Gentle sniffing keeps the medication in the nasal passages. Bottles are not shared.

options.text: "Tilt your head far back and spray forcefully toward the septum."
"Gently blow your nose first, keep your head upright, aim the tip slightly away from the center of your nose, and sniff gently while spraying."
"Blow your nose right after spraying."
"Share the bottle with family."

questions.stem: Which intervention should the LPN/VN encourage for a client with pneumonia who has thick secretions and no fluid restriction?
questions.rationale: Adequate hydration thins secretions, making them easier to cough up. Upright positioning and deep breathing improve ventilation.

options.text: Limit fluids to 500 mL per day
Drink about 2–3 L of fluid per day, and cough and deep breathe regularly
Stay flat in bed
Avoid coughing

questions.stem: A client reports right shoulder pain the day after laparoscopic gallbladder surgery. What should the LPN/VN explain and suggest?
questions.rationale: CO2 used to inflate the abdomen can irritate the diaphragm and cause referred shoulder pain. Ambulation helps the body absorb the gas. Severe or worsening pain should still be reported.

options.text: "This means you had a heart attack."
"Shoulder pain is common after laparoscopy from the gas used during surgery. Walking and changing position can help it pass."
"Stay completely still in bed."
"Apply ice to your abdomen."

questions.stem: When inserting a urinary catheter in a female client, where does the LPN/VN expect to find the urethral meatus?
questions.rationale: The urethral meatus lies below the clitoris and above the vaginal orifice. If the catheter enters the vagina, it is left in place as a landmark and a new sterile catheter is used.

options.text: Below the vaginal opening
Between the clitoris and the vaginal opening
Above the clitoris
Inside the vaginal opening

questions.stem: When the LPN/VN strokes the sole of an adult's foot, the big toe extends upward and the other toes fan out. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: A positive Babinski sign is normal in infants up to about 1–2 years but abnormal in adults, suggesting upper motor neuron dysfunction.

options.text: Document it as normal for adults
Report it, because a positive Babinski sign in an adult may indicate a central nervous system problem
Repeat the test until the toes curl down
Ignore it

questions.stem: The LPN/VN observes a small, raised skin lesion filled with clear fluid, less than 1 cm across. How should the nurse describe it?
questions.rationale: A vesicle is a small, clear fluid-filled blister. A pustule contains pus, a macule is flat, and a nodule is a solid, raised lesion.

options.text: Macule
Vesicle
Pustule
Nodule

questions.stem: A client after a stroke keeps the affected hand tightly clenched. Which intervention helps prevent a contracture?
questions.rationale: Regular ROM and positioning devices maintain joint function and prevent permanent flexion deformities.

options.text: Leave the hand clenched to protect it
Perform range-of-motion exercises and use a hand roll or resting splint as prescribed
Tape the fingers together
Keep the arm hanging at the side

questions.stem: A client with generalized anxiety drinks five energy drinks a day. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Stimulants can trigger or worsen anxiety symptoms. Gradual reduction prevents withdrawal headaches and fatigue.

options.text: "Energy drinks help anxiety."
"Caffeine can worsen anxiety, heart palpitations, and sleep problems. Try gradually cutting back to avoid withdrawal headaches."
"Switch to espresso instead."
"Stop all fluids."

questions.stem: A newly hired aide asks whether having a suicidal client sign a promise not to hurt themselves is enough to keep the client safe. Which response by the LPN/VN is accurate?
questions.rationale: No-harm contracts provide false reassurance. Collaborative safety planning, removing means, and appropriate observation are evidence-based approaches.

options.text: "Yes, a signed contract guarantees safety."
"No. Signed promises are not proven to prevent suicide and should never replace observation, environmental safety, and a safety plan."
"Only if the client signs it twice."
"Contracts are required for all clients."

questions.stem: A pregnant client says her gums bleed when brushing and asks whether she should avoid the dentist until after birth. What should the LPN/VN advise?
questions.rationale: Hormonal changes cause pregnancy gingivitis. Untreated gum disease may be linked to adverse pregnancy outcomes, and dental care is safe throughout pregnancy.

options.text: "Avoid all dental care during pregnancy."
"Gum changes are common in pregnancy. Routine dental care and cleanings are safe and recommended, so let your dentist know you're pregnant."
"Stop brushing to prevent bleeding."
"Only go to the dentist if a tooth falls out."

questions.topic: When to go to the hospital in labor
questions.stem: A first-time mother at 39 weeks asks when to go to the hospital. Which guidance should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: The 5-1-1 guideline helps identify active labor. Ruptured membranes, bleeding, decreased fetal movement, and severe pain require prompt evaluation. Instructions vary by provider.

options.text: "Wait until contractions are every 30 minutes."
"Go in when contractions are about 5 minutes apart, last about 1 minute, for about 1 hour, or right away if your water breaks, you have heavy bleeding, or the baby moves less."
"Go in only after your water breaks."
"Stay home until you feel the urge to push."

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce about cleaning breast pump parts?
questions.rationale: Milk residue can grow bacteria that may harm infants. CDC recommends cleaning after every use and sanitizing regularly for young or medically fragile infants.

options.text: "Rinse the parts only once a week."
"After each use, take apart and wash pump parts that touch milk in hot, soapy water or a dishwasher, then air dry."
"Store wet parts in a closed bag."
"Share the pump parts with friends."

questions.stem: For each household measure, indicate the equivalent volume in milliliters.
questions.rationale: 1 tsp = 5 mL, 1 tbsp = 3 tsp = 15 mL, and 1 fl oz = 2 tbsp = 30 mL. Clients are taught to use calibrated devices rather than kitchen spoons.
questions.answer_summary: 5 mL: 1 tsp. 15 mL: 1 tbsp, 3 tsp, 1/2 oz. 30 mL: 1 fl oz, 2 tbsp.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old resident suddenly reports crushing chest pressure spreading to the left arm and jaw. The resident is sweaty, pale, and short of breath. HR is 108/min, and BP is 150/92 mm Hg. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the resident is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Crushing chest pain with radiation, diaphoresis, and dyspnea suggest ACS, where time to treatment saves heart muscle. Aspirin and nitroglycerin may be given per protocol or order. The nurse stays with the resident because sudden cardiac arrest can occur.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: acute coronary syndrome. Actions: activate emergency response and notify the RN; keep the resident at rest with HOB elevated and stay. Monitor: vital signs and pain; responsiveness and breathing with an AED available.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Activate the emergency response system and notify the RN immediately
Keep the resident at rest with the head of the bed elevated and stay with the resident
Have the resident walk to the nurses' station
Offer a large meal to settle the stomach
Wait 1 hour to see if the pain passes

bowtie_groups.label: Parameters to monitor (choose 2)
options: Responsiveness and breathing, with an AED available

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is teaching new parents to recognize early hunger cues. Which behavior is an early cue?
questions.rationale: Crying is a late hunger cue. Feeding in response to early cues makes latching easier and reduces infant distress.

options.text: Crying loudly
Rooting, lip smacking, and bringing hands to the mouth
Turning away from the breast or bottle
Falling asleep

questions.stem: A family with a toddler has a tall dresser and a flat-screen TV. Which safety measure should the LPN/VN recommend?
questions.rationale: Tip-overs cause serious injuries and deaths in young children. Anchoring furniture and not placing enticing items on top prevent climbing accidents.

options.text: "Put toys on top of the dresser so your toddler can't reach them."
"Anchor dressers, bookcases, and TVs to the wall with anti-tip devices."
"Place the TV on the edge of the dresser."
"Let your toddler climb the dresser to build strength."

questions.stem: A 4-year-old becomes upset after a blood draw and insists on a bandage over the tiny puncture site. How should the LPN/VN respond?
questions.rationale: Preschoolers commonly fear mutilation and bodily harm. Bandages provide reassurance and a sense of control.

options.text: "You don't need a bandage for that."
Apply a bandage. Preschoolers often fear body injury, and a bandage helps them feel their body is "fixed."
Tell the child to stop crying
Ignore the request

questions.stem: Which behavior in a 15-year-old should the LPN/VN report as a possible warning sign of an eating disorder?
questions.rationale: Early identification of eating disorders improves outcomes. Other signs include frequent bathroom trips after meals, wearing baggy clothes, and preoccupation with weight.

options.text: Eating a larger lunch after sports practice
Rapid weight loss, skipping meals, rigid food rituals, and excessive exercise
Trying a new vegetable
Snacking after school

questions.stem: An older adult has lost muscle strength and eats mostly toast and tea. Which dietary suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Older adults need adequate protein to prevent sarcopenia and frailty. Combining protein intake with physical activity preserves strength and function.

options.text: "Protein isn't important at your age."
"Include a source of protein, such as eggs, yogurt, fish, beans, or poultry, at each meal to help maintain muscle."
"Eat only one meal a day."
"Increase sweets for energy."

questions.stem: An older resident often feels dizzy and has nearly fallen shortly after large meals. What should the LPN/VN suggest?
questions.rationale: Postprandial hypotension occurs as blood flow shifts to the digestive tract after eating. Smaller meals, water before meals, and caution when rising reduce falls.

options.text: "Walk right after meals."
"Eat smaller, more frequent meals, and sit or rest for a while after eating before standing up."
"Drink alcohol with meals."
"Skip meals entirely."

questions.stem: A client with suspected tuberculosis needs sputum specimens for acid-fast bacilli (AFB). Which instruction is correct?
questions.rationale: Multiple specimens improve detection. Early-morning specimens contain secretions that collect overnight. The client coughs deeply to produce sputum, not saliva.

options.text: "Collect one specimen at any time."
"Collect three sputum specimens, ideally early in the morning, about 8–24 hours apart."
"Spit saliva into the cup."
"Rinse with mouthwash first."

questions.stem: The provider orders blood cultures and IV antibiotics for a client with suspected sepsis. Which action is correct?
questions.rationale: Antibiotics can prevent organisms from growing in cultures. Two sets from different sites improve detection and help distinguish true infection from contamination. Skin is cleaned thoroughly first.

options.text: Give the antibiotic, then draw cultures the next day
Collect cultures, usually two sets from separate sites, before the first antibiotic dose if this doesn't significantly delay treatment
Draw cultures from the IV line where antibiotics are running
Collect only one bottle

questions.stem: Besides prescribed antiemetics, which nonpharmacological measure may the LPN/VN offer a client with postoperative nausea?
questions.rationale: P6 acupressure and relaxation techniques can reduce nausea. Strong odors and rapid intake can worsen it.

options.text: Strong-smelling foods
Acupressure wristband at the P6 point, slow deep breathing, and a calm, odor-free environment
Lying flat immediately after eating
Drinking large amounts of carbonated fluid quickly

questions.stem: A client needs frequent dressing changes on a large abdominal wound. Which product helps protect the skin from repeated tape removal?
questions.rationale: Montgomery straps stay on the skin while the dressing is changed underneath by untying and retying the straps, which reduces skin damage from repeated adhesive removal.

options.text: Wrapping tape around the abdomen
Montgomery straps (tie tapes)
Adhesive tape applied directly each time
Staples

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is checking pedal pulses. Which technique gives the most useful information?
questions.rationale: Comparing both sides helps detect decreased perfusion on one side. The thumb has its own pulse and can cause errors, and excessive pressure can obliterate a weak pulse.

options.text: Check one foot only
Palpate pulses on both feet at the same time or one right after the other, and compare their strength
Use the thumb to palpate
Press firmly enough to stop the pulse

questions.stem: Which symptoms suggest influenza rather than a common cold?
questions.rationale: Influenza typically starts abruptly with systemic symptoms. Colds develop gradually with mainly nasal symptoms. High-risk clients with influenza may benefit from early antivirals.

options.text: Gradual onset of a runny nose and sneezing without fever
Sudden onset of fever, body aches, chills, fatigue, and headache
Mild sore throat only
Itchy, watery eyes

questions.stem: Under current anesthesia guidelines for healthy adults having elective surgery, how long before anesthesia may clear liquids generally be taken?
questions.rationale: American Society of Anesthesiologists guidelines allow clear liquids up to 2 hours before anesthesia and a light meal up to 6 hours before. Facilities and surgeons may give specific instructions, and some medications may change this guidance.

options.text: Up to 12 hours before
Up to 2 hours before
Up to 30 minutes before
No liquids for 24 hours

questions.stem: What is the minimum acceptable urine output that the LPN/VN should expect for an adult?
questions.rationale: Output below about 30 mL/hr may indicate poor kidney perfusion or dehydration and should be reported.

options.text: About 5 mL/hr
About 30 mL/hr (about 0.5 mL/kg/hr)
About 200 mL/hr
About 500 mL/day

questions.stem: A client with epilepsy says, "I smell burning rubber. That usually happens before my seizures." What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: An aura warns that a seizure may follow. Lying down in a safe area prevents injury from falling. The nurse observes and documents the seizure.

options.text: Ignore the comment
Help the client lie down in a safe place, move nearby objects away, stay with the client, and call for help
Give the client a drink of water
Walk the client to the bathroom

questions.stem: A client has a painful, red sunburn without blisters. Which comfort measure should the LPN/VN suggest?
questions.rationale: Cooling and moisturizing ease discomfort, and hydration replaces fluid loss. Blistering, fever, or chills may indicate a more severe burn that needs evaluation.

options.text: Apply butter
Take cool showers or use cool compresses, apply aloe or moisturizer, drink extra fluids, and avoid further sun exposure
Scrub the skin
Apply petroleum jelly and cover with plastic

questions.stem: Which intervention helps prevent footdrop in a client on prolonged bed rest?
questions.rationale: Keeping the feet in a neutral position and exercising the ankles prevents plantar flexion contracture. Tight linens push the feet into plantar flexion.

options.text: Tucking the top sheet tightly over the feet
Using high-top sneakers, foot boots, or splints as prescribed and performing ankle range-of-motion exercises
Keeping the feet pointed down
Placing pillows under the knees

questions.stem: Which action by staff should the LPN/VN avoid around a client with paranoid thinking?
questions.rationale: Whispering and laughing can reinforce the client's belief that others are talking about or plotting against them.

options.text: Explaining procedures clearly
Whispering or laughing near the client where it may seem directed at them
Being consistent and honest
Offering choices

questions.stem: Which instruction is correct for using nicotine gum?
questions.rationale: The "chew and park" method lets nicotine be absorbed through the lining of the mouth. Continuous chewing causes nicotine to be swallowed, leading to hiccups and nausea. Acidic drinks reduce absorption.

options.text: "Chew it continuously like regular gum."
"Chew slowly until you notice a peppery taste or tingling, then park it between your cheek and gum. Repeat for about 30 minutes."
"Drink coffee or soda while using it."
"Swallow the gum."

questions.stem: A pregnant client asks whether an occasional glass of wine is safe. Which response by the LPN/VN is correct?
questions.rationale: Alcohol crosses the placenta and can cause lifelong physical, behavioral, and learning problems. Clients who need help stopping are supported without judgment.

options.text: "One glass a day is fine."
"No amount of alcohol is known to be safe during pregnancy. Avoiding alcohol completely prevents fetal alcohol spectrum disorders."
"Only liquor is harmful."
"Alcohol is safe after the first trimester."

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce for parents who are bottle-feeding a newborn?
questions.rationale: Holding the baby semi-upright and keeping the nipple full reduce swallowed air, and burping relieves gas. Bottle propping increases choking and ear infection risk. Responsive feeding respects the infant's fullness cues.

options.text: "Prop the bottle so the baby can feed alone."
"Hold the baby semi-upright, tilt the bottle so the nipple stays full of milk, and burp the baby periodically during the feeding."
"Enlarge the nipple hole so the baby feeds faster."
"Force the baby to finish every bottle."

questions.stem: Parents ask how much a newborn usually sleeps. Which response by the LPN/VN is accurate?
questions.rationale: Newborns sleep much of the day but wake frequently to feed. A newborn who is very difficult to wake for feedings should be evaluated.

options.text: "About 8 hours a day."
"About 14–17 hours a day in short periods, waking to feed about every 2–3 hours."
"Newborns sleep through the night from birth."
"About 22 hours without waking."

questions.stem: The LPN/VN needs to step into a client's room briefly during a medication pass. What should the nurse do with the medication cart?
questions.rationale: Unattended, unlocked medications can be taken or tampered with, which risks harm and diversion.

options.text: Leave it unlocked in the hallway
Lock the cart or keep it within direct sight so no one can access medications
Ask a visitor to watch the cart
Leave medications on top of the cart

questions.stem: For each adult lab value, indicate whether it is within the usual normal range or abnormal and should be reported.
questions.rationale: Typical adult ranges are potassium 3.5–5.0, sodium 135–145, fasting glucose 70–99, hemoglobin about 12–16 (female), WBC 4,500–11,000, and platelets 150,000–400,000. Reference ranges vary slightly by lab.
questions.answer_summary: Normal: K 4.0, fasting glucose 90, WBC 7,500. Abnormal: Na 128, Hgb 9.0, platelets 60,000.

rows.text: Hemoglobin 9.0 g/dL in an adult female

questions.stem: One week after a posterior-approach total hip replacement, a resident bends forward in a low chair to pick up a dropped item and cries out in severe pain. The operative leg now appears shorter and turned inward, and the resident cannot move it. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the resident is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Hip flexion beyond 90 degrees violates posterior hip precautions and can dislocate the prosthesis, causing sudden pain, shortening, and rotation. Reduction is done by the provider. Pulling or moving the leg can injure nerves and vessels.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: hip prosthesis dislocation. Actions: keep the resident still and support the leg; notify the RN and provider immediately. Monitor: neurovascular status; pain and vital signs.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Keep the resident still and support the leg in the position found
Notify the RN and provider immediately
Pull the leg to straighten it
Help the resident stand to test the hip

bowtie_groups.label: Parameters to monitor (choose 2)
options: Neurovascular status of the operative leg

questions.stem: Which observation shows a rear-facing infant car seat harness is used correctly?
questions.rationale: Correct strap height and snugness prevent ejection and injury. Bulky coats compress in a crash, leaving the harness too loose. Blankets can be placed over the buckled harness instead.

options.text: Harness straps above the shoulders with the chest clip at the belly
Harness straps at or below the shoulders, snug with no slack, and the chest clip at armpit level
The infant wearing a puffy winter coat under the harness
Loose straps for comfort

questions.stem: How much fluoride toothpaste should parents use for a 2-year-old?
questions.rationale: For children under 3, a rice-grain-sized smear provides cavity protection while limiting swallowed fluoride. A pea-sized amount is used for ages 3–6.

options.text: A full strip on the brush
A smear about the size of a grain of rice
A pea-sized amount for children under 3
No toothpaste until age 6

questions.stem: Which change in a school-age child should the LPN/VN recognize as a possible sign of bullying?
questions.rationale: Unexplained physical complaints, school avoidance, and social withdrawal may indicate bullying. Parents are encouraged to talk openly with the child and involve the school.

options.text: Increased interest in school activities
Frequent stomachaches before school, avoiding school, lost belongings, and withdrawal from friends
Making new friends
Improved grades

questions.stem: Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce with an adolescent who uses tampons?
questions.rationale: Prolonged use and high-absorbency tampons increase the risk of toxic shock syndrome, a rare but life-threatening condition.

options.text: "Leave the same tampon in overnight for 12 hours."
"Use the lowest absorbency needed, change tampons every 4–8 hours, and seek care for sudden high fever, rash, or vomiting."
"Use the highest absorbency at all times."
"Tampons can be worn continuously for several days."

questions.stem: An older adult reports sudden hearing loss in one ear that started yesterday. What should the LPN/VN advise?
questions.rationale: Sudden sensorineural hearing loss is an otologic emergency. Corticosteroids are most effective when started early. Age-related hearing loss develops gradually in both ears.

options.text: "This is normal aging, so no action is needed."
"Sudden hearing loss should be evaluated urgently, ideally within days, because early treatment may improve recovery."
"Use cotton swabs to clean the ear."
"Buy a hearing aid online."

questions.stem: Which action is correct when the LPN/VN (where permitted) or RN uses a saline lock to give an IV medication?
questions.rationale: Flushing confirms patency, prevents mixing of incompatible drugs, and keeps the catheter clear. If resistance is felt, the nurse does not force the flush.

options.text: Give the medication without flushing
Flush with normal saline before and after the medication, and between incompatible medications, per policy
Flush forcefully against resistance
Use tap water to flush

questions.stem: The LPN/VN is weighing a bedbound client on a bed scale each day. Which action ensures accurate results?
questions.rationale: Consistent conditions, same equipment, same linens, and same time allow true weight changes, such as fluid gain, to be detected.

options.text: Weigh the client at different times each day
Zero the scale with the same linens and equipment present, and weigh at the same time each day
Add pillows on some days
Weigh the client with the drainage bag full

questions.stem: A client uses a TENS unit for chronic back pain. Which instruction is correct?
questions.rationale: Correct electrode placement and settings deliver safe, comfortable stimulation. Electrodes over the carotid sinus, in water, or near a pacemaker without approval are unsafe.

options.text: "Place the electrodes over the front of your neck."
"Place electrodes on clean, intact skin around the painful area, and avoid use over the carotid area, over broken skin, or if you have certain implanted devices unless approved."
"Use it in the bath."
"Turn it to maximum strength immediately."

questions.stem: A client who has worn an oxygen mask continuously for 2 days has red areas on the bridge of the nose and behind the ears. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Medical devices can cause pressure injuries. Padding and frequent skin checks help prevent skin breakdown while oxygen therapy continues.

options.text: Tighten the mask
Pad pressure points as allowed, reposition the straps, check the skin frequently, and report the redness
Remove the oxygen
Apply adhesive tape to hold the mask

questions.stem: A client with a pacemaker set at a lower rate of 60/min is taught to check the pulse at home. Which finding should the client report?
questions.rationale: A pulse below the programmed lower rate may mean the pacemaker is malfunctioning or the battery is low. Symptoms require prompt evaluation.

options.text: Pulse of 72/min
Pulse below 60/min, or symptoms such as dizziness or fainting
Pulse of 80/min after walking
Pulse of 64/min at rest

questions.stem: Which technique should the LPN/VN teach for abdominal massage to relieve constipation?
questions.rationale: Clockwise massage follows the colon from ascending to transverse to descending and may promote peristalsis. It complements fiber, fluids, and activity.

options.text: Rub counterclockwise around the abdomen
Use gentle circular strokes in a clockwise direction, following the path of the colon
Press hard on the stomach
Massage only the upper chest

questions.stem: A postoperative client has difficulty starting urination. Which measure should the LPN/VN try first?
questions.rationale: Nursing measures can stimulate voiding. If the client still can't void and the bladder is distended, the nurse reports it for a bladder scan or catheterization order.

options.text: Insert an indwelling catheter immediately
Provide privacy, help the client into a natural position (such as standing for males if allowed), run water, and pour warm water over the perineum
Restrict fluids
Tell the client to wait until tomorrow

questions.stem: A client with Parkinson's disease "freezes" and cannot start walking. Which strategy should the LPN/VN suggest?
questions.rationale: External cues help bypass the motor-planning difficulty that causes freezing. Pulling can cause falls.

options.text: Pull the client forward by the arms
Use a visual or auditory cue, such as stepping over a line on the floor or counting a rhythm, and shift weight side to side
Tell the client to hurry
Have the client look at their feet

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN document the size of a pressure injury?
questions.rationale: Consistent, objective measurements track healing over time. Undermining and tunneling are also measured and documented using a clock-face reference.

options.text: Estimate it as "about the size of a coin"
Measure length (head to toe), width (side to side), and depth in centimeters using a disposable ruler and a sterile applicator
Measure only the depth
Measure in inches without a ruler

questions.stem: A client with knee osteoarthritis and obesity asks how to reduce knee pain. Which suggestion is supported by evidence?
questions.rationale: Each pound of body weight adds several pounds of force across the knee during walking. Weight loss and exercise are core treatments for knee osteoarthritis.

options.text: "Avoid all activity."
"Even modest weight loss can reduce the stress on your knees and lessen pain, especially combined with low-impact exercise."
"Weight has no effect on knee pain."
"Run on hard surfaces daily."

questions.stem: A client shouts at the LPN/VN, "This place is terrible! Nobody answers my call light!" What is the best initial response?
questions.rationale: Acknowledging feelings and focusing on the client's needs de-escalates anger. Defensive or dismissive responses escalate conflict. The nurse maintains safety if the client's behavior becomes threatening.

options.text: "Stop yelling at me."
"You're frustrated that it's taken a long time to get help. Tell me what you need right now."
Leave the room without responding
"That's not true; we answer quickly."

questions.stem: A resident with advanced dementia suddenly becomes agitated and is hitting at staff. What should the LPN/VN check first?
questions.rationale: People with dementia often express unmet needs through behavior. Identifying and meeting those needs is the first step before considering medication.

options.text: Whether the resident needs a sedative
Whether the resident has unmet needs, such as pain, hunger, thirst, a full bladder or bowel, or discomfort
Whether the resident is being difficult on purpose
Whether the family visited

questions.stem: A client in the third trimester reports low back pain. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Pregnancy shifts the center of gravity and loosens ligaments. Posture, pelvic tilts, supportive shoes, and body mechanics ease back pain. Rhythmic back pain may indicate labor.

options.text: "Wear high heels to improve posture."
"Practice good posture, do pelvic tilt exercises, wear low-heeled supportive shoes, and bend at the knees when lifting."
"Stay in bed all day."
"Take aspirin regularly."

questions.stem: A postpartum client has a repaired fourth-degree perineal laceration. Which action should the LPN/VN avoid?
questions.rationale: A fourth-degree laceration extends through the rectal mucosa. Anything inserted into the rectum can disrupt the repair. Stool softeners prevent straining.

options.text: Giving a prescribed stool softener
Administering a rectal suppository or taking a rectal temperature
Offering sitz baths
Applying ice packs in the first 24 hours

questions.stem: New parents are worried because their 3-day-old sneezes and hiccups often. How should the LPN/VN respond?
questions.rationale: These are normal newborn behaviors. Fever, poor feeding, labored breathing, or lethargy would need evaluation. Water is not given to young infants.

options.text: "Your baby may have a serious infection."
"Sneezing and hiccups are common in newborns. Sneezing helps clear the nose, and hiccups usually go away on their own."
"Give your baby water to stop the hiccups."
"Your baby is allergic to your milk."

questions.stem: What should the LPN/VN do each time before entering an airborne isolation room while wearing a fit-tested N95 respirator?
questions.rationale: Annual fit testing confirms the correct model and size, but a seal check with each use makes sure the respirator is on properly. Facial hair can prevent a proper seal.

options.text: Nothing, since the respirator was fit-tested last year
Perform a user seal check by covering the respirator and exhaling and inhaling to check for air leaks, adjusting as needed
Wear a surgical mask over it instead of checking
Pinch the nosepiece loosely

questions.stem: Which action should the LPN/VN take when leaving a toddler in a hospital crib?
questions.rationale: Children can fall from cribs with lowered rails. Climbing toddlers may need a crib top, and soft bedding increases suffocation risk for infants.

options.text: Leave one side rail down for easy access
Raise and lock both side rails fully, and consider a crib top if the child can climb out
Place stuffed animals and pillows in the crib for comfort
Leave the crib next to an open window

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN apply ophthalmic ointment?
questions.rationale: This technique distributes medication and avoids contamination. The client closes the eye gently and rolls the eye to spread the ointment. Vision may blur briefly.

options.text: Place a large blob directly on the cornea
Apply a thin ribbon along the inside of the lower eyelid from the inner to the outer corner, without touching the eye
Rub the ointment into the eyelashes
Apply it to the upper lid only

questions.stem: For each nurse statement, identify the therapeutic communication technique used.
questions.rationale: Open-ended prompts invite detailed responses. Reflection mirrors feelings back to the client. Clarification seeks to understand vague or confusing statements.
questions.answer_summary: Open-ended: feelings since surgery, tell me about your family. Reflection: angry about delay, worried about going home. Clarification: what "off" means, asking to explain again.

rows.text: "How have you been feeling since your surgery?"
"What do you mean when you say you feel 'off'?"
"I'm not sure I understand. Can you explain that again?"

questions.stem: While being fed lunch, a resident with a history of stroke begins coughing, has a wet, gurgly voice, and the SpO2 drops from 95% to 88%. The resident can still speak. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the resident is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Coughing, a wet voice, and falling SpO2 during eating suggest aspiration. The resident can still speak, so this is not complete obstruction. Feeding is stopped until a swallow evaluation is done. Aspiration pneumonia may develop over the next 24–72 hours.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: aspiration during feeding. Actions: stop feeding, keep upright, suction as needed; notify the RN. Monitor: SpO2 and breathing; lung sounds and temperature.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Stop the feeding, keep the resident upright, and suction the mouth if needed
Give sips of thin water to wash the food down
Lay the resident flat to rest

bowtie_groups.label: Parameters to monitor (choose 2)
options: Lung sounds and temperature over the next several days

questions.stem: A parent asks whether to give fruit juice to a 7-month-old. What does the AAP recommend?
questions.rationale: Juice offers no nutritional benefit for infants and increases the risk of tooth decay and poor weight gain. Whole fruit is preferred when the child is ready.

options.text: "Give 8 oz of juice daily for vitamins."
"Avoid juice before age 1. Offer breast milk or formula, and introduce small sips of water with solids."
"Juice can replace formula."
"Put juice in the bottle at bedtime."

questions.stem: A parent says the 4-year-old sometimes sits up screaming during the night, seems unaware of the parent, and doesn't remember it in the morning. What should the LPN/VN explain?
questions.rationale: Night terrors occur in deep sleep, and children usually don't remember them. Nightmares occur in REM sleep, and the child wakes and remembers. Unusual features or frequency warrant evaluation.

options.text: "Wake your child fully and ask about the dream."
"This sounds like night terrors. Keep your child safe, don't try to fully wake them, and keep a regular sleep schedule."
"This is a seizure every time."
"Punish your child for screaming."

questions.stem: How much sleep does a 9-year-old generally need each night?
questions.rationale: School-age children need 9–12 hours of sleep for learning, growth, and mood. Consistent bedtimes and no screens in the bedroom help.

options.text: About 5–6 hours
About 9–12 hours
About 15–16 hours
Sleep needs don't matter at this age

questions.stem: Which finding in a 14-year-old may indicate depression and should be reported?
questions.rationale: Adolescent depression often presents as irritability rather than sadness. Persistent changes in functioning warrant screening, including for suicide risk.

options.text: Occasional moodiness after an argument
Persistent irritability, withdrawal from friends, falling grades, and changes in sleep or appetite for several weeks
Enjoying time with friends
Interest in a new hobby

questions.stem: An 82-year-old resident has been taking lorazepam nightly for sleep and has fallen twice this month. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: Benzodiazepines increase the risk of falls, fractures, and confusion in older adults and are on the Beers Criteria list. Nonpharmacological sleep measures are preferred.

options.text: Increase the dose so the resident sleeps through the night
Report the falls and the medication to the RN and provider for review, and reinforce fall precautions
Give the dose earlier in the evening
Add diphenhydramine

questions.stem: For which client should the LPN/VN avoid taking a rectal temperature?
questions.rationale: Rectal temperatures can injure mucosa and introduce infection in neutropenic clients, and can disrupt rectal surgical sites. Rectal temperatures are also avoided in clients with bleeding disorders.

options.text: A healthy adult who cannot hold an oral thermometer
A client with severe neutropenia or who recently had rectal surgery
A client who just drank water
A client with a cold

questions.stem: Which technique is correct for taking an axillary temperature?
questions.rationale: A dry axilla and good skin contact improve accuracy. Axillary readings are generally lower than core temperatures and are used for screening.

options.text: Place the thermometer over clothing
Place the probe in the center of a dry axilla and hold the arm snugly against the side until the reading is complete
Take the reading right after bathing
Hold the arm away from the body

questions.stem: A client with diabetes has deep, rapid, labored breathing. How should the LPN/VN document this pattern, and what does it suggest?
questions.rationale: Kussmaul breathing blows off CO2 to compensate for acidosis. It is reported immediately, along with glucose and ketone checks.

options.text: Cheyne-Stokes respirations, suggesting approaching death
Kussmaul respirations, suggesting the body is compensating for metabolic acidosis such as DKA
Bradypnea, suggesting opioid overdose
Normal breathing

questions.stem: What water temperature should the LPN/VN use for a bed bath?
questions.rationale: Warm water is comfortable and safe. Older adults and clients with decreased sensation are at risk for burns from hot water.

options.text: Very hot, about 130°F (54°C)
Warm, about 110–115°F (43–46°C), checked with a thermometer or wrist and adjusted to client comfort
Cold tap water
Whatever temperature comes out of the tap

questions.stem: A client uses an oxygen concentrator at home. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Concentrators need electricity, so backup cylinders prevent dangerous interruptions. Generators must never be run indoors because of carbon monoxide risk.

options.text: "The concentrator works without electricity."
"Keep a backup oxygen cylinder, register with your power company as having medical equipment, and know how to switch to the backup."
"Use a gas generator indoors during outages."
"You don't need a backup."

questions.stem: Which instruction is correct for using a nitroglycerin translingual spray?
questions.rationale: The spray is absorbed through the oral mucosa. As with tablets, the client calls 911 if chest pain isn't relieved 5 minutes after the first dose.

options.text: "Inhale the spray deeply into your lungs."
"Sit down, spray onto or under your tongue without inhaling, and close your mouth. Don't shake the canister."
"Swallow the spray immediately."
"Spray it on your chest."

questions.stem: A client started on oxycodone 2 days ago reports mild nausea. Which information should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Tolerance to opioid-related nausea usually develops within days, but tolerance to constipation does not. Antiemetics may be prescribed if needed.

options.text: "Nausea means you are allergic to the medication."
"Nausea is a common side effect that often improves within a few days. Taking the medication with food may help, and let us know if it continues or you vomit."
"Stop the medication immediately."
"Double the dose to get past the nausea."

questions.stem: An older man with benign prostatic hyperplasia wakes several times a night to urinate. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Shifting fluid intake earlier and avoiding bladder irritants reduce nighttime urination while maintaining total daily hydration.

options.text: "Drink most of your fluids in the evening."
"Limit fluids for a few hours before bed, avoid caffeine and alcohol in the evening, and empty your bladder before sleep."
"Stop drinking fluids entirely."
"Drink coffee at bedtime."

questions.topic: Skin checks in spinal cord injury
questions.stem: A client with paraplegia is going home. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce about skin care?
questions.rationale: Without sensation, pressure injuries can develop unnoticed. Daily inspection and pressure relief are essential, and heat can cause burns on skin without sensation.

options.text: "Check your skin once a month."
"Inspect your skin every day, using a mirror for hard-to-see areas like the buttocks and heels, and shift your weight often while sitting."
"Only check areas that hurt."
"Use a heating pad on your legs."

questions.stem: A client has an intact friction blister on the heel from new shoes. What should the LPN/VN advise?
questions.rationale: The blister roof protects the skin underneath from infection. Clients with diabetes or poor circulation should have foot blisters evaluated.

options.text: "Pop it with a pin."
"Leave it intact, cover it with a protective dressing or padding, and wear shoes that don't rub."
"Peel off the skin."
"Apply rubbing alcohol daily."

questions.stem: Which action is correct when the LPN/VN provides skin care for a client in a rigid cervical collar?
questions.rationale: The chin, occiput, and clavicles are at risk for pressure injury. Care must maintain spinal alignment and follow orders on whether the collar may be opened.

options.text: Remove the collar and let the client move the neck freely
With a second person holding the head in alignment (if permitted per orders), remove the front and back pads one at a time, clean and dry the skin, and inspect for pressure areas
Never check the skin under the collar
Pad the collar with extra towels to make it looser

questions.stem: A parent smokes but says, "I only smoke outside." Which information should the LPN/VN share?
questions.rationale: Secondhand and thirdhand smoke exposure increases children's risk of asthma, ear infections, and SIDS. Cessation support benefits the whole family.

options.text: "That completely protects your child."
"Smoking outside helps, but smoke residue on clothes, hair, and skin (thirdhand smoke) can still affect your child. Quitting is the best protection, and we can connect you with resources."
"Smoke doesn't affect children."
"Only cigars are harmful."

questions.stem: A pregnant client plans a 6-hour car trip. Which advice should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: Pregnancy increases the risk of blood clots. Regular movement and hydration promote circulation, and correct seat belt use protects both client and fetus.

options.text: "Stay seated the whole trip."
"Stop every 1–2 hours to walk, stay hydrated, and wear your seat belt correctly."
"Skip your seat belt for comfort."
"Limit fluids so you won't need to stop."

questions.stem: A client on postpartum day 2 reports waking up drenched in sweat. Her temperature is normal. How should the LPN/VN respond?
questions.rationale: Postpartum diuresis and diaphoresis are normal as the body sheds excess fluid. A fever would suggest infection.

options.text: "You have an infection."
"Night sweats are common in the first days after birth as your body gets rid of extra fluid from pregnancy. Let us know if you develop a fever."
"Stop drinking fluids."
"This means you have thyroid disease."

questions.stem: The LPN/VN notes bluish-gray, flat patches on a newborn's lower back and buttocks. Which action is appropriate?
questions.rationale: These common birthmarks are especially frequent in infants with darker skin. Documenting them at birth prevents later confusion with bruising.

options.text: Report them as bruises from possible abuse
Document their size and location as a normal birthmark (congenital dermal melanocytosis) and explain to the parents that they usually fade
Apply ice
Scrub the area gently

questions.stem: The LPN/VN has just provided perineal care and now needs to do mouth care for the same client. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Moving from a contaminated site to a clean site with the same gloves spreads microorganisms, even on the same client.

options.text: Continue with the same gloves
Remove the gloves, perform hand hygiene, and put on clean gloves before mouth care
Rinse the gloves in the sink
Put a second pair over the first

questions.stem: A grandparent with arthritis asks the pharmacy for easy-open medication caps. Grandchildren visit often. What should the LPN/VN recommend?
questions.rationale: Grandparents' medications are a common source of child poisonings. Child-resistant caps slow access but aren't childproof, so safe storage is essential.

options.text: "Keep easy-open bottles on the kitchen counter."
"If you use easy-open caps, store all medications locked or up high, out of children's sight and reach, especially when they visit."
"Put pills in candy dishes."
"Children won't open medicine bottles."

questions.stem: What should the LPN/VN do before pouring an oral antibiotic suspension?
questions.rationale: Suspensions separate while standing, so shaking ensures a consistent dose. Many reconstituted antibiotics require refrigeration and have a limited shelf life.

options.text: Pour from the top without mixing
Shake the bottle well to evenly distribute the medication, then measure with a calibrated device
Heat the bottle
Dilute it with water to make it last longer

questions.stem: For each respiratory pattern observed in an adult, indicate whether it is normal or abnormal and should be reported.
questions.rationale: Normal adult respirations are about 12–20/min and effortless, and occasional sighs help expand the alveoli. Kussmaul suggests acidosis, Cheyne-Stokes suggests brain or heart dysfunction or approaching death, and bradypnea with opioids suggests respiratory depression.
questions.answer_summary: Normal: eupnea at 16, occasional sigh, effortless breathing at 14. Abnormal: Kussmaul, Cheyne-Stokes, bradypnea at 8 with opioids.

rows.text: Cycles of increasing then decreasing breaths with periods of apnea (Cheyne-Stokes)
Regular breathing at 8/min in a client receiving opioids

questions.stem: A 13-year-old with sickle cell disease comes to the school health office during a cold, rainy recess reporting severe pain in the legs and lower back. The student is alert, breathing comfortably, and has a temperature of 99.1°F (37.3°C). The student has an individualized health plan with prescribed pain medication. Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the student is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Cold exposure and dehydration can trigger sickling. Warmth, hydration, and analgesia are first-line. Fever of about 101°F or higher, chest pain, or breathing difficulty requires emergency care because of sepsis and acute chest syndrome risk. Cold packs cause vasoconstriction and worsen sickling.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: vaso-occlusive crisis. Actions: give prescribed pain medication, fluids, and warmth; notify parents and school RN and arrange evaluation as needed. Monitor: pain level; temperature and breathing.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Give the prescribed pain medication per the health plan, and encourage oral fluids and warmth
Notify the parents and the school RN, and arrange evaluation if pain isn't controlled or new symptoms develop
Apply cold packs to the painful areas
Have the student return to recess to walk it off
Withhold fluids until a parent arrives

bowtie_groups.label: Parameters to monitor (choose 2)
options: Temperature and breathing (for fever or chest pain suggesting acute chest syndrome)

questions.stem: A parent asks when the baby's soft spots will close. Which response by the LPN/VN is accurate?
questions.rationale: Early or delayed closure may indicate problems such as craniosynostosis or hydrocephalus. A bulging or sunken fontanel is reported.

options.text: "Both close at birth."
"The back soft spot usually closes by about 2 months, and the front one by about 12–18 months."
"They close at age 5."
"They never close."

questions.stem: A family has a newly crawling 9-month-old. Which safety measure should the LPN/VN recommend?
questions.rationale: Falls are a leading cause of injury in infants and toddlers. Hardware-mounted gates are required at the top of stairs because pressure gates can dislodge.

options.text: "Use a baby walker near the stairs."
"Install safety gates at the top and bottom of stairs. Use gates that screw into the wall at the top."
"Let the baby practice climbing stairs alone."
"Pressure-mounted gates are best at the top of stairs."

questions.stem: A parent asks how heavy a school backpack should be. Which guideline should the LPN/VN share?
questions.rationale: Heavy or improperly worn backpacks can cause back and shoulder pain and poor posture.

options.text: "As heavy as needed."
"No more than about 10–15% of the child's body weight, carried on both shoulders with the heaviest items closest to the back."
"Carry it on one shoulder."
"Half of the child's body weight."

questions.stem: A teen listens to music with earbuds for hours at high volume. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Prolonged loud sound causes permanent noise-induced hearing loss. Ringing in the ears is a warning sign.

options.text: "Turn the volume up to block outside noise."
"Follow the 60/60 rule: keep volume at no more than 60% for no more than 60 minutes at a time, and take breaks."
"Hearing loss from music always goes away."
"Only headphones, not earbuds, cause damage."

questions.stem: A healthy 77-year-old asks about the RSV vaccine. Which response reflects current CDC recommendations?
questions.rationale: RSV can cause severe illness in older adults. Current CDC guidance recommends a single dose for all adults 75 and older and for those 60–74 with increased risk. Clients should check with their provider, since recommendations may be updated.

options.text: "It's only for infants."
"A single dose is recommended for all adults 75 and older, and for adults 60–74 at increased risk."
"You need it every year."
"It's not available for adults."

questions.stem: Which type of gloves should the LPN/VN wear when drawing blood by venipuncture?
questions.rationale: Standard precautions require gloves for anticipated blood contact. Venipuncture uses clean gloves with aseptic technique.

options.text: No gloves are needed
Clean (nonsterile) gloves
Sterile gloves
Cotton gloves

questions.stem: An IV pump alarms "air in line," and the LPN/VN sees a column of air in the tubing. What should the nurse do (within scope)?
questions.rationale: Air in IV tubing can cause an air embolism. The nurse removes it safely before resuming the infusion and reports to the RN as needed.

options.text: Ignore the alarm and restart the pump
Stop the pump, clamp the tubing, and remove the air per facility procedure (such as through a port or by priming), then restart
Increase the rate to push the air through
Disconnect the tubing and leave it open to air

questions.stem: Which technique ensures accurate daily weights for a hospitalized infant?
questions.rationale: Consistent conditions detect small but important changes in fluid status and growth. The nurse keeps a hand just above the infant for safety.

options.text: Weigh the infant fully clothed at different times
Weigh the infant without clothing or diaper, on the same scale, at the same time each day
Weigh the infant on an adult bathroom scale
Estimate the weight

questions.stem: How should the LPN/VN collect a nasal swab for MRSA screening?
questions.rationale: The anterior nares are the most common site of MRSA colonization. Facility protocols for specific tests should be followed.

options.text: Swab the throat
Insert the swab about 1/2 inch into each nostril and rotate it against the inner walls, using the same swab for both nostrils unless instructed otherwise
Swab the outside of the nose only
Have the client blow their nose into a cup

questions.topic: Spacer with mask for young children
questions.stem: A 3-year-old uses an inhaler with a spacer and mask. Which technique is correct?
questions.rationale: Young children cannot coordinate an inhaler directly. A spacer with a mask lets them inhale the medication with normal breaths. One puff is given at a time.

options.text: Spray the inhaler into the air near the child
Shake the inhaler, attach it to the spacer, seal the mask over the nose and mouth, press once, and let the child breathe normally for about 6 breaths
Have the child hold their breath for 10 seconds
Press the inhaler several times at once

questions.stem: Which technique is correct when the LPN/VN palpates the carotid pulse?
questions.rationale: Pressing both carotids can reduce blood flow to the brain, and firm pressure high in the neck can stimulate the carotid sinus and cause bradycardia.

options.text: Press both carotid arteries at the same time
Palpate one side at a time, gently, in the lower half of the neck
Massage the carotid firmly to feel the pulse
Palpate high at the jaw angle with strong pressure

questions.stem: A client with a colostomy is concerned about odor. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Modern pouches are odor-proof when sealed properly. Puncturing the pouch causes leaks and odor. Parsley and yogurt may reduce odor.

options.text: "Poke a hole in the pouch to release gas."
"Use an odor-proof pouch and pouch deodorizers, empty the pouch regularly, and limit odor-causing foods such as eggs, fish, and onions."
"Eat only eggs and fish."
"Change the pouch only once a week regardless of odor."

questions.stem: A drowsy client begins to vomit. What should the LPN/VN do first?
questions.rationale: Side-lying allows vomit to drain from the mouth, which protects the airway in clients with decreased consciousness.

options.text: Leave to get an emesis basin
Turn the client onto their side to prevent aspiration, and suction the mouth if needed
Give the client water to drink
Lay the client flat on their back

questions.stem: Which action is correct when caring for a client with a suprapubic catheter?
questions.rationale: Site care and gravity drainage prevent infection and blockage. Suprapubic catheters are changed on a schedule by trained staff.

options.text: Clamp the catheter for long periods
Clean the insertion site daily with soap and water, keep the drainage bag below the bladder, and report redness, drainage, or leakage
Remove the catheter to clean it daily
Apply powder around the site

questions.stem: A client with essential tremor has difficulty eating. Which adaptive equipment should the LPN/VN suggest?
questions.rationale: Weighted utensils dampen tremor movement, and lidded cups reduce spills, supporting independence and nutrition. An occupational therapy referral can help.

options.text: Lightweight plastic utensils
Weighted utensils and cups with lids to reduce spilling
Chopsticks
Glass cups filled to the top

questions.stem: A client is going home after surgery with a closed incision. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce (per surgeon orders)?
questions.rationale: Showering is usually allowed early, but soaking can soften the incision and introduce bacteria. Harsh agents damage healing tissue. Signs of infection are reported.

options.text: "Soak in a bathtub daily."
"You may shower when your surgeon allows, often after 24–48 hours. Let water run over the incision, pat it dry, and don't scrub or apply lotions."
"Apply hydrogen peroxide several times a day."
"Cover it with plastic wrap for a week."

questions.stem: A client who works at a computer all day has neck and wrist pain. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Neutral posture and regular movement reduce musculoskeletal strain and repetitive stress injuries.

options.text: "Place the monitor below desk level."
"Position the top of the monitor at or slightly below eye level, keep wrists straight, feet flat, and take short breaks to stretch."
"Sit on the edge of the chair without back support."
"Work for hours without breaks."

questions.stem: A client says, "I've been so sad this week, and I don't know why." The LPN/VN recalls that the client's son died 2 years ago this week. How should the nurse respond?
questions.rationale: Anniversary reactions are a normal part of grief. Gently making the connection and offering support validates the client's experience.

options.text: "You should be over it by now."
"This week is the anniversary of your son's death. It's common for grief to return around these dates. Would you like to talk about him?"
"Let's change the subject."
"Try to stay busy so you don't think about it."

questions.stem: A client with schizophrenia appears to be listening to voices and is becoming distressed. Which approach by the LPN/VN is most helpful?
questions.rationale: A calm environment and a concrete, reality-based task can reduce the intensity of hallucinations. The nurse also assesses for command hallucinations and reports concerns to the RN.

options.text: Argue that the voices aren't real
Reduce stimulation, stay with the client, and engage them in a simple, reality-based activity
Ask the client to describe the voices in detail for an hour
Leave the client alone

questions.stem: A pregnant client notices dark, blotchy patches on her face. What should the LPN/VN tell her?
questions.rationale: Chloasma (melasma) is a common pigment change in pregnancy that worsens with sun exposure. Many skin-lightening agents are avoided during pregnancy.

options.text: "This is a sign of liver disease."
"This is chloasma (the 'mask of pregnancy'), caused by hormones. Sunscreen and sun protection help, and it often fades after birth."
"Use bleaching creams during pregnancy."
"It means the baby is a boy."

questions.stem: A breastfeeding mother asks whether she can have a glass of wine at a family dinner. Which response by the LPN/VN is accurate?
questions.rationale: Alcohol levels in milk follow blood levels, so waiting allows alcohol to clear. Pumping does not speed removal, and alcohol can actually reduce milk supply.

options.text: "Never drink any alcohol while breastfeeding."
"Not drinking is safest, but an occasional single drink is generally acceptable if you wait at least 2 hours before nursing."
"Pumping and dumping immediately removes all alcohol."
"Alcohol increases milk supply."

questions.stem: A parent asks why the newborn wasn't bathed right after birth. Which response by the LPN/VN reflects current practice?
questions.rationale: Delayed bathing reduces hypothermia and hypoglycemia and supports skin-to-skin contact. Sponge baths are used until the cord falls off.

options.text: "We forgot."
"Waiting to bathe, often at least 24 hours, helps keep the baby warm, supports breastfeeding and bonding, and leaves the protective vernix on the skin."
"Babies should never be bathed."
"We wait until the umbilical cord falls off before any cleaning."

questions.stem: When washing hands with soap and water, how should the LPN/VN hold the hands while rinsing?
questions.rationale: For routine handwashing, holding the fingertips down lets water carry contaminants off the hands. A surgical scrub uses the opposite position. Hands are dried with a paper towel, and a paper towel is used to turn off the faucet.

options.text: Fingertips pointing up so water runs to the elbows
Fingertips pointing down so water flows from the wrists toward the fingertips
Hands held horizontally without moving
Hands inside the sink touching the basin

questions.topic: Early vs late signs of hypoxia
questions.stem: For each finding, indicate whether it is an early or late sign of hypoxia.
questions.rationale: The body first compensates with increased heart and respiratory rates, and restlessness reflects early brain hypoxia. Cyanosis, bradycardia, and declining consciousness indicate decompensation and require emergency intervention.
questions.answer_summary: Early: restlessness, tachycardia, tachypnea. Late: cyanosis, bradycardia, decreased LOC.

questions.stem: A resident admitted 30 hours ago after a fall reported drinking a pint of vodka daily. The resident now has a hand tremor, sweating, anxiety, nausea, and HR 118/min, and says, "I feel like I'm crawling out of my skin." Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the resident is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the LPN/VN should take, and 2 parameters to monitor.
questions.rationale: Tremor, sweating, anxiety, and tachycardia 6–48 hours after the last drink indicate withdrawal, which can progress to seizures and delirium tremens. Benzodiazepines and thiamine are commonly prescribed. Giving alcohol is not appropriate treatment, and restraints increase agitation and injury.
questions.answer_summary: Condition: early alcohol withdrawal. Actions: notify the RN for a CIWA-Ar assessment and treatment; provide a quiet, well-lit room with seizure and fall precautions. Monitor: vital signs; LOC, hallucinations, and seizures.

bowtie_groups.label: Actions to take (choose 2)
options: Notify the RN promptly for a CIWA-Ar assessment and prescribed treatment
Provide a quiet, well-lit room and implement seizure and fall precautions
Offer the resident a small drink of alcohol
Apply restraints to prevent a fall
Leave the resident alone to rest

bowtie_groups.label: Parameters to monitor (choose 2)
options: Level of consciousness, hallucinations, and seizure activity

questions.stem: A parent asks how often to bathe a 3-month-old. Which response by the LPN/VN is appropriate?
questions.rationale: Frequent bathing can dry an infant's skin. Mild, fragrance-free cleansers are preferred.

options.text: "Twice a day with scented soap."
"About two or three times a week is usually enough, with daily cleaning of the face, neck folds, and diaper area."
"Once a month."
"Only when the baby smells."

questions.stem: When should parents generally help a child transition from a bottle to a cup?
questions.rationale: Prolonged bottle use increases the risk of tooth decay, ear infections, and excessive milk intake.

options.text: At 3 years
Around 12–18 months
At 4 months
When the child starts school

questions.stem: A parent asks how to teach a 7-year-old about personal safety. Which suggestion should the LPN/VN offer?
questions.rationale: Most abuse is committed by someone the child knows. Clear language and permission to tell a trusted adult help protect children.

options.text: "Don't discuss it; it will scare your child."
"Teach correct names for body parts, that no one should touch private areas, to say no and tell a trusted adult, and that some secrets should never be kept."
"Tell your child that only strangers can be dangerous."
"Teach your child to keep secrets with adults."

questions.stem: A 16-year-old wants to use tanning beds before prom. Which information should the LPN/VN share?
questions.rationale: Indoor tanning significantly increases the risk of skin cancer and premature skin aging.

options.text: "Tanning beds are safer than the sun."
"Tanning beds expose you to UV radiation that increases the risk of melanoma, especially when used before age 35. Sunless tanning products are a safer choice."
"A base tan prevents skin cancer."
"Tanning beds only affect older adults."

questions.stem: A 74-year-old reports new constipation over the past 2 months and a 12-lb unintentional weight loss. What should the LPN/VN do?
questions.rationale: New bowel changes with unexplained weight loss are red flags that require prompt evaluation.

options.text: Recommend a laxative and reassure the client
Report the findings to the RN or provider, because a change in bowel habits with weight loss needs evaluation for conditions such as colorectal cancer
Tell the client this is normal aging
Suggest skipping meals

questions.stem: Which technique is correct when using a temporal artery thermometer?
questions.rationale: Temporal artery devices measure skin temperature over the artery. Sweat, hair, and head coverings can affect accuracy, so the manufacturer's technique is followed.

options.text: Press it firmly on one spot on the cheek
Place the probe at the center of the forehead and slide it across to the hairline (or behind the ear per device instructions), keeping contact with the skin
Use it over a hat
Hold it 12 inches from the forehead

questions.stem: Which position does the LPN/VN typically use for inserting a urinary catheter in a female client?
questions.rationale: Dorsal recumbent positioning exposes the perineum. Side-lying (Sims') may be used for clients who cannot abduct the hips.

options.text: Prone
Dorsal recumbent: on the back with knees bent and feet flat, legs apart
High-Fowler's
Trendelenburg

questions.stem: A glucose meter reading seems inaccurate and doesn't match the client's symptoms. What should the LPN/VN check?
questions.rationale: Expired or heat- or humidity-exposed strips, failed quality control, and contaminated fingers cause errors. When readings don't match symptoms, the result is confirmed and reported.

options.text: Nothing; meters are always accurate
Whether the test strips are expired or improperly stored, the meter's quality control, and the client's hands were clean, then repeat the test and report per policy
The client's hearing
The time of day only

questions.stem: Which needle length is generally appropriate for an IM deltoid injection in an average-sized adult?
questions.rationale: The needle must reach the muscle. Longer needles may be needed for larger adults and shorter ones for very thin adults. CDC vaccine guidelines provide size-based recommendations.

options.text: 1/4 inch
About 1 to 1.5 inches, adjusted for body size
3 inches
1/2 inch for all adults

questions.stem: A client taking guaifenesin for a productive cough asks how to make it work best. What should the LPN/VN suggest?
questions.rationale: Hydration enhances the effect of expectorants. Suppressing a productive cough may trap secretions. A cough lasting more than a week or with fever should be evaluated.

options.text: "Limit fluids."
"Drink plenty of fluids, which help thin mucus so it's easier to cough up."
"Take it with alcohol."
"Take a cough suppressant at the same time to stop all coughing."

questions.stem: A client says, "I stop my blood pressure pills when I feel fine." Which response by the LPN/VN is most appropriate?
questions.rationale: Hypertension is often silent, and stopping some medications abruptly can cause rebound hypertension. Addressing side effects improves adherence.

options.text: "That's a good idea."
"High blood pressure usually has no symptoms, so it's important to keep taking your medication even when you feel well. Let's talk about any side effects that bother you."
"Take them only when you have a headache."
"Double the dose on days you remember."

questions.stem: A client recovering from mild viral gastroenteritis asks what to eat. Which guidance reflects current recommendations?
questions.rationale: Early return to a normal diet shortens illness and maintains nutrition. Restrictive diets alone lack protein and nutrients.

options.text: "Eat only bananas, rice, applesauce, and toast for a week."
"Resume a regular, balanced diet as tolerated while staying hydrated, and avoid very fatty or sugary foods at first."
"Don't eat for 3 days."
"Drink only soda."

questions.stem: A client with urinary incontinence is asked to keep a bladder diary. What should the LPN/VN tell the client to record?
questions.rationale: A bladder diary identifies patterns and incontinence type, such as urge or stress incontinence, and guides treatment like timed voiding.

options.text: Only the number of accidents
Times and amounts of fluid intake, times of urination and leakage, and activities or urges associated with leakage, for several days
Only bowel movements
Meals eaten

questions.stem: A client with benign paroxysmal positional vertigo has brief spinning spells when rolling over in bed. Which instruction should the LPN/VN reinforce?
questions.rationale: BPPV is caused by displaced inner-ear crystals. Repositioning maneuvers are often curative. Slow movement reduces falls.

options.text: "Move your head quickly to get used to it."
"Move slowly when changing positions, sit on the edge of the bed before standing, and ask about repositioning exercises such as the Epley maneuver."
"Drive during spells."
"Sleep flat without pillows only."

questions.stem: A client develops redness and blistering under adhesive tape. Which action should the LPN/VN take?
questions.rationale: Medical adhesive-related skin injury is preventable. Gentle removal, barrier films, and appropriate products reduce harm.

options.text: Reapply the same tape more tightly
Remove the tape gently, protect the skin with a barrier film, use a less irritating product such as paper or silicone tape, and document and report the reaction
Pull the tape off quickly
Ignore it

questions.stem: Which action is correct when caring for a client wearing a knee immobilizer?
questions.rationale: Braces can cause pressure injuries and impair circulation. Skin and neurovascular checks, as permitted by orders, prevent complications.
